items.title: Bleeding-edge compiler options (es2025, stableTypeOrdering) can break typecheck on pinned TypeScript versions
items.recommendation: Verify the typescript version resolved by the lockfile supports all options used (>= the release introducing stableTypeOrdering, and es2025 target/lib); pin the dependency with a minimum version and add a CI step that runs `bun run typecheck` with the pinned version. If older TypeScript must be supported, drop stableTypeOrdering and downgrade target/lib.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature ships with no tests (tests: []), and the vitest suite does not exercise tsc option compatibility or compiler-version constraints; option-support failures surface only when typecheck runs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step (or a small script/test) that runs `bun run typecheck` with the lockfile-pinned TypeScript and asserts exit code 0; alternatively a test that invokes the typescript API against this tsconfig and asserts no TS5023/unsupported-target diagnostics.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json (pin typescript >= required minimum) and/or tsconfig.json (remove or gate unsupported options).

items.title: No include field and broad excludes make root typecheck coverage implicit and silently partial
items.recommendation: Add an explicit include listing the source directories that must be typechecked, and either declare references to app tsconfigs or verify each app has its own typecheck script wired into the root `bun run typecheck` command so no tree is skipped silently.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this feature (tests: []), and vitest does not assert the file-list scope of the root typecheck program.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A script/test that builds the root program (e.g., via typescript API or `tsc --listFiles`) and asserts expected source dirs are covered and that each app in apps/ participates in the root typecheck (directly or via an invoked per-app config).
items.minimumFixScope: tsconfig.json: add include and references (or wire per-app typecheck into the root command).

items.title: VITE_WS_URL omitted from production secret validation loop
items.recommendation: Add VITE_WS_URL to the name list in the validation loop at line 111 so a missing/empty secret fails the deploy job before any infrastructure or Pages changes are made.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this workflow file; the inline validation loop is the only runtime guard, and it currently excludes the variable, so nothing detects the omission.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A shell test that extracts the deploy job's env block variable names (lines 70-88) and asserts every secret-sourced name appears in the validation loop's list (line 111).
items.minimumFixScope: Add `VITE_WS_URL` to the name list in .github/workflows/release.yml line 111.

items.title: Release version guard relies on a hardcoded package list that can silently drift
items.recommendation: Derive the package list from the workspace (e.g., enumerate package.json files under apps/ and packages/, or use `bun pm ls`/workspace metadata), or add a CI check that fails when a package.json exists that is not covered by the hardcoded list.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The check runs inline in the workflow and no tests are included for this feature; the drift only manifests at the moment a new package is added, with no test or automation forcing list updates.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that enumerates all package.json files under apps/ and packages/ and asserts each one appears in the version guard's file list.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace the hardcoded array in the inline Node script (lines 49-54) with a workspace-derived list, or add a drift-checking job/step.

items.title: Production web app (Pages) deployment is not smoke-tested
items.recommendation: After web:deploy:production, add a smoke check that curls the production web origin (e.g., the Pages URL or SIWE_URI) with --fail and asserts a 200 response with expected content, or verify the Pages deployment status via the Cloudflare API before the github-release job runs.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The workflow has a smoke-test step but it is limited to API endpoints; no test file is included for this feature.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A workflow step that runs `curl --fail --max-time 30 "$WEB_ORIGIN"` (with the origin derived from the deployed Pages URL or SIWE_URI) and asserts an expected HTTP status/marker after the web deploy step.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend the smoke-test step (lines 123-126) to include the web origin, or add a step between the web deploy and github-release jobs.

items.title: passWithNoTests: true can silently mask zero executed tests in CI
items.recommendation: Remove passWithNoTests from the shared config, or scope it to local development only (e.g., set it conditionally via an environment variable such as NODE_ENV !== 'production' or via a separate dev-only config override). Additionally, consider a CI assertion that the run executed at least one test (e.g., parse vitest's JSON reporter output and fail if numTotalTests === 0).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: vitest.config.ts is the test runner's own configuration; the repository has no test that executes the config and asserts how many tests the suite actually runs, so nothing guards against a silent zero-test pass.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A script or CI step that runs `vitest run --reporter=json` and fails if the reported total test count is 0, ensuring the projects entry always resolves to runnable tests.
items.minimumFixScope: Remove or conditionally disable the passWithNoTests option in vitest.config.ts.

items.title: Root dev/build scripts use --filter '*' and fail if any workspace lacks the script
items.recommendation: Ensure every workspace declares `dev` and `build` (even as no-ops), or drop the all-workspace filter and drive each app via the dedicated api:dev/web:dev scripts; add a CI check that lists workspaces and verifies script symmetry.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature; the failure happens when running the root scripts, before any vitest suite executes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A config-validation test that enumerates workspaces and asserts each one declares the scripts referenced by root `--filter '*'` commands.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json scripts (lines 8-9) plus workspace package.json updates

items.title: packageManager pins floating bun@canary dist-tag, making installs non-reproducible
items.recommendation: Pin a concrete package manager version, e.g. `"packageManager": "bun@1.4.0"` (or a specific canary build hash if a pre-release is truly required), and enforce it in CI by verifying `bun --version` matches before `bun install`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature; package.json toolchain pinning is not exercised by the vitest suite.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A config-validation test or CI step that reads package.json and asserts the packageManager value is an exact version (no 'canary', 'latest', or range tag).

items.title: typescript@^7.0.2 may not exist on npm or may change tsc CLI behavior
items.recommendation: Confirm `typescript@7.0.2` resolves on the registry and that `bun run typecheck` passes across all workspaces; otherwise pin a released major (e.g. 6.x/5.x) known to work with the workspace tsconfigs.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature; an install-time failure would prevent the test suite from running at all.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI smoke step running `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `bun run typecheck` to catch unresolvable or incompatible toolchain versions.

items.title: test:coverage script references a coverage provider not declared in devDependencies
items.recommendation: Add `@vitest/coverage-v8` (matching the vitest 4 major) to the root devDependencies.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and the failure occurs at script-invocation time, outside the coverage suite itself (the coverage run never starts).
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A config-validation test asserting that when a `test:coverage` script exists, a matching `@vitest/coverage-*` provider is present in devDependencies.

items.title: Hand-rolled forge coverage summary parser can silently mis-gate if the summary column layout changes
items.recommendation: Validate column semantics instead of position (e.g., match the header row '| File | % Lines | % Statements | % Branches | % Funcs |' before parsing and index by header), or compute the gate from the lcov.info report (already generated on line 204) rather than the human summary; add a unit test for the parser fed with captured forge output.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The parser is embedded in a YAML run block and is not covered by the repository's vitest/forge test suites; only real Foundry output would exercise it.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A small script/test that feeds a sample summary including the header row and a 'Total' row into the parsing logic and asserts the extracted lines/statements/functions values match expectations.
items.minimumFixScope: Harden the coverage step's parser (header validation or lcov-based computation) in .github/workflows/ci.yml.

items.title: Unpinned/never-verified third-party tooling installs (slither-analyzer, solc-select, echidna binary)
items.recommendation: Pin exact versions for pip installs (e.g., `pip3 install slither-analyzer==0.10.4 solc-select==1.0.4` or a requirements file with hashes) and pin/verify a SHA-256 digest of the echidna tarball before extraction (download, `sha256sum`, compare against a committed digest, then extract). Consider caching the installed tools so they are not re-downloaded every run.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Workflow install steps execute directly on runners; the repository's test suites (vitest/forge/playwright) do not exercise CI provisioning, so nothing validates version reproducibility or integrity.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A small smoke step or script that asserts the resolved tool versions match the pins (e.g., `slither --version`, `solc-select versions`) and that the echidna tarball digest matches a committed value.
items.minimumFixScope: Add version pins/hashes to the pip and curl install steps in .github/workflows/ci.yml.

items.title: No job-level timeouts: hung or unbounded steps can block the required ci-status gate for up to 6 hours
items.recommendation: Set timeout-minutes per job (e.g., 15-30 min for quality/backend/frontend, 45-60 min for contracts and e2e, 90-120 min for echidna) and enforce fuzzing limits via the echidna.yaml config (testLimit/timeout) as well.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Job timing is static workflow YAML and is not exercised by any test suite; there is no CI-level check that jobs declare timeouts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A lint-style check (e.g., a small script) that parses the workflow and fails if any job lacks timeout-minutes.
items.minimumFixScope: Add timeout-minutes to each job in .github/workflows/ci.yml.

items.title: Workflow shell logic (secret validation, retry loop, smoke-test URL derivation) has no automated coverage and is not linted
items.recommendation: Add actionlint (or a YAML+shell lint step) to CI for `.github/workflows/*`, and add a unit test for the health-URL derivation covering: exact `/api/v1` suffix, trailing slash, and non-`/api/v1` base URLs. Prefer deriving the health URL from an explicit base secret or a dedicated `HEALTH_URL` rather than suffix manipulation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The project's test command targets the TypeScript codebase; GitHub Actions YAML and inline shell blocks are outside its coverage, and no workflow-level test harness exists.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A shell test that runs the derivation expression against sample VITE_API_URL values (with and without trailing slash, with and without `/api/v1`) and asserts the expected health URL, plus an actionlint step in CI.
items.minimumFixScope: .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml — make the health URL derivation explicit/robust; optionally add actionlint to the repo's CI.

items.title: VITE_WS_URL is sourced from secrets but omitted from the Validate deployment inputs check, so a missing/empty websocket secret deploys a broken canary silently
items.recommendation: Add VITE_WS_URL to the name list in the Validate deployment inputs loop (line 61), or explicitly document it as optional and add a smoke-test assertion for it if the app can run without websockets.
items.reproduction: Delete or empty the VITE_WS_URL secret, push to main; the deploy job passes all validation and smoke tests while the deployed frontend receives an empty websocket URL.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this workflow (tests: []), and the omission is invisible to CI since the validation step only fails on variables that are listed.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A small script that parses the workflow YAML and asserts every env var whose value is `${{ secrets.* }}` appears in the Validate deployment inputs loop's name list; wire it into CI so future secret additions cannot be missed.
items.minimumFixScope: .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml — add `VITE_WS_URL` to the for-loop list at line 61.

items.title: Deploy checks out mutable `main` and verifies it against a CI-run SHA, creating a TOCTOU race that aborts deploys when main advances
items.recommendation: Check out the tested commit directly: set `ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}` on actions/checkout (keeping the Verify tested commit step as a guard, or replacing it since checkout is then exact). This removes the race window entirely while preserving the 'deploy exactly what CI tested' guarantee.
items.reproduction: Push commit A (CI completes, deploy job starts); push commit B before the deploy job's checkout step runs; `git rev-parse HEAD` returns B's SHA while TESTED_SHA is A's, so the Verify tested commit step exits non-zero and the deploy is skipped.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no tests (tests: []), and GitHub workflow_run timing races cannot be exercised by the repo's existing unit/integration suites; the behavior is only observable in production scheduling.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A workflow-level test (e.g., actionlint plus a small script) that parses the YAML and asserts the checkout `ref` is the pinned `head_sha` expression rather than a branch name, so a future change cannot silently reintroduce the moving-target checkout.
items.minimumFixScope: .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml — change the checkout step's `ref` to `${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}`.

items.title: Scheduled CodeQL runs share the concurrency group with push runs and can be cancelled mid-analysis
items.recommendation: Include the event type in the concurrency group key so schedule and push runs do not cancel each other, e.g. `group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}`, or set `cancel-in-progress: false` (or drop the concurrency block) for the schedule trigger.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no tests (tests: []), and GitHub Actions concurrency semantics cannot be exercised by the project's bun-based test/lint commands; this behavior is only observable in live workflow runs.

items.title: No CI validation covers the CodeQL workflow YAML or its referenced config file
items.recommendation: Add an actionlint (or at minimum a YAML syntax) check to the lint/test pipeline for .github/workflows and verify that the referenced ./.github/codeql-config.yml exists and is valid, so workflow breakage is caught in PR CI rather than only in live GitHub Actions runs.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are associated with this feature (tests: []), and none of the detected project commands target GitHub Actions workflow files.
items.minimumFixScope: Add a workflow-YAML lint step (e.g., actionlint) to CI and a check that ./.github/codeql-config.yml exists

items.title: No CI validation of workflow YAML/expressions; breakage surfaces only at the weekly scheduled run
items.recommendation: Add an actionlint check for .github/workflows/*.yml to CI (or extend the lint command), and configure a notification (status badge, scheduled-failure issue, or workflow dispatch fallback) so a missing weekly run is surfaced promptly.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing typecheck/lint/format/test commands are JavaScript-oriented and do not parse GitHub Actions YAML, and the workflow itself has no self-validation step.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: CI step running actionlint on .github/workflows/renovate.yml for PRs touching .github/

items.title: renovate-version container pin can silently drift from the action SHA pin
items.recommendation: Add a packageRule in renovate.json matching renovatebot/github-action with the renovateVersion option so renovate-version tracks the action version in lockstep (verify the rule exists before assuming drift is handled); otherwise document a manual bump procedure for both pins.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover synchronization between the action SHA and the renovate-version input; drift is only observable at the next scheduled run.
items.minimumFixScope: renovate.json (add renovateVersion packageRule) - outside included files, so verify current contents first

items.title: Long-lived write-scoped PAT available to scheduled job that rewrites workflow files
items.recommendation: Rotate RENOVATE_TOKEN regularly and scope it to the minimum (Contents and Pull requests write); consider dropping the Workflows write scope by disabling or narrowly constraining the github-actions manager, or use a GitHub App installation token with expiring, per-repo credentials; keep postUpgradeTasks disabled in renovate.json; treat any Renovate PR touching .github/ as high-risk and review diffs carefully.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this workflow's secret handling; this is a configuration-level security posture issue that CI tests cannot exercise without the real PAT.
items.minimumFixScope: .github/workflows/renovate.yml (and renovate.json if the github-actions manager scope is reduced)

items.title: V4 position reconcile maps ownership mismatch to 502 'Unable to read v4 position state'
items.recommendation: Use a dedicated error (or a tag on V4PositionReadError) for ownership mismatch and return 403 with the same message as the V3 path; reserve 502 for actual RPC/read failures.
items.reproduction: POST /api/v1/positions/v4/:tokenId/reconcile for a tokenId owned by another wallet returns 502 instead of 403.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No positions route tests exist in the included scope.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that reconciling a tokenId owned by a different wallet returns 403, while an RPC failure returns 502.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/positions.ts V4 reconcile handler and its error mapping.

items.title: POST /api/v1/positions records positions with no format validation (poolId, tokenId, ticks, liquidity, protocol)
items.recommendation: Add runtime validation matching sibling routes: poolId against the 64-hex poolKey pattern (or address pattern), integer ticks, liquidity as a non-negative integer string, tokenId as digits when provided, protocol within {v3,v4}; return 400 on failure.
items.reproduction: POST /api/v1/positions with body {poolId:'garbage', tickLower:1.5, tickUpper:2.5, liquidity:'abc', protocol:'v5'} returns 200 and persists the row.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No positions route tests exist in the included scope; the sole test covers only the price-guard helper.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Route test asserting malformed poolId/tick/liquidity/protocol bodies return 400 and are never passed to PositionService.

items.title: Route handlers have no test coverage — only the price-guard pure helper is tested
items.recommendation: Add route-level tests with mocked D1/RPC (the repo already depends on @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers and @effect/vitest) covering auth failures, TP/SL creation verification, reconcile ownership checks, and param validation for each route.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test deliberately targets only the exported pure function and cannot exercise handlers, middleware, or on-chain verification.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A route-level suite parameterizing each endpoint with valid/invalid inputs, asserting status codes and that services are never called on validation failures.

items.title: GET /api/v1/quote accepts unvalidated slippage (NaN/negative/unbounded) that can null out minAmountOut
items.recommendation: Validate slippage with Number.isFinite and a bounded range (e.g. 0 to 100 percent) before building the quote, returning 400 on invalid input, mirroring the v3-quote.ts validation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only included test covers the price-guard helper; there are no swap route tests exercising query-parameter validation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Route-level test asserting GET /quote with slippage=abc, slippage=-1, and slippage=999 each return 400 and never reach the quote service.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/swap.ts GET /quote handler — add slippage validation before getQuote.

items.title: Missing/invalid CHAIN_ID silently defaults to Sepolia in TP/SL routes and yields NaN chainId in POST /positions
items.recommendation: Use parseChainId in both files and return 500 'Invalid chain configuration' on null (or a non-safe-integer value), matching pools.ts/price-guard.ts; never fall back to a hardcoded chain.
items.reproduction: Deploy with CHAIN_ID unset: POST /api/v1/tp-sl/orders succeeds and persists the order with chainId 11155111.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No TP/SL or positions tests exist; the misconfiguration path is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that TP/SL and positions handlers return 500 when CHAIN_ID is missing or non-numeric, and never write a fallback chainId.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/tp-sl.ts chainIdFor and apps/api/src/routes/positions.ts POST /positions chainId computation.

items.title: POST /api/v1/swap/record accepts unverified tx hashes and amounts from any authenticated user
items.recommendation: Before inserting, fetch the transaction receipt on-chain and verify status success and that the sender matches session.userAddress (mirroring tp-sl.ts creation verification); at minimum validate txHash format and add a unique constraint on (chainId, txHash).
items.reproduction: Authenticated user POSTs /api/v1/swap/record with a random hex txHash, blockNumber 1, and amountUsd 1e9; the row is persisted without any on-chain check.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No swap route tests exist; the included test only exercises the price-guard helper.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Route test with mocked RPC: recording a txHash with no receipt (or a receipt whose sender is not the session user) must be rejected with 4xx and no row inserted.

items.title: TP/SL order id parsing via Number.parseInt accepts malformed ids and loses precision for large uint256 order ids
items.recommendation: Validate the param with /^[0-9]+$/ and keep the id as a decimal string (or BigInt) end-to-end instead of converting through Number.
items.reproduction: DELETE /api/v1/tp-sl/orders/12abc deletes order 12 instead of rejecting; an order with id 9007199254740993 resolves to 9007199254740992.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No TP/SL route tests exist; only the price-guard helper is tested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that /orders/12abc returns 400 and that an id > 2^53 round-trips through getOrder/cancelOrder without precision loss.

items.title: GET /api/v1/pools accepts unvalidated sortBy/sortDirection/filterToken query params
items.recommendation: Validate sortBy against ['tvl','volume','fees','created'], sortDirection against ['asc','desc'], and filterToken against /^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/ when provided; return 400 on violation.
items.reproduction: GET /api/v1/pools?sortBy=INJECTED returns 500 or unspecified ordering instead of 400.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No pools route tests exist in the included scope.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Route test asserting invalid sortBy/sortDirection/filterToken values return 400 and valid values pass through to the service.

items.title: No tests for the WorkerEnv tag and layer factory
items.recommendation: Add a small unit test (e.g., apps/api/src/layers/WorkerEnv.test.ts) using @effect/vitest that builds the layer and asserts the provided env is retrievable via Effect.service(WorkerEnv), and that the tag id is '@aetherdex/WorkerEnv'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files are associated with this feature; the feature metadata lists an empty tests array and none of the included files reference a test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: `const env = { DB: {} as D1Database, ... }; const result = await Effect.runPromise(Effect.provide(makeWorkerEnvLayer(env), Effect.service(WorkerEnv))); expect(result).toEqual(env)` plus an assertion on the tag's service id.

items.title: WorkerEnv tag uses Context.Service, an API removed in Effect 3/4; pinned effect 4.0.0-beta.100 expects Context.Tag
items.recommendation: Replace line 13 with `export const WorkerEnv = Context.Tag<WorkerEnv>("@aetherdex/WorkerEnv")` and keep the exported WorkerEnv interface; Layer.succeed on line 15 is then correct as-is.
items.reproduction: Run `bun run typecheck` in apps/api against the pinned effect version; expect TS2339 (Property 'Service' does not exist) on line 13, and a TypeError at import time under vitest or wrangler dev if the export is also missing at runtime.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this file (feature tests array is empty), and vitest's esbuild transform strips types without typechecking, so even a passing runtime test would not flag a missing/renamed Effect export; the typecheck script is the only gate and it is currently at risk.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest case that imports WorkerEnv.ts (import fails if Context.Service is undefined at runtime) and asserts WorkerEnv.serviceId (or the tag's id) equals '@aetherdex/WorkerEnv' and that Effect.provide(makeWorkerEnvLayer(env), Effect.service(WorkerEnv)) yields the same env instance.

items.title: Portfolio fetch race: aborted request's finally clears the pending state and stale cross-account positions remain visible
items.recommendation: Mirror positions.tsx: add an `active`/`cancelled` flag, guard setPositions/setIsPending in then/catch/finally with it, and clear positions when starting a new request.
items.reproduction: Start a slow /users/:address/positions request, switch wallet accounts before it resolves; the spinner disappears and the previous account's positions render until the second request completes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The portfolio tests cover only pure helpers (getPortfolioStatus, formatPositionValue) and static render states; the fetch effect with abort semantics is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Component test that starts a fetch, unmounts/refetches with a pending promise, resolves the first request after abort, and asserts isPending stays true and positions are not clobbered.

items.title: Post-swap /record request is fire-and-forget: index sync failures are silent and the swap is reported as fully successful
items.recommendation: Surface record failures (retry with backoff, or show a non-blocking 'index sync pending' notice with a manual retry), and/or have the indexer reconcile from chain events as a backstop.
items.reproduction: Block the /record endpoint (or expire the auth token) and complete a swap; the page shows 'Swap Confirmed' and resets after 3 seconds, and the swap is absent from the index.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exercise the post-confirmation record flow; swap.spec.ts covers only initial page rendering.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test the confirmation effect: assert /record is called with the quote payload, and that a failed response triggers a visible retry path rather than silent swallow.

items.title: formatAmount decimal 'trim' is a no-op: slice never truncates and the 'at least 2 decimals' guarantee is not implemented
items.recommendation: Decide on the intended policy and implement it explicitly, e.g. cap fraction at 6 digits with trailing-zero trim: fracPart.replace(/0+$/, '').slice(0, 6) || '0', and pad to 2 when shorter if 'at least 2 decimals' is truly desired.
items.reproduction: Quote an amount whose formatted output has many fractional digits (e.g., 18-decimal token amounts) and observe the full un-capped fraction rendered in the 'You receive' area.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: formatAmount is module-private and the included tests never call it; swap coverage is limited to e2e rendering assertions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test formatAmount for cases like '1500000000000000000'/18 (expect '1.5'), a tiny amount, and a zero-decimal token.

items.title: Pools filter input desynchronizes from the URL filterToken on navigation
items.recommendation: Derive the input value from Route.useSearch().filterToken (and update on navigation), or add an effect syncing search state when the URL value changes.
items.reproduction: Type a token into the filter, click the header 'Pools' link (resets filterToken to ''); the list is unfiltered but the input still shows the old token.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: pools.test.tsx tests only the PoolsResults presentational component with static props; no test mounts PoolsIndexPage with router search state.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Router-level test: navigate to /pools?filterToken=X, then to /pools, and assert the input clears to match the URL.

items.title: Stale swap quote expiry (expiresAt) is never enforced before building/signing the transaction
items.recommendation: Before calling /build (and ideally again before sendTransaction), verify quote.expiresAt * 1000 > Date.now() and abort with a 'Quote expired — refresh' error; alternatively re-fetch the quote when it is within a short window of expiry.
items.reproduction: Fetch a quote, wait longer than expiresAt, click Swap; the flow proceeds to wallet signing without any expiry warning or re-quote.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only swap tests are e2e rendering smoke tests (apps/web/test/e2e/swap.spec.ts lines 8-34) that never exercise the signing flow or quote lifecycle.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test handleSwap (or an extracted helper) with an expired quote and assert it rejects without calling /build or sendTransaction.

items.title: Pool detail page masks network/server failures as 'Pool not found' with no retry
items.recommendation: Check response.ok, distinguish HTTP/network errors from a 404 (missing pool), surface an error state with a retry button, and only render 'Pool not found.' for genuine 404s.
items.reproduction: Stop the API server and open /pools/<valid-pool-id>; the page shows 'Pool not found.' instead of an availability error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for PoolDetailPage or its data fetching; pools.test.tsx only covers the PoolsResults list component.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render test that stubs a failed/500 fetch and asserts an error state with retry is shown rather than 'Pool not found.'

items.title: Exported money-moving validation logic (pool creation, rebalance position selection) has no unit tests
items.recommendation: Add unit tests for validatePoolCreationForm (distinct/ordered tokens, fee/tickSpacing caps, sqrtPriceX96 range, price too small to encode, past/equal deadline), buildPoolCreationTransactionIntent encoding, and selectIndexedPosition fallback semantics.
items.reproduction: Run bun --cwd apps/web run test; no test imports pools.new.tsx or positions.tsx helpers.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Coverage exists only for PoolsResults, PortfolioResults, playground lib/table, and swap rendering; the exported validators were evidently written for testability but never tested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Table-driven vitest suite over validatePoolCreationForm covering each error branch and a valid case producing a request.

items.title: listTokens accepts negative or NaN limits: unbounded result set or 500
items.recommendation: Clamp exactly like applyOptions in token-list.service.ts: const rawLimit = options?.limit; const limit = Math.min(rawLimit === undefined || !Number.isFinite(rawLimit) || rawLimit < 0 ? 100 : rawLimit, 500).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included in this feature, and observing the SQL LIMIT behavior requires a D1/SQLite-backed test that asserts row counts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: listTokens({limit: -1}) and listTokens({limit: NaN}) must each return at most 500 rows (or the default limit), not the full table / an error.

items.title: No tests exist for either token service
items.recommendation: Add unit tests with injected SqlClient/fetcher mocks covering: limit edge cases (-1, NaN, 0, >500), upsert failure propagation, case-insensitive address lookup, chain scoping, and the full cache-fallback chain (KV hit, KV miss + fetch success, fetch failure + D1 fallback, all-miss).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist in this feature (tests: []), so there is nothing to contradict or cover the behaviors described.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest suite using @effect/vitest with mocked SqlClient and TokenListFetcher exercising each resolveTokens branch and the listTokens/getToken edge cases above.
items.minimumFixScope: New test files under apps/api/test/ for both services

items.title: D1 fallback serves arbitrary verified rows and truncates the canonical list at 500
items.recommendation: Add a source/canonical marker column (e.g., source = 'token-list') set by writeThroughD1 and filter on it in readD1Cache, and remove or raise the arbitrary 500 cap for getToken lookups (e.g., lookup by address directly from D1 instead of materializing a capped list).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included, and this path only activates when KV misses and the upstream fetch fails, so it is easy to miss in integration testing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Seed D1 with 500+ verified rows (including a canonical row beyond the 500th by symbol order), simulate a fetch failure with empty KV, and assert getToken still finds the canonical token.

items.title: upsertToken silently swallows every write failure and reports success
items.recommendation: Do not swallow the error: expose an error channel (e.g., Effect<void, TokenWriteError>) or at minimum log the failure via Effect.logError and propagate, so HTTP callers can return 500/503. Also add is_native = excluded.is_native to the conflict update for consistency with the other columns.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no tests (tests: []), and the never error channel leaves tests nothing to assert on without injecting a failing SqlClient.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Inject a SqlClient stub whose query rejects and assert upsertToken fails (or logs) instead of resolving undefined.

items.title: getToken matches addresses case-sensitively; inconsistent with token-list service
items.recommendation: Normalize addresses on write (store lowercase) or compare case-insensitively: WHERE LOWER(address) = LOWER(${address}) AND chain_id = ${deps.chainId}; if normalizing, add a unique index on LOWER(address) to keep (chain_id, address) deduplication meaningful.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included; this requires a seeded row with checksummed casing plus a lowercase query to expose.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Insert a token with a checksummed address, call getToken with the lowercased address, and assert the token is returned.

items.title: Three of four Durable Objects (order book, websocket hub, volume alert hub) have zero test coverage; the only generic test is a placeholder
items.recommendation: Add vitest-pool-workers tests covering: WebSocket upgrade + receive of update frames, per-pool/per-token filtering, subscribe/unsubscribe persistence via attachments, and wake-after-hibernation broadcast for all three DOs (the harness already exists, per @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers in package.json and siwe-nonce-do.test.ts). Replace the placeholder index.test.ts with meaningful assertions or remove it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is the finding itself: no such tests exist.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Per-DO test suites: connect N sockets with mixed filters, POST updates, assert only matching sockets receive frames; then simulate hibernation and repeat.

items.title: WebSocket error handlers send internal exception details to untrusted clients
items.recommendation: Send a fixed generic message (e.g. { type: 'error', message: 'Invalid message' }) to the client and console.error the full error server-side; narrow the catch to JSON.parse only.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exercise malformed-message handling on either DO.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Send a malformed frame (e.g. invalid JSON or a frame that throws in the handler) and assert the client receives a sanitized error without embedded exception text.

items.title: SiweNonceDO issue() is not atomic with consume(): a concurrent issue can have its fresh record deleted by an in-flight consume
items.recommendation: Wrap the issue() body (or at least the put/deleteAlarm/setAlarm sequence) in this.ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile so issue and consume serialize on the same lock, or run consume's block inside blockConcurrencyWhile that also covers setAlarm ordering.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: siwe-nonce-do.test.ts tests concurrent consume-only traffic (lines 5-23) and expiry paths, but no test interleaves issue() with consume().
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Fire issue() and consume() concurrently against the same named instance many times and assert every 201-issued nonce is consumable exactly once.

items.title: WebSocketHubDO knownTokens set does not survive hibernation, breaking list_pools and /stats after idle
items.recommendation: Persist knownTokens in ctx.storage (e.g. a storage set updated in the /price handler) and load it in hydrateSubscribers()/fetch, or reconstruct the token set by unioning watchedKeys from all socket attachments plus a persisted set for tokens without active subscribers.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for WebSocketHubDO; the included test files cover only nonce semantics (siwe-nonce-do.test.ts) and placeholder assertions (index.test.ts).
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that after issuing /price broadcasts, simulating instance eviction/wake, a list_pools request still returns the previously known token addresses.

items.title: OrderBookDO loses its subscriber map on hibernation; orderbook updates are silently dropped after wake
items.recommendation: Drop the in-memory map and enumerate ctx.getWebSockets() at broadcast time (as VolumeAlertHubDO does), carrying the pool filter in the socket attachment via serializeAttachment, and/or add a hydrateSubscribers() step (mirroring websocket-hub-do.ts lines 167-177) invoked at the start of fetch() and webSocketMessage(). Compute subscriber counts from getWebSockets().length for accurate stats.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test exists for OrderBookDO; the only DO tests (apps/api/test/siwe-nonce-do.test.ts) cover the nonce DO, and apps/api/test/index.test.ts is a placeholder asserting string concat and 2+2.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest-pool-workers test that accepts a WebSocket, hibernates/evicts the instance (or simulates wake on a fresh instance), POSTs /update, and asserts the still-connected socket receives the orderbook_update frame.

items.title: useWebSocket reconnect, message parsing, and url-change paths have no test coverage
items.recommendation: Add tests that fire onclose/onmessage/onerror events on MockWebSocket instances (e.g., a static helper to emit events), covering reconnect scheduling with fake timers, attempt cap, backoff values, JSON and non-JSON messages, and url-change remounts.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests assert only the happy-path open and cleanup behavior; the mock's close() never triggers onclose, so reconnect logic has zero coverage.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Emit onclose on the mock instance and assert a new WebSocket instance is created after reconnectInterval with reconnectCount incremented, and that after reconnectAttempts closes no further instances are created.

items.title: SIWE auth token persisted in localStorage, readable by any script and never expired client-side
items.recommendation: Prefer an httpOnly SameSite cookie set by the /auth/verify endpoint; otherwise store the token in sessionStorage with an expiry timestamp and validate it on read, and ensure the server enforces short-lived tokens with refresh/revocation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file exists for useSiweAuth in the included set, and storage behavior is not asserted anywhere.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock localStorage and assert the token is not readable from localStorage when cookie mode is enabled (or that an expired stored token is treated as unauthenticated).

items.title: Stale WebSocket close event can trigger reconnect with the old URL and orphan the live socket after effect re-run
items.recommendation: Capture the socket instance in the onclose/onopen/onmessage handlers and bail out when wsRef.current !== ws; additionally use a monotonically increasing connection generation/epoch (or the effect run itself) to ignore events and reconnect timers from superseded connections, and clear reconnectTimerRef when the timer fires.
items.reproduction: Mount a component using useWebSocket with StrictMode (or change the url prop while connected); the first socket's close event fires after the remount, scheduling a reconnect to the old URL and creating a second connection that replaces wsRef.current, leaving the first new socket open and unreferenced.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: MockWebSocket.close is a vi.fn() that never dispatches an onclose event (test lines 12-19), and no test re-renders the hook with a different url while a socket is open, so the stale-close/reconnect path is never exercised; the unmount test only asserts close() was called.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render the hook, wait for open, re-render with a new url, then simulate the old instance's onclose firing afterwards; assert no additional WebSocket instance is created, wsRef still targets the new url socket, and reconnectCount is not incremented.

items.title: API_URL silently falls back to http://localhost:8080 and is baked into production builds
items.recommendation: Make the API base URL a required build-time variable (fail the build when missing in production mode) or default to a same-origin relative path, and add a CI check that the deployed bundle does not contain localhost.
items.reproduction: Run `VITE_API_URL= bun run build` (or no env var) and deploy; the built JS contains http://localhost:8080 and all SIWE requests fail in production.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No build-time or e2e test asserts the API endpoint used in production bundles.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A build script test that runs `vite build` without VITE_API_URL and asserts the output contains no localhost URL.

items.title: Alert rules config has no tests validating threshold/severity/message invariants
items.recommendation: Add a small vitest unit test that iterates over ALERT_RULES and asserts: each rule has non-empty metric and message strings, threshold > 0, windowMinutes > 0, severity is one of "warn" | "critical", and optionally that message/percentage pairs are mutually consistent (0.01 ↔ "1%"). Also assert all rules share the same field set or that field differences (filter, ratio) are intentional.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files exist for this module; package.json's test setup (vitest run with @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers) has no test targeting monitoring config.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest test that imports ALERT_RULES and, for each rule key, asserts typeof rule.threshold === "number" && rule.threshold > 0, rule.windowMinutes > 0, rule.severity is "warn" | "critical", and rule.message.trim().length > 0.
items.minimumFixScope: Add apps/api/test/monitoring/alerts.test.ts (or equivalent) without changing alerts.ts.

items.title: AlertSeverity type is hand-maintained and can drift from severities actually used in ALERT_RULES
items.recommendation: Define a shared AlertRuleConfig interface (metric, threshold, windowMinutes, severity, message, plus optional filter/ratio) and annotate the map with it, e.g. `const ALERT_RULES = {...} satisfies Record<string, AlertRuleConfig>`. Derive the severity type from the config instead of hand-writing it, e.g. `type AlertSeverity = (typeof ALERT_RULES)[keyof typeof ALERT_RULES]["severity"]`, so any new severity value is either accepted everywhere or rejected at compile time.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no tests (tests: []), and this is a type-level contract issue that no runtime test currently exercises; the file is only covered by tsc --noEmit, which cannot detect drift between the hand-written AlertSeverity union and rule severities because both are inferred independently.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A type-level test asserting `type Severities = (typeof ALERT_RULES)[keyof typeof ALERT_RULES]["severity"]` is assignable to AlertSeverity and that every rule satisfies a common AlertRuleConfig shape (e.g., using a `satisfies` check or an expect-type assertion that each rule has metric, threshold, windowMinutes, severity, and message).

items.title: Type-unsafe casts mask a @wagmi/core v2/v3 adapter mismatch, defeating typecheck coverage
items.recommendation: Prefer depending on an @reown/appkit-adapter-wagmi version built against @wagmi/core v3 (or pin @wagmi/core to the adapter's expected major) so the casts can be removed; if the casts must stay, isolate them in one typed wrapper module with a comment and a smoke test that constructs the adapter and config.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this feature, and unit tests using happy-dom would not exercise the adapter's real runtime integration with wagmi v3; the mismatch is only detectable in a browser E2E test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A Playwright smoke test that mounts AppKitProvider and asserts the WagmiProvider renders and `config` exposes the expected chain/account state, catching a v2/v3 runtime contract break.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/src/wagmi.tsx (align dependency majors or centralize the casts)

items.title: Missing VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID fails at runtime with a blank page instead of failing the build
items.recommendation: Validate the variable at build time (e.g., in vite.config.ts or a prebuild script that fails CI) and/or replace the module-scope throw with a rendered fallback screen (error boundary or a small component) so the failure is visible and diagnosable instead of a blank page.
items.reproduction: Run `vite build` without VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID set: the build succeeds. Serve the output: the page is blank and the console shows 'VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID is required...'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature links no tests (tests: []), so the module-load throw path is never exercised; a unit test importing wagmi.tsx without the env var would crash the test runner, which is why the behavior has gone unnoticed.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that imports a non-throwing variant (or a build-time config check) asserting that a missing VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID produces a clear, controlled failure message rather than an uncaught module-scope exception.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/src/wagmi.tsx (move the guard into an initializer with a graceful failure path) plus optional build-time validation in the Vite config.

items.title: No tests cover app bootstrap, env validation, or wallet-provider wiring
items.recommendation: Add a render test asserting AppKitProvider/QueryClientProvider/RouterProvider mount without crashing (with VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID stubbed), and a config test asserting the queryClient defaults (staleTime 60000, refetchOnWindowFocus false) and the env-var guard behavior.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no tests, and the module-scope throw in wagmi.tsx actively discourages importing it in test setups without env setup, so the entry path is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest + testing-library test that stubs import.meta.env.VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID, renders <AppKitProvider>, and asserts the provider tree mounts and exposes a wagmi config.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/src (add test files; no production code change required)

items.title: Non-atomic KV read-modify-write on counters lets concurrent requests exceed the configured rate limit and delays circuit-breaker trips
items.recommendation: Serialize per-key counter updates, e.g., a Durable Object per caller/breaker used as an atomic counter, or a single DO sharded by key; alternatively detect and merge concurrent writes via the metadata timestamp. At minimum document that limits are approximate under concurrency.
items.reproduction: Set RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2 and fire 3 concurrent POSTs from the same caller bucket; observe 3x 200 (expected at most 2x 200).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: rate-limit.test.ts posts sequentially and awaits each response (lines 38-55, 58-66), so the get/put interleaving never occurs; the KV-error test (lines 113-122) covers fail-open on errors only, not the lost-update path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: With RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2, Promise.all 3 posts against the same IP bucket and assert no more than 2 succeed.

items.title: MEV_PROTECTION_MODE=private with any non-empty PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL claims private routing that the middleware cannot provide
items.recommendation: Gate private mode on an actual relayer capability (e.g., a signing key binding or a health-checked relay client); degrade to client with a warning unless the relayer is confirmed available, and only emit the private/configured headers when submission through the relay is actually performed.
items.reproduction: Set MEV_PROTECTION_MODE=private and PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL to any non-empty string, issue a /build request, and observe X-MEV-Protection: private / X-MEV-Relay: configured with no relay submission code in the middleware.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: mev-protection.test.ts asserts the current intended behavior (headers claim private/configured when the URL is set, lines 82-92) and does not verify that any private submission occurs or that the URL is usable.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Configure MEV_PROTECTION_MODE=private with a placeholder/unreachable relay URL and assert the effective mode degrades to client (no X-MEV-Relay header) until relayer capability is confirmed.

items.title: Half-open trial admission is not exclusive: concurrent requests all pass as probes, and a failed trial can be masked by a concurrent successful trial
items.recommendation: Make trial admission single-flight and atomic: claim the probe with a short-TTL marker via a conditional/atomic KV write (or a Durable Object) and return 503 to any request observing an in-flight trial; serialize close/re-open decisions (e.g., re-read state before closeCircuit and only close if still half_open with the same openedAt) so a failed trial cannot be undone by a concurrent success.
items.reproduction: Open the circuit with 3 failing posts, sleep past cooldownSeconds, then fire N concurrent posts against a still-failing handler: all N reach the handler (expected exactly 1). Interleave one failing and one succeeding trial concurrently and observe the final state key absent (circuit closed) even though a trial failed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: circuit-breaker.test.ts awaits each post sequentially (lines 55-97, 100-112, 149-157), so requests never interleave inside the middleware; the half-open tests exercise a single trial at a time and never a concurrent success+failure pair.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: After opening the circuit and sleeping past cooldown, Promise.all N posts against a failing handler and assert exactly 1 reaches the handler; plus a test running a failing trial and a succeeding trial concurrently and asserting the state key is still present (circuit open) afterward.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/middleware/circuit-breaker.ts — half-open admission path (lines 167-180) and close path (lines 211-213)

items.title: Swap quote expiry is never enforced: expiresAt/deadline are dead fields and the 'expired' error reason is unreachable
items.recommendation: Enforce expiry in getQuote/buildCalldata: reject quotes older than quote.expiresAt (or honor params.deadline when provided) with a SwapQuoteError('expired', ...) before building calldata, and stop minting a fresh deadline in buildCalldata — either pass the quote's expiresAt through or re-quote when the quote is stale.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests (quote-engine, chain-state-reader, position.service) never exercise swap.service; there is no test asserting that a stale quote is rejected or that buildCalldata respects expiresAt.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that buildCalldata on a quote whose expiresAt is in the past (or whose age exceeds the advertised window) fails with reason 'expired' and produces no calldata.

items.title: Phase-2 keeper/auto-recenter paths are stubs that emit plausible-but-wrong results: constant-zero counters, unreachable failure branches, and current-range values labeled as rebalance targets
items.recommendation: Either implement the stubbed paths (evaluate TP/SL with real price reads, compute and persist optimal target ranges before queueing) or explicitly mark the methods/metrics as not-implemented: return distinct 'stub' markers, throw a typed not-implemented error, or omit the counters from KeeperTickResult so consumers cannot mistake them for real zeros.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No keeper.service or auto-recenter.service tests are included, and the stub behavior is only visible by executing the full D1-backed tick path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that tick() on a policy that passes the anti-whipsaw check reports rebalancesQueued/ordersTriggered consistent with what was actually queued (0 until implementation), or fails explicitly instead of returning zeros.

items.title: PriceService.readD1Price returns updatedAt double-converted to ms for millisecond-stored rows
items.recommendation: Return updatedAt: rowUpdatedAtMs (the same normalized value used for the freshness check) instead of row.updated_at * 1000.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No price.service tests are included, and the included tests never construct D1 rows with millisecond timestamps.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test readD1Price with a stub D1 returning updated_at = 1719715200000 (ms) and assert the returned PriceData.updatedAt equals 1719715200000; repeat with a seconds value.

items.title: KVCacheService reads parse JSON outside Effect.tryPromise: a single corrupt KV entry becomes an unhandled defect
items.recommendation: Wrap each JSON.parse in Effect.tryPromise (or Effect.try) alongside the kv.get and return Option.none on parse failure, matching the pattern in price.service.ts.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No kv.ts tests are included; the included tests never feed corrupt KV payloads to the service.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test getPrice/getSession with a KV mock returning 'not-json{' and assert the Effect succeeds with Option.none rather than dying.

items.title: SwapService.buildCalldata converts every typed failure into an Effect defect via Effect.die
items.recommendation: Remove the Effect.die catch and let buildCalldata's typed SwapQuoteError propagate (change the return type to Effect.Effect<{to,data,value}, SwapQuoteError>), or at minimum only die on unexpected (non-SwapQuoteError) errors.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No swap.service tests are included; the included tests only cover quote-engine, chain-state-reader, and position.service.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test buildCalldata with an unknown poolId resolves the failure as a typed SwapQuoteError with reason 'no_pool' (not a defect) when run via Effect.runPromise.

items.title: ChainStateReader tick scan issues up to 1025 parallel RPC readContract calls per getPoolState
items.recommendation: Lower the practical cap, make the scan size conservative by default, batch the probes (multicall3 or eth_call aggregation), or bound concurrency with a semaphore so a rate-limit failure is distinguishable and recoverable.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included chain-state-reader tests use tickScanEachSide: 1 with a mock client, so the live fan-out and rate-limit behavior are never exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test makeStateViewReaderLayer with tickScanEachSide = 512 asserts the client receives no more than a configured concurrency bound (or fails with a typed error rather than an unhandled burst).

items.title: R2 appendToArchive is a read-modify-write with no locking: concurrent appends silently drop trade records
items.recommendation: Serialize appends per key (e.g., a per-period queue consumer with a single in-flight writer, or D1-backed append journaling), or use R2 conditional writes/ETag checks to detect concurrent modification and retry, so a lost update fails loudly instead of overwriting silently.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests for r2.ts are included, and the race only manifests with concurrent callers, which no single-threaded unit test exercises.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that two sequential appendToArchive calls on the same period preserve both batches; additionally, a test asserting the service rejects/retries when the object changed between get and put (stubbed conditional write).

items.title: simulatePriceScenarios reports feePercent validation errors under the currentPrice field key
items.recommendation: Add a dedicated error key for the fee input (e.g., extend PlaygroundField with a feePercent key, or define a separate fee error channel) so the message renders under the fee field; if the field-set limitation is intentional, document the currentPrice attachment and surface the message generically.
items.reproduction: simulatePriceScenarios({ currentPrice: 2000, lowerPrice: 1500, upperPrice: 2500, amount0: 1, amount1: 1, priceChangesPercent: [0], feePercent: -1 }) returns errors.currentPrice === 'Fee percent must be zero or positive.'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: playground.test.ts covers invalid ranges and empty positions (lines 186-193) but never passes a negative/non-finite feePercent, so the misattributed error key is unexercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Call simulatePriceScenarios with feePercent: -1 and assert the returned errors are keyed by a feePercent-dedicated field (once added) rather than currentPrice.

items.title: Hand-written calldata ABIs are only regex-tested; ABI drift against deployed contracts would pass CI and revert on-chain
items.recommendation: Decode the produced calldata with viem decodeFunctionData against the same ABI and assert every argument value (ticks, amounts, fee, deadline, hookData/salt); add golden calldata fixtures generated from the deployed contracts' ABIs and selector-level assertions (like the existing 0xac9650d8 check) for zap and addLiquiditySingleSided.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests verify only that encodeFunctionData produced hex; they cannot detect any semantic mismatch between the locally hand-written ABI and the on-chain contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert decodeFunctionData(buildV4SingleSidedCall(...).calldata, AETHER_ROUTER_ABI) returns the exact args object (poolKey fields, liquidityDelta, minAmount0/minAmount1, deadline) for the fixture inputs.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/test/lib/v3-liquidity.test.ts and apps/web/test/lib/v4-liquidity.test.ts (plus golden fixtures from the contract ABIs).

items.title: V3 calldata builders accept non-positive deadlines while the V4 path rejects them
items.recommendation: Add a deadline > 0n validation in buildV3MintCall and buildV3SingleSidedZapCall (and, for symmetry, buildV3RebalancePlan), mirroring v4's validateInput check, or validate at the shared entry point before calldata construction.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: v3-liquidity.test.ts always passes future deadlines (2_000_000_000n and 123n); no test exercises a zero or past deadline for the v3 builders, so the divergence from the v4 path is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert buildV3MintCall and buildV3SingleSidedZapCall throw on deadline 0n (mirroring the existing v4 deadline rejection test coverage).

items.title: listPools and fetchTokens ignore HTTP error status (res.ok never checked)
items.recommendation: After fetch, check res.ok in listPools and fetchTokens and fail with an error that includes the HTTP status (mirroring fetchTokenByAddress), before calling res.json(). Optionally read the error body to surface the server message.
items.reproduction: Stub global fetch to resolve with new Response('<html>upstream error</html>', { status: 500 }) and run Effect.runPromise(listPools()): the rejection is a JSON parse error with no HTTP status anywhere in the message.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The suite contains no test/lib/api.test.ts at all; the only API-adjacent tests are protocol-fee tests for fetchDepositEstimate, which does check res.ok, so the inconsistent behavior in api.ts is never exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock fetch to return a 500 with a non-JSON body; assert Effect.runPromise(listPools(...)) rejects with an error matching /HTTP 500/ (repeat for fetchTokens).

items.title: Protected RPC broadcast has no timeout or abort path; non-JSON 200 bodies throw a raw SyntaxError
items.recommendation: Wire an abort path (accept an AbortSignal and/or apply AbortSignal.timeout) and convert AbortError into a descriptive error; wrap response.json() so a malformed 200 body yields a clear 'invalid RPC response' error instead of a raw SyntaxError.
items.reproduction: Stub fetch to return a promise that never resolves; await submitProtectedRawTransaction(...) — the call hangs indefinitely with no way to abort.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: protected-submission.test.ts only covers the HTTPS rejection and a single happy-path broadcast returning a JSON result; no stalled-response, abort, or malformed-body cases are tested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Stub fetch with a never-resolving promise and assert the call rejects within a bounded timeout with a descriptive error; also stub a 200 non-JSON body and assert a descriptive parse error rather than SyntaxError.

items.title: Unauthenticated, unthrottled /api/v1/auth/nonce creates one persistent Durable Object instance per nonce — unbounded instance growth
items.recommendation: Rate-limit the nonce endpoint (mount rateLimit() or a dedicated nonce limiter) and/or replace per-nonce DO instances with a small fixed set of DOs storing records keyed by nonce, consumed under blockConcurrencyWhile — or accept the tradeoff explicitly with instance-growth monitoring.
items.reproduction: Repeatedly POST /api/v1/auth/nonce; observe a distinct DO instance created per request with no deletion mechanism (only the record expires via alarm).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests verify issue/consume semantics for a single nonce; instance-count growth over many issuances is not asserted and the resource cost is invisible in the test pool.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/auth/routes.ts (rate limit on /nonce) and/or apps/api/src/auth/siwe.ts + apps/api/src/durable-objects/siwe-nonce-do.ts (bounded nonce storage design).

items.title: Malformed or missing JSON body on POST /api/v1/auth/verify returns 500 instead of 400
items.recommendation: Wrap the body parse in try/catch (or use a Hono validation middleware) and return 400 for JSON parse failures; optionally use Hono's app.onError to distinguish HTTPException (client) from thrown errors.
items.reproduction: POST /api/v1/auth/verify with body '{invalid' (or no body); the response is 500 Internal server error rather than a 400 validation error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: auth tests in the excerpted set exercise valid messages/signatures; the malformed-body path falls through to the global error handler and is not asserted as a 400.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: POST /api/v1/auth/verify with an invalid JSON body and assert status 400 (and no 5xx alert increment).
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/auth/routes.ts — catch the JSON parse error in the /verify handler and return 400.

items.title: Keeper advances the local nonce before receipt confirmation; a transient confirmation failure can double-execute or permanently stall an order on retry
items.recommendation: Persist submission state (nonce, txHash) before awaiting confirmation and make retries idempotent: on retry, first check on-chain order state / pending tx for the account before resubmitting; treat receipt-wait failures as 'submitted, unconfirmed' and reconcile rather than blindly retrying the submission.
items.reproduction: 1) Relay accepts eth_sendRawTransaction (tx N). 2) waitForTransactionReceipt throws (RPC timeout). 3) Queue retries sendTransaction. 4) Fresh signer: pendingNonce from public RPC = N → nonce N reused → relay rejects → order marked failed while tx N confirms. Same-instance retry: tx N+1 submitted while N pending → possible duplicate execution.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: keeper-signer.test.ts exercises single submissions and error mapping; the cross-retry interaction (private relay invisible to the public RPC's pending count, nonce advanced before confirmation) requires simulating a lost response between relay and receipt wait, which the existing test surface does not appear to cover.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A test where the relay accepts a tx, waitForTransactionReceipt throws, and a subsequent sendTransaction with a fresh signer instance must not reuse the in-flight nonce (assert the second submission either skips to N+1 or is refused as duplicate before signing).
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/lib/keeper-signer.ts — move nextNonce advancement and confirmation handling behind a persisted in-flight marker, and add an on-chain/order-state idempotency check on the retry path.

items.title: Non-atomic KV read-modify-write in rate limiter and circuit breaker lets concurrent requests bypass limits and lose failure counts
items.recommendation: Move counters to a Durable Object (per-caller or per-breaker) with blockConcurrencyWhile for atomic increments, or accept and document the approximate enforcement; for the breaker, at minimum re-read the state/count immediately before opening and treat half-open admission under a single-flight guard.
items.reproduction: Fire N concurrent POSTs to a rate-limited route with max=1 and a fresh KV counter: all N pass because each reads count 0 and writes 1. Similarly, trigger 10 concurrent 5xx responses with failureThreshold=5: the stored count ends up well below 5 and the circuit does not open.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests (circuit-breaker.test.ts, mev-protection.test.ts, etc.) exercise sequential requests; reproducing the lost-update race requires concurrent interleaving, which the KV-backed design makes non-deterministic.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Promise.all of N concurrent consumeRateLimit(kv, key, {max:1}) calls asserting exactly one is allowed (currently fails); for the breaker, N concurrent recordFailure calls with threshold 5 asserting the circuit opens exactly once.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts and apps/api/src/middleware/circuit-breaker.ts — replace KV counter increments with an atomic primitive (DO) or document the race and cap burst exposure.

items.title: OrderBookDO broadcasts to an empty in-memory subscriber map after hibernation, silently dropping live order book updates
items.recommendation: Mirror the WebSocketHubDO pattern: enumerate ctx.getWebSockets() in broadcast() (and hydrate the subscribers map on wake), or drop the in-memory map entirely and serialize the subscription state in the socket attachment, filtering per-socket by the poolId tag/attachment.
items.reproduction: 1) Connect a WebSocket to /ws/orderbook/:poolId; receive the initial snapshot. 2) Let the DO idle long enough to be evicted (hibernation). 3) POST an /update to the DO (queue consumer path). 4) The client receives no orderbook_update even though the handler returns { ok: true, subscribers: 0 }.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included/excerpted tests were omitted from the review context, and unit tests in the vitest workers pool exercise fetch()/webSocketMessage() within a single instance lifetime; they cannot reproduce workerd's eviction-and-wake cycle that destroys the in-memory map.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A pool-workers test that (1) upgrades a socket on the DO, (2) simulates eviction by clearing instance memory (or asserts broadcast delivery derives from ctx.getWebSockets() rather than the in-memory Map), and (3) POSTs /update and asserts the socket receives orderbook_update with delivered == 1.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/durable-objects/order-book-do.ts only — make broadcast() enumerate ctx.getWebSockets() (and hydrate the map like WebSocketHubDO.hydrateSubscribers).

items.title: bun run typecheck excludes test/ and vitest.config.ts, so type errors in tests and the test harness go undetected
items.recommendation: Add "test/**/*" and "vitest.config.ts" to tsconfig include (with a separate tsconfig.test.json if DOM/worker types conflict), so `bun run typecheck` covers the whole package.
items.reproduction: Introduce a type error in any apps/api/test/*.ts file; `bun run typecheck` exits 0 and `bun run test` still runs (esbuild strips types).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is a gap in the verification tooling itself; no test can detect that tests are not type-checked.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/tsconfig.json — extend include to test/**/* and vitest.config.ts (and package.json typecheck script if a dedicated tsconfig is needed).

items.title: cancelOrder/executeOrder/expireOrder report OrderNotFoundError when the row exists but is not pending
items.recommendation: Distinguish the two cases: check existence first (or use RETURNING) and return a distinct state-conflict error when the order exists but is not pending; at minimum document that OrderNotFoundError covers non-pending states.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for tp-sl.service.ts is included in this feature, so the error semantics of the status transitions are unverified.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Seed an executed order, call executeOrder again, and assert a state-conflict error is returned rather than OrderNotFoundError.

items.title: Indexer fetches block timestamps with one sequential RPC call per unique block
items.recommendation: Fetch timestamps for all unique blocks concurrently (e.g., Promise.all over the unique block numbers) or batch the lookups, preserving a bounded concurrency limit.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover only log parsing and the reducer; the indexer's RPC fetching path is not under test.

items.title: V3QuoteService never verifies the RPC chain, unlike every other chain-bound reader in this feature
items.recommendation: Add chainId to V3QuoteServiceDeps and verify it (with caching) before quoting, mirroring the pattern in v4-position-reader.service.ts.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for v3-quote.service.ts is included in this feature, and the chain check is absent, so nothing asserts it.

items.title: Collect event ABI marks recipient as indexed, so real NonfungiblePositionManager Collect logs fail to decode and are silently dropped
items.recommendation: Change the Collect entry in POSITION_MANAGER_ABI so recipient is `indexed: false` (matching the deployed contract), and add a fixture decoding a real Collect log (topics = signature + tokenId, recipient/amount0/amount1 in data).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: v3-liquidity-events.test.ts only tests IncreaseLiquidity and pool Mint events; there is no Collect fixture, and any test built from this same (wrong) ABI would encode the bug into the fixture and pass.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Encode a Collect log with the canonical ABI (only tokenId indexed) and assert parseV3LiquidityLog returns eventType 'collect' with the correct recipient, amount0, and amount1.

items.title: executeOrder and recordKeeperExecution are separate non-transactional writes; keeper audit records can be lost or orphaned
items.recommendation: Wrap both writes in a single transaction (e.g., a CTE or transaction block that updates the order and inserts the keeper execution), and/or make executeOrder idempotent so a retry with the same txHash can backfill the record.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for tp-sl.service.ts, and the interplay between executeOrder and recordKeeperExecution is not exercised anywhere in the included tests.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: With a stubbed SqlClient that fails the second statement, assert the order status and keeper record stay consistent (both committed or both rolled back), and assert retry behavior with the same txHash.

items.title: verifyTrigger hardcodes TWAP to null and returns isTriggered as dualTriggerMet, so it always returns false
items.recommendation: Either implement the AetherHook TWAP read, or fail the effect with a VerificationError when TWAP is unavailable instead of returning a successful always-false verdict; surface errors[] to callers and stop computing an isTriggered result that is unconditionally overridden.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for verification.service.ts is included in this feature, and the placeholder is self-documented as a TODO, so no test asserts actual trigger behavior.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test verifyTrigger with a stubbed ChainStateReader asserting that when TWAP is unavailable the effect fails (or errors[] is non-empty) rather than returning isTriggered: false.

items.title: Volume-alert cooldown is a check-then-act race that can emit duplicate alerts
items.recommendation: Accept and document the duplicate risk, or make the guard atomic — e.g., use an insert with a unique constraint keyed on (chainId, poolId, window) in D1, or deduplicate by envelope identity in the hub.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for volume-alerts.service.ts is included in this feature, and the race only manifests with concurrent tick invocations, which the included tests never exercise.

items.title: TP/SL order lifecycle service has no tests covering status transitions and error semantics
items.recommendation: Add a vitest suite for tp-sl.service.ts using @effect/sql-d1 against an in-memory/seeded D1 covering create/get/list, every status transition including double-transition errors, and keeper execution recording.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for tp-sl.service.ts is included in the feature; existing tests cover only v3-liquidity-events and v3-position-reducer.

items.title: Integer-only fields typed as Schema.Number accept fractional values
items.recommendation: Use Schema.Int (or more specific refinements like Schema.NonNegativeInt / Schema.PositiveInt) for fee, tickSpacing, currentTick, chainId, decimals, and count fields.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no tests for the schemas, so the absence of integrality enforcement is unobserved.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest test asserting that decoding { fee: 3000.5, ... } with PoolSchema fails with a parse error while { fee: 3000 } succeeds.

items.title: No tests or test script for the shared API-contract package
items.recommendation: Add a `test` script (e.g. `vitest run`) plus a vitest devDependency, and add unit tests that encode/decode each schema against representative fixtures and assert decode failures for malformed payloads.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist anywhere in the package (no test script, no test files, no test devDependency), so there is nothing covering the schema contracts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest test that decodes a full Pool fixture through PoolSchema and asserts the result matches the input, plus negative cases asserting failure for a missing field and a non-string sqrtPriceX96.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/shared/package.json (scripts + devDependencies) and a new test file under packages/shared/src/__tests__/

items.title: Shared contract built on exact-pinned beta and unstable API surface
items.recommendation: Track effect releases deliberately (upgrade in a dedicated commit, run full-workspace typecheck and decode smoke tests), and consider moving to stable Effect APIs once available; at minimum add a smoke test that constructs the RPC group and round-trips a payload to catch upstream churn.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist, so upstream beta API changes would only surface via typecheck of downstream packages at upgrade time.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A smoke test that builds PoolsRpcGroup and round-trips a ListPools payload through the RPC schema encoders/decoders.

items.title: Package exports raw TypeScript source with no build step
items.recommendation: Either keep private:true and document the workspace-only TS-source contract explicitly, or add a build step that emits dist/ with proper exports/types conditions (with a files allowlist) before any publication is considered.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is a packaging/tooling hazard not exercised by the current lint/typecheck scripts, and there are no tests or CI packaging steps in the package.

items.title: README/AGENTS.md toolchain claims contradict package.json (TypeScript, Biome, Vitest versions)
items.recommendation: Update README.md and AGENTS.md version inventories to match package.json (or pin the rc/native-preview toolchain if that is the intended state), and keep a single source of truth for toolchain versions.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Documentation drift is not exercised by tests.

items.title: Root typecheck excludes apps/** so the documented typecheck gate does not validate application code
items.recommendation: Compose per-workspace typecheck into the root script (e.g., `typecheck`: `bun run --filter '*' typecheck` with per-app typecheck scripts, or explicit `tsc -p apps/web` / `tsc -p apps/api` invocations), or wire tsconfig project references so the root gate covers all workspaces.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Typechecking is a build-time gate, not covered by unit tests; the gap only manifests as uncaught type errors in workspace code.

items.title: test:coverage depends on an undeclared @vitest/coverage-v8 provider
items.recommendation: Add @vitest/coverage-v8 (matching the vitest major version) to devDependencies and, when threshold enforcement is intended, configure coverage.thresholds per project in vitest.config.ts.
