items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test exercises the npm scripts; the failure manifests only when a developer or CI runs `bun run test:coverage`.

items.title: packageManager pinned to floating bun@canary tag — non-reproducible toolchain
items.recommendation: Pin an exact build (e.g., bun@1.4.x-canary.<build> or a released version) in packageManager, and record the resolved `bun --version` output in tooling/scripts/VERSIONS.md as AGENTS.md already intends, ideally with a CI check that the installed Bun matches the recorded version.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Toolchain reproducibility is not exercised by unit tests; nothing in the test suite verifies the resolved Bun version.

items.title: Root vitest config only runs apps/web tests; documented 'all workspaces' test command silently skips the backend
items.recommendation: List every test-bearing workspace in vitest.config.ts projects (e.g., projects: ["./apps/web", "./apps/api"] or a glob), and drop passWithNoTests (or set it per-project) so empty/missing suites fail loudly. Add a root project or CI step that asserts the expected projects are configured.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The misconfiguration causes the test command to skip suites while still succeeding, so no failing test can surface it — the gap is in the runner configuration itself, not in any test body.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A small root vitest project that imports the vitest config and asserts every workspace directory containing a vitest config (or test files) — at minimum apps/api — appears in the projects list.

items.title: MEV private relay accepts cleartext http URLs in safety-config, contradicting the https-only policy enforced in keeper-signer
items.recommendation: Reuse the same https-only parsing as keeper-signer (new URL + protocol === "https:" check) in readMevProtectionConfig, requiring a valid host, and add unit tests for safety-config.ts covering http, ws, bare 'http://', and malformed values.
items.reproduction: readMevProtectionConfig({ PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL: "http://relay.example" }) returns privateRelayUrl = "http://relay.example", whereas readKeeperSignerConfig with the same env value yields privateRelayUrl = null.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: keeper-signer.test.ts (lines 82-89) tests parseRelayUrl's https enforcement, but there is no test file for safety-config.ts at all, so the lenient http-accepting regex in readMevProtectionConfig is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: expect(readMevProtectionConfig({ PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL: "http://relay.example" }).privateRelayUrl).toBeNull(); expect(readMevProtectionConfig({ PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL: "http://" }).privateRelayUrl).toBeNull(); expect(readMevProtectionConfig({ PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL: "https://relay.example" }).privateRelayUrl).toBe("https://relay.example")

items.title: Keeper nonce tracking is per-signer-instance: a transient failure after private-relay acceptance can reuse a nonce and permanently fail the order
items.recommendation: Make nonce state durable (persist nextNonce in KV/D1 keyed by keeper address, or have the relay/submission path acknowledge the accepted nonce) and treat post-acceptance failures as ambiguous: before retrying with a fresh signer, query the relay/RPC for the transaction by hash or advance the nonce from durable state instead of re-deriving it from the public pending count.
items.reproduction: 1) Signer A submits via private relay; relay accepts and returns a valid hash. 2) waitForTransactionReceipt throws (RPC timeout) → KeeperRpcError. 3) Queue retries with a freshly constructed signer B. 4) preflight reads pending nonce from the public RPC (does not include the private tx) → same nonce N. 5) Relay rejects with nonce-too-low (non-retryable) → submission fails permanently.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: keeper-signer.test.ts line 422-443 ('serializes concurrent submissions and allocates distinct pending nonces') exercises only concurrent calls on one signer instance where nextNonce is shared; no test simulates a retry with a new signer instance after a transient failure post-acceptance.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create signer A, submit with mocked waitForTransactionReceipt rejecting; then create signer B with the same config and a chain stub whose getTransactionCount still returns 7; assert the second submission does not reuse nonce 7 (either via a nonce store or an explicit duplicate-nonce guard).
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/lib/keeper-signer.ts (durable nonce state or ambiguity-aware retry) + regression test

items.title: Public submission signs transactions without an explicit chainId (chain: null), losing EIP-155 replay protection
items.recommendation: Create the wallet client with the configured chain (e.g. define a viem chain with the keeper's chainId) or pass chainId explicitly in the sendTransaction call so the signature includes EIP-155 chainId, mirroring the private-relay path (line 456).
items.reproduction: With KEEPER_ALLOW_PUBLIC_SUBMISSION=true on an EIP-155 chain, walletClient.sendTransaction is called with chain: null and no chainId; the resulting legacy signature omits the EIP-155 chainId.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The public-submission tests (keeper-signer.test.ts lines 384-443) use a stubbed walletClient that returns a hash without performing real signing, and assert only that chain: null is passed; no test verifies the chainId embedded in the signed transaction.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Use a real local account with the public path against a stubbed transport capturing the serialized transaction and assert the raw tx contains the EIP-155 chainId (e.g. re-derive the v value / inspect the serialized fields for the configured chain).
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/lib/keeper-signer.ts (supply chainId in public submission) + signing-level regression test

items.title: Unauthenticated /nonce endpoint creates one Durable Object per request with no rate limiting
items.recommendation: Add per-client/IP rate limiting (e.g., a KV- or DO-based token bucket) on POST /nonce and /verify, and/or cap outstanding nonces per client; alternatively use a single DO that stores nonces keyed by name instead of one DO per nonce.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this source group, and rate-limit behavior would require the DO implementation, which is not included in this feature's files.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that issues N nonce requests from the same client and asserts the client is throttled after a configured limit (or that a bounded number of DO instances are created).
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/auth/routes.ts and/or the siwe-nonce Durable Object

items.title: No tests exist for the authentication flow (session validation, SIWE verify, nonce consumption)
items.recommendation: Add vitest/cloudflare-pool-workers tests covering: happy-path verify → session readable via /me; reusing the same nonce twice fails; expired session JSON is rejected and deleted from KV; wrong chainId/domain/uri in message fails; malformed session JSON falls through to 401 on requireAuth; logout deletes the session so /me then returns 401.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files exist for this source group (tests: [] in feature metadata); the vitest infrastructure is configured in apps/api/package.json but nothing covers apps/api/src/auth.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: verifyAndCreateSession: issue nonce, verify with valid signature, assert second verify with the same (message, signature) fails with invalid/expired nonce; authMiddleware: write a session with expiresAt in the past into KV and assert requireAuth returns 401 and the KV key is removed.

items.title: /verify collapses all failures, including server-side errors, into a 401 Authentication failed response
items.recommendation: Distinguish failure classes: map Effect.fail from verification logic to 401, but map thrown/unexpected errors (KV, DO, JSON parsing) to 500 with a generic server-error message and log the underlying error; do not expose String(err) internals to clients.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this source group; the error-classification behavior is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock KVCacheService.putSession to throw and assert POST /verify returns 500 (not 401); assert an invalid signature returns 401.

items.title: Inconsistent handling of invalid sessions in authMiddleware: malformed JSON is never deleted and kv.delete is unguarded
items.recommendation: Delete the session key in the catch block as well (best-effort, wrapped in try/catch), and wrap the validation-failure kv.delete in try/catch so middleware failures never 500 the request.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this source group, and malformed-session cleanup is an edge path unlikely to be exercised manually.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Insert a session key with invalid JSON into KV, make a request with that Bearer token, and assert the middleware passes through and the key is deleted.

items.title: fetchTokenPrice ignores the chain id and hardcodes the Ethereum CoinGecko endpoint; price KV keys are chain-agnostic
items.recommendation: Map CHAIN_ID to the CoinGecko platform (e.g., 'ethereum', 'base', 'arbitrum-one') and namespace KV keys by chain, or restrict price refresh to the configured chain explicitly.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover fetchTokenPrice or KV key scoping.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test fetchTokenPrice with a non-Ethereum chain id asserting the correct platform in the request URL, and that price keys include the chain.

items.title: No test coverage for cron and queue handlers; index.test.ts is a placeholder
items.recommendation: Add unit tests for the trigger-condition matrix (take_profit/stop_loss × zeroForOne × spot/TWAP), toScaledBigInt, keeper tick enqueue/expire behavior, and handler skip paths; replace the placeholder index.test.ts.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The listed tests only cover v3-indexer-cursor helpers; no test imports cron-handler or queue-handler.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Parameterized tests over the four trigger branches asserting isTriggered, plus a keeper-tick test with mocked D1 asserting enqueue and expiry side effects.

items.title: Price-refresh consumer performs unbounded sequential HTTP fetches with no timeout
items.recommendation: Add an AbortSignal timeout to fetchTokenPrice, cap per-message token count, and/or process tokens with bounded concurrency (e.g., batches of 5-10).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover handlePriceRefresh or fetchTokenPrice.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock a hanging fetch and assert fetchTokenPrice aborts within a bounded time and handlePriceRefresh continues to the next token.

items.title: Unguarded JSON.parse of KV payload aborts the entire pool refresh
items.recommendation: Wrap the JSON.parse per address (or per batch) so a corrupt entry degrades to null for that token only, matching the per-pool try/catch already used in the write loop.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover refreshTopPools behavior with malformed cache entries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Seed one corrupt `price:` KV value among valid ones and assert the remaining pools still receive poolSpot writes.

items.title: TP/SL and auto-recenter evaluation depends on `poolSpot` cache entries that are only written for the top 50 pools by TVL
items.recommendation: Compute/store pool spot prices for all pools referenced by active orders/policies (e.g., backfill poolSpot for pools with pending tp_sl_orders or active position_policies), or fall back to an on-chain spot read in the evaluation handlers.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exercise the poolSpot lifecycle or the skip paths in handleTpSlEvaluate.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Seed a pending order for a pool ranked outside the top 50 by TVL, run the refresh + evaluate flow, and assert the order is evaluated rather than skipped.

items.title: Inconsistent silent chain-id fallbacks: keeper tick defaults to 11155111 and price enqueue to 1 when CHAIN_ID is invalid
items.recommendation: Use `parseChainId` consistently in all ticks and skip (log) on invalid CHAIN_ID instead of falling back to a hardcoded chain.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover cron-handler tick behavior with invalid CHAIN_ID.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Call runKeeperTick and enqueuePriceRefresh with CHAIN_ID='not-a-chain' and assert no queries/enqueues occur.

items.title: Auto-recenter never triggers: poolSpot cache payload never contains the `tick` field the handler requires, and the handler queues no rebalance action
items.recommendation: Either write `tick` into the poolSpot payload in `refreshTopPools` (or a dedicated pool-state writer), or derive the tick from the stored 1e18 price in `handleAutoRecenterCheck` as its own comment suggests; and actually dispatch the rebalance work (queue message or direct call) instead of only logging/updating counters.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for `refreshTopPools` or `handleAutoRecenterCheck`; the only worker test (v3-indexer-cursor.test.ts) covers cursor helpers, and index.test.ts is a placeholder.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Integration test: run `handleAutoRecenterCheck` against a poolSpot KV entry produced by `refreshTopPools` with an out-of-range tick and assert a rebalance is enqueued; also assert the poolSpot payload contains the tick field.

items.title: Input generates non-deterministic DOM ids with Math.random() instead of useId()
items.recommendation: Replace Math.random() with React's useId() (const inputId = id ?? useId()), which is stable across hydration and collision-free.
items.reproduction: Render <Input label="X" /> twice without an id; the id attributes differ between renders, and a hydrated/prerendered page would mismatch the client-generated id.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included test imports or renders Input, so id generation behavior is entirely untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render <Input label="x" />, re-render, and assert the id attribute is stable across renders; also assert the label's htmlFor matches the input's id.

items.title: Card accepts variant="bordered" but never implements it
items.recommendation: Either remove "bordered" from the variant union, or implement it (e.g., treat it as forcing the border regardless of the `bordered` prop). Also consider whether `bordered` defaulting to true while "default" is the default variant is intentional.
items.reproduction: Render <Card variant="bordered" bordered={false}> — no border class is emitted despite the variant name; render <Card variant="bordered"> — identical markup to <Card variant="default">.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only test file for this feature (apps/web/test/index.test.ts) never imports or renders any component from this source group, so the dead variant is never exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A component test asserting that <Card variant="bordered" bordered={false}> still renders the border classes (if the variant is kept), or a type-level test asserting the variant union no longer contains "bordered" (if removed).

items.title: Feature's only test never imports or exercises any owned component
items.recommendation: Add component tests under apps/web/test that import from the ui barrel and render Button, Card, Input, and Stat (e.g., with @testing-library/react, which is already in devDependencies), covering loading disables the button, variant/className composition, and label/input id association. Ensure a vitest environment (happy-dom) is configured for DOM assertions.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test deliberately avoids the components — it is a smoke test of the test harness itself, not of the feature.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A test file that renders each component via @testing-library/react and asserts: Button with loading disables the button and shows the spinner; Card variant="compact" emits card-compact; Input without id matches label htmlFor to input id; Stat trend="down" emits text-error.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/test (new test file) plus confirming vitest environment config

items.title: Button applies daisyUI loading state twice (btn loading class plus a second spinner span)
items.recommendation: Pick one mechanism: either keep the `loading` class on the button (and drop the inner span, letting the `btn loading` modifier render the spinner) or drop the class and keep the span. Also consider aria-busy for accessibility.
items.reproduction: Render <Button loading> with daisyUI styles applied; two spinner indicators appear inside the button.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test imports or renders Button, and the smoke test asserts only vitest globals and window/document existence.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render <Button loading> and assert exactly one element with the daisyUI loading spinner classes is present.

items.title: Button propagates className via rest spread after attribute composition, allowing callers to silently clobber styling
items.recommendation: No change required; pattern is idiomatic.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: N/A

items.title: Selected-token logo renders without the image-host allowlist used in the results list
items.recommendation: Render the selected-token logo only when isSafeImageUrl(token.logoURI) is true, mirroring TokenListItem, and apply the same guard in TokenChip.tsx. Consider centralizing logo rendering in a single shared component.
items.reproduction: Mock /tokens to return a token with logoURI 'https://evil.example/pixel.png'; open the picker (placeholder shows, no img), select the token, and observe an in the button.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: TokenSearch.test.tsx fixtures all use logoUrl: null, so no test exercises a logoURI value, let alone one from a disallowed host.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Select a token whose logoURI is 'https://untrusted.example/x.png' and assert the button contains no img element (and that a disallowed-host token still renders the symbol text).

items.title: PriceTicker crashes on WebSocket frames without tokenAddress
items.recommendation: Add a typeof payload.tokenAddress === 'string' condition to the existing guard (or use optional chaining: payload.tokenAddress?.toLowerCase() === tokenAddress.toLowerCase()) before setData.
items.reproduction: Feed the useWebSocket hook an envelope of the form { type: 'price', data: { price: 1.23 } } (no tokenAddress) and observe an uncaught TypeError in the effect.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no PriceTicker tests in the included test files, and the useWebSocket hook is not stubbed anywhere, so the frame-filtering path is entirely untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render PriceTicker with a mocked useWebSocket that first emits { type:'price', data:{ price: 1 } } (no tokenAddress) and assert the component does not throw and keeps showing the placeholder price.

items.title: ThemeToggle reads/writes localStorage unguarded and applies stored theme only after first paint
items.recommendation: Read the stored theme synchronously in the useState initializer (with try/catch around getItem) and apply the data-theme attribute in the same render, or use useLayoutEffect; wrap both getItem and setItem in try/catch with a sensible fallback so storage failures degrade gracefully instead of crashing.
items.reproduction: Set localStorage['aetherdex-theme']='light', reload the page: first paint is 'aetherdex' before flipping to 'light'. Alternatively, make localStorage.getItem throw and observe the effect error propagate.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: ThemeToggle.test.tsx stubs localStorage with a permissive Map-based mock (lines 8-23) and asserts post-mount behavior only; it never simulates storage throwing and cannot observe pre-effect paint.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A test where the localStorage mock's getItem throws, asserting the component still renders with data-theme='aetherdex'; plus a test asserting data-theme equals the stored value on the very first render (initializer-based, no effect).

items.title: Stale in-flight search responses can overwrite newer TokenSearch results
items.recommendation: Guard searchTokens with a request sequence number or AbortController: capture a monotonically increasing request id (or abort the previous fetch) before each call, and ignore setResults/setIsSearching from any response whose id is not the latest. The cleanup in the debounce effect should also invalidate the in-flight request.
items.reproduction: Mock fetch with manually resolved deferred promises: type 'US' (slow request), then type 'USD' (fast request), then resolve the 'US' promise after the 'USD' promise; the list shows tokens matching 'US' while the input says 'USD'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: TokenSearch.test.tsx mocks fetch as an instant resolver and types queries sequentially; no test simulates overlapping in-flight requests with out-of-order resolution, so the race is never exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that returns manually-controlled deferred promises from the fetch mock, types 'US' then 'USD', resolves the 'US' request after 'USD', and asserts the rendered list matches 'USD' and the spinner state reflects the newest request.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/src/components/TokenSearch.tsx (searchTokens and the debounce effect only)

items.title: Address truncation is wrong when length is 0
items.recommendation: Guard the truncation branch: only truncate when length > 0 (or when the computed result is shorter than the original), e.g., if (length <= 0 || address.length < length * 2 + 3) return the full address.
items.reproduction: Render <Address address={'0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678'} length={0} /> and observe output longer than the input with a spurious ellipsis.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for Address.tsx, and the default (length=4) path is the only one that would be exercised incidentally.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A parameterized test rendering Address with lengths 0, 1, 4 and asserting the rendered text length is strictly less than the input length whenever the input is long enough to truncate.

items.title: Most owned components have no tests; formatting and range-clamping edge cases are uncovered
items.recommendation: Add unit tests for the pure formatting helpers (formatPrice, formatUsd, formatChange, formatVolume), Address truncation boundaries, and RangeSelector snap/clamp invariants (lower < upper, step alignment, NaN inputs); add a PoolStats test with a mocked fetch covering empty/malformed pairs responses and the chainId filter.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test files only import ThemeToggle and TokenSearch; the other components are not referenced by any included test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A new test file (e.g., apps/web/test/components/format.test.tsx) covering formatPrice(0), formatPrice(0.001), formatPrice(-5), formatUsd(2_000_000), and a RangeSelector render asserting the two range inputs never cross (lower <= upper).
items.minimumFixScope: Add tests only; no production code changes required.

items.title: Hand-rolled SIWE message omits EIP-4361 Issued At and leaves nonce replay window unbounded
items.recommendation: Build the message with the `siwe` package (or at minimum append an Issued At line) and keep the nonce server-issued, single-use, and expiry-bound.
items.reproduction: Attempt verification of the generated message with a siwe-compliant parser: parsing/verification fails on missing issuedAt.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No useSiweAuth test is among the included files; the handshake is only exercised against the live backend, so message-format conformance is never asserted.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test that the constructed message round-trips through siwe.Message parsing and includes issuedAt.

items.title: listPools/fetchTokens parse error responses as JSON and hide the HTTP status
items.recommendation: Mirror fetchTokenByAddress: check res.ok and Effect.fail with the HTTP status before parsing.
items.reproduction: Point the app at a backend returning 500 with a non-JSON body and call listPools; the error message says "Pools parse failed" rather than reporting HTTP 500.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests among the included files are not visible (test/lib/* omitted); unit tests typically mock 2xx JSON responses only.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock a 500 response with an HTML body; assert the resulting error mentions the HTTP status.

items.title: PoolStats assumes pairs is always an array; DexScreener returns pairs:null for unknown tokens
items.recommendation: Normalize with `const pairs = json.pairs ?? []` before filtering/sorting, and consider retry:false for this third-party, rate-limited query.
items.reproduction: Open PoolStats with any address that has no pairs on DexScreener; the queryFn throws and the query enters error state with retries.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No PoolStats test is among the included files; typical mocks return a pairs array, and the null-pairs shape of the real API is easy to miss.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock fetch returning {pairs:null}; assert the query resolves to null without error state and without retries.

items.title: useWebSocket URL-change race defeats the unmount guard: stale onclose reconnects to the old URL and leaks the active socket
items.recommendation: Guard every handler by socket identity (e.g. `if (wsRef.current !== ws) return` inside onopen/onmessage/onclose/onerror) and clear any pending reconnect timer when a new connection is opened, or track a per-connection generation counter captured in connect().
items.reproduction: Mount useWebSocket with url A, wait for onopen, then re-render with url B. Observe isConnected flicker, a reconnect timer to A, and two live sockets (A's reconnect socket plus B's orphaned one).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The useWebSocket test file (test/hooks/useWebSocket.test.ts) was omitted from the included excerpts, so there is no evidence it exercises URL changes while connected; typical tests cover open/close/reconnect on a fixed URL only.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test: connect with url A, change url to B while connected, assert exactly one live socket (track close() calls), no reconnect timer scheduled for A, and isConnected stays true for B.

items.title: TokenSearch debounced search applies stale responses over newer queries (no abort/sequencing)
items.recommendation: Create an AbortController per debounce run and abort it in the effect cleanup, or track a request sequence number and discard resolutions from stale runs (the cancelled-flag pattern already used for defaultTokens load).
items.reproduction: Type "uni" and let the 300ms debounce fire, then type "usdc" before the first response arrives; if the first request resolves last, the dropdown shows "uni" results for the "usdc" query.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: test/components/TokenSearch.test.tsx was omitted from the included excerpts; happy-path tests with instantly-resolving mocks cannot expose interleaved slow responses.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock fetch with manually-resolved promises: trigger query A, change to query B before A resolves, resolve A after B; assert displayed results and isSearching reflect B.

items.title: PriceTicker crashes when a WebSocket frame carries a numeric price without tokenAddress
items.recommendation: Guard with `typeof payload.tokenAddress === "string"` before toLowerCase() (or validate envelopes with a runtime schema such as Effect Schema, consistent with api.ts), and require Number.isFinite(payload.price).
items.reproduction: Point PriceTicker at a hub that emits {type:"ping", data:{price:0}} or any envelope whose data has price but no tokenAddress; the component throws.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No PriceTicker test is among the included files, and the omitted useWebSocket test cannot cover PriceTicker's payload-shape assumptions; tests likely only feed well-formed PricePayload frames.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render PriceTicker with a mocked WebSocket that delivers {data:{price:1}} without tokenAddress; assert no throw and the placeholder dash is shown.

items.title: Input generates a new Math.random-based id on every render
items.recommendation: Use React's useId() for a stable id.
items.reproduction: Render Input, force a parent re-render, and observe the input's id attribute change.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests (ui.test.tsx omitted from included files) typically query by label/role text, which does not assert id stability across re-renders.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render Input inside a stateful parent, re-render the parent, and assert the input id is unchanged.

items.title: README documents outdated Vite version and wrong typecheck tool
items.recommendation: Update README to Vite 8 and correct the typecheck annotation to tsc.
items.reproduction: Read README.md, then compare with package.json scripts/dependencies.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Not applicable; documentation accuracy is not covered by tests.

items.title: Beta dependency and unstable API surface (effect/unstable/rpc) with no upgrade guard
items.recommendation: Keep the exact beta pin deliberately (document why in the manifest), and add a contract test that constructs the RpcGroup and decodes a sample payload so an upgrade that changes the unstable API fails CI instead of production.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist in this feature, so the RPC definitions' validity against the unstable API is never exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that calls RpcGroup.make(ListPools) and decodes an example payload through the RPC's payload schema, run after any dependency bump.
items.minimumFixScope: Add RPC-definition smoke test in packages/shared; no production change required beyond the existing pin.

items.title: Shared contract package has no tests and no test script
items.recommendation: Add a test script (e.g. bun test) and schema round-trip tests using Schema.encodeSync/decodeUnknownSync for PoolSchema, TokenSchema, ListPoolsPayloadSchema, and the response schemas, plus a smoke test that Rpc.make/RpcGroup.make construct successfully.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included in this feature and no test script exists in packages/shared/package.json, so schema/RPC correctness is entirely unverified.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Round-trip test: encode a Pool object with Schema.encodeSync(PoolSchema) then decode with Schema.decodeUnknownSync(PoolSchema) and assert equality; likewise for a ListPools payload and the ListPools RPC success schema.
items.minimumFixScope: Add tests and a test script under packages/shared; no production code change required.

items.title: List-pools response has two competing shapes: bare array in RPC vs unused PoolListResponseSchema wrapper
items.recommendation: Pick one contract: either set the RPC success schema to PoolListResponseSchema or delete the unused wrapper schemas (and align TokenListResponseSchema/TokenResponseSchema usage) so the shared package exposes a single shape per operation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist, and the server implementation is outside this feature's files, so nothing detects the shape mismatch between the two definitions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert that the ListPools RPC success schema is Schema.Array(PoolSchema) (or the wrapper, per chosen contract) and that PoolListResponseSchema is referenced somewhere or removed.
items.minimumFixScope: Align rpc.ts success schema with the response schema (or remove the unused wrapper) in packages/shared/src.

items.title: Health endpoint body always reports status "ok" even when dependency probes fail (503)
items.recommendation: Derive the body status from the probe results, e.g. `status: allHealthy ? "ok" : "degraded"` (compute allHealthy before building the payload, or set the field after), so the payload and the HTTP status code can never disagree.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only linked test file (apps/api/test/index.test.ts) contains placeholder assertions for string concatenation and arithmetic; no test exercises the /health handler or its degraded path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: With stubbed bindings where checkD1/checkKV/checkR2 fail, call app.request('/health') and assert the HTTP status is 503 and the body's status field is not "ok".

items.title: Structured request log is skipped for requests whose handler throws (500s logged without request context)
items.recommendation: Wrap the post-next logging in try/finally (or catch, log the 500 entry, and rethrow) so a structured log line with method, path, status 500, and duration is emitted for every request, including failures.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests do not exercise middleware behavior or logging at all.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Register a stub route that throws, spy on console.log/console.error, and assert a JSON log line containing method, path, and status 500 is emitted in addition to the onError output.

items.title: CORS default allowlist includes http://localhost:3000 and is inherited by any environment that omits CORS_ORIGINS
items.recommendation: Remove localhost from the fallback default (use only the production origin) and require CORS_ORIGINS to be set explicitly per environment, or gate the localhost entry on c.env.ENVIRONMENT being a dev value.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No CORS tests exist in the linked suite; the placeholder tests never construct requests with an Origin header.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Call the origin callback (or app.request with an Origin header) with ENVIRONMENT=production and no CORS_ORIGINS set, asserting that http://localhost:3000 is not allowed.

items.title: Feature test suite is placeholder-only; the API entry point has no test coverage
items.recommendation: Replace the placeholder tests with real coverage using the already-declared @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers devDependency: test /health (healthy and degraded), CORS allow/deny for configured origins, invalid poolId → 400, canonicalized poolId forwarding (uppercase hex input maps to lower-case idFromName), 404 JSON shape, and onError returning a generic 500.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests assert unrelated trivial behavior and were evidently written as scaffolding; they cannot catch regressions in any code path of apps/api/src/index.ts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Describe suite: (1) `app.request('/health')` with healthy bindings → 200 + status "ok"; (2) with a failing D1 stub → 503 + degraded status; (3) `app.request('/ws/orderbook/0xABC...')` with 64-hex uppercase poolId → request forwarded with lower-cased poolId; (4) invalid poolId → 400.

items.title: Dev-stage name derivation diverges between the alchemy scripts and the Pages upload script
items.recommendation: Derive the dev stage name once (e.g., a shared helper script or a single environment variable set before all commands) using the same sanitization, and use that value in `plan:dev`, `deploy:dev`, `destroy:dev`, and `web:deploy:dev`; add `test -n "$USER"` guards to the alchemy dev scripts as well.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The package has no test script and no test files, so the shell pipelines in package.json scripts are never exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A shell test that runs the STAGE_SUFFIX derivation against representative usernames (all-lowercase, mixed case, longer than 44 chars, characters outside [a-z0-9-]) and asserts the resulting Pages project name matches the stage name used by `deploy:dev`.
items.minimumFixScope: infra/alchemy/package.json (scripts: stage derivation and USER guard)

items.title: No test coverage for the deploy script pipelines
items.recommendation: Add a `test` script (e.g., a small Bun/shell test that executes the script pipelines with sample environment values and asserts expected stage/project names and failure modes).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test script or test files exist in the package.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that runs `web:deploy:dev`'s STAGE_SUFFIX derivation with representative usernames and asserts the output equals the stage name used by `deploy:dev` (same as the regression test for the stage-derivation finding).

items.title: Floating dependency specs ("latest" and ">=" ranges) make installs non-reproducible
items.recommendation: Pin exact versions or narrow ranges, commit the lockfile, and add a CI step that verifies `bun install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No CI or install-verification logic exists in the reviewed files.

items.title: Package entrypoint is a Hello World stub and package metadata lacks main/exports
items.recommendation: Point `module`/`exports` at the real stack entrypoint, or drop the entrypoint fields entirely if this is purely a scripts package, and remove the scaffold `console.log` side effect.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist in the package, and nothing imports the package to trigger the side effect.

items.title: loadTimestamps issues one sequential getBlock RPC call per unique block, making batch latency scale with block count
items.recommendation: Fetch timestamps in parallel or batched (viem batchRequests / multicall, or parallel Promise.all over getBlock calls with bounded concurrency), and/or persist block timestamps in a small cache table so repeated windows and backfills reuse previously fetched values instead of re-querying the RPC.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No service tests exist, and the decoder tests do not exercise RPC call patterns.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Service test with a counting fake client asserting the number of getBlock calls for a batch of N unique blocks is N (or fewer after a timestamp cache is added).

items.title: Swaps for pools initialized before the initial index window are persisted without pool linkage and the pool row is never created
items.recommendation: Ensure the pool exists before recording a swap: either upsert a minimal pool row from the Swap event (using the poolId with null/placeholder token fields) or require/validate that genesisBlock covers contract deployment and fail loudly when swaps reference unknown pools. Additionally, add a repair/backfill query that re-associates orphaned swap rows once the pool row exists.
items.reproduction: Configure a chain with no genesisBlock and no cursor, deploy the indexer more than 10,000 blocks after the v4 PoolManager contract, and run indexBatch for v4_pool_manager: the Initialize event is outside the first window, the pool is never upserted, and every swap on it is persisted with poolId=null and null token linkage.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test file only exercises the pure decoders (parseV4PoolManagerLog, toRawLog); there are no tests for persistV4, resolveStartBlock, or the pool-missing swap path, so the orphaned-swap behavior is unverified.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Service-level test with a fake PublicClient returning a Swap log for a pool whose Initialize is outside the indexed range: assert recordSwap receives poolId and token linkage once the pool later becomes known, and that a backfill over the same range repairs previously orphaned rows.

items.title: Core indexer service logic (cursor advancement, batch windowing, swapSides, orphan-pool path) has no tests
items.recommendation: Add a service-level test suite using the documented clientFactory injection point (line 38) with a deterministic fake PublicClient and an in-memory/seed D1 binding, covering: cursor resolution from DB vs genesisBlock vs head-10k fallback, cursor advancement order relative to persist failures, swapSides mapping for both signs and the zero case, and the pool-missing swap path.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing suite deliberately targets only pure side-effect-free decoders (see file header doc), so none of the service behaviors are exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Effect/vitest test driving indexBatch with a fake client: assert that a persist failure leaves the cursor unchanged, that a successful batch advances it to toBlock + 1n, and that swapSides maps (amount0>0, amount1<0) and (amount0<0, amount1>0) to the correct tokenIn/tokenOut/amountIn/amountOut.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/services/indexer.service.ts plus a new test file

items.title: Non-reproducible bun canary dist-tag in packageManager
items.recommendation: Pin the package manager to a stable exact version, e.g. "packageManager": "bun@1.4.0" (matching engines.bun), or if canary is genuinely required, pin a specific canary version/commit so resolution is deterministic. Optionally add a CI check that verifies the packageManager field matches /^bun@\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no tests for this feature (the owned file is a placeholder), and unit tests would not exercise package manager version resolution; only a CI/version-manager step would.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step asserting the packageManager field in package.json matches an exact semver (e.g. bun@<version>) rather than a dist-tag, failing on mutable tags like canary.

items.title: lint script coverage misses e2e test files and root configs
items.recommendation: Either expand the paths in scripts.lint (and lint:fix/format) to cover all project source, e.g. 'biome check src/ test/ e2e/' plus explicit root config files, or run 'biome check .' (with ignores for dist/ and node_modules) so e2e tests and configs are included. Verify the e2e test directory name in the repo before choosing paths.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and package.json script scope is not exercised by the vitest test suite; lint coverage is only observable when running the lint script against the full repo.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/package.json scripts.lint (and lint:fix, format) path arguments

items.title: lint script only checks src/, leaving package-level files outside verification
items.recommendation: Either widen the script to cover the whole package (e.g. 'biome check .') or list the extra files explicitly (e.g. 'biome check src/ package.json tsconfig.json'), and ensure the monorepo-root lint/CI job covers whatever this per-package script does not.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This feature ships no tests and script scope is a configuration property; no included test exercises which files the lint command inspects.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI check that places a file with a deliberate formatting/lint violation outside src/ (e.g. at the package root), runs 'bun run lint', and asserts a non-zero exit — proving out-of-scope files are covered.

items.title: Caret range on @biomejs/biome allows non-reproducible lint results
items.recommendation: Pin the exact Biome version (e.g. '2.5.5' without the caret) or rely strictly on a committed lockfile with 'bun install --frozen-lockfile' in CI so lint results are deterministic.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and dependency-version drift is not exercised by unit tests; it is a release-process concern.

items.title: packageManager pinned to floating 'bun@canary' tag makes builds non-reproducible and may violate the declared engines range
items.recommendation: Pin a concrete stable version, e.g. `"packageManager": "bun@1.4.x"` (or the current stable release), and keep `engines.bun` consistent with the pinned version; a floating `@canary` tag is not acceptable for a release pipeline.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no tests, and a version-pinning/reproducibility problem would not be observable from functional tests of the lint command itself; it only manifests across installs and CI runs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI check that runs the pinned package manager (e.g., `bun --version` after install) and asserts the resolved version is an exact, stable version matching the packageManager field rather than a canary build.
items.minimumFixScope: Single-line change to package.json line 40 pinning a stable bun version (and aligning line 37 if needed).

items.title: lint script does not fail on Biome warnings, so the CI lint gate can pass with outstanding diagnostics
items.recommendation: Change the script to `biome check --error-on-warnings .` (or use `biome ci .` for CI semantics) so warning-level diagnostics fail the lint gate, or explicitly configure warning severities in biome.json.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no tests; Biome's exit-code semantics are only exercised when CI runs the script, and a pass-with-warnings state produces no failure that a test would observe.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step that seeds a warning-level diagnostic in a fixture file and asserts `bun run lint` exits non-zero, or an assertion that the exact command executed contains `--error-on-warnings`/`ci`.

items.title: Aggregate `build` script fails (or silently skips) any workspace lacking a `build` script
items.recommendation: Verify every workspace package defines a `build` script (or use `--if-present` where the installed bun supports it), scope the filter to packages that actually produce artifacts, and document how `contracts:build`/`web:build` relate to the aggregate `build`. Add a CI check that runs `bun run build` and asserts all expected artifacts exist afterward.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature and script presence across workspace packages is not exercised by the vitest suite declared in package.json.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step (or a small script invoked from `test`) that asserts every workspace package under apps/*, packages/*, infra/* either defines a `build` script or is explicitly excluded, and that `bun run build` exits 0 and produces expected artifacts.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json scripts plus `build` script definitions in workspace packages.

items.title: Build toolchain pinned to `bun@canary`, making `build` non-reproducible
items.recommendation: Pin a stable, released bun version (e.g., `bun@1.2.x`) in `packageManager` and align `engines` with it; if canary is truly required, pin a specific canary build identifier.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and toolchain version pinning is an environment concern outside the vitest suite.

items.title: `format` script rewrites files in place, so any CI/release gate invoking it never fails on unformatted code and mutates the tree
items.recommendation: Split into `format` = `biome format .` (check-only, exits non-zero on diffs) and `format:fix` = `biome format --write .` (mutating), mirroring the existing `lint`/`lint:fix` pair; or keep `format` mutating but add a separate `format:check` script and use it (or `biome ci`) in CI/release gates.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and package scripts are not exercised by the vitest suite; the mutating-vs-checking behavior is only observable when the script is invoked by CI/release tooling, which is not part of the included files.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A workflow-level check that runs `biome format .` (no `--write`) against a fixture containing an unformatted file and asserts a non-zero exit code and no file modifications.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json (scripts `format`/`format:fix`) plus whatever CI config consumes the script.

items.title: `format` (and `lint`) bypass the workspace delegation used by sibling scripts, leaving non-Biome sources unformatted and generated files exposed to rewriting
items.recommendation: Decide on a single convention: either keep root-level `biome format --write .` and add explicit coverage for Solidity (e.g., a `format` script that also runs `forge fmt` in packages/contracts), or delegate via `bun run --filter '*' format` with per-workspace scripts; ensure biome.json ignores generated/artifact directories before running `--write .` repo-wide.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests or CI definitions are included, so the workspace-delegation inconsistency and the Solidity/artifact coverage gaps are not exercised anywhere.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json scripts (and per-workspace format scripts and/or biome.json ignores, depending on the chosen convention).

items.title: format and lint scripts only cover src/ and test/, omitting package-root config files
items.recommendation: Scope the format/lint scripts to the package root (e.g. `biome check --write .` with a biome.json `files.ignore` for dist/generated output) or explicitly list root-level config files so format and lint cover the whole package consistently.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover the script scope; the feature metadata lists no tests and package.json has no test entries for the format script.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step that runs biome in check mode across the package root (including config files) and fails on any unformatted file, proving the format script's scope is complete.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the path arguments of the format (and lint) scripts in apps/web/package.json to include package-root config files or the package root with proper ignores.

items.title: format script uses deprecated `biome format` command, inconsistent with `biome check`-based lint
items.recommendation: Align format with lint by using `biome check --write src/ test/` (or add a `format:check` script such as `biome check src/ test/` for CI), so formatting and linting share one command family and survive a Biome major upgrade.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no tests, and package.json contains no test entries that exercise script definitions; script behavior is only verified manually or in CI pipelines not included in this review.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A repo-level test (or CI step) that parses apps/web/package.json and asserts the format and lint scripts use the same biome subcommand family, plus a smoke check that a formatted tree passes `biome check` in dry-run mode.
items.minimumFixScope: Edit the format script in apps/web/package.json to use `biome check --write` and add a format:check script for CI.

items.title: Typecheck gate relies on tsconfig discovery and stale wrangler-generated bindings
items.recommendation: Pin the config with `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and either commit the generated bindings file and add a `pretypecheck` hook running `wrangler types`, or chain the scripts as `"typecheck": "wrangler types && tsc --noEmit"` so the gate always validates current bindings.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This feature has no linked tests, and package-script execution order/environment is not exercised by the vitest suite.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: CI smoke check: run `rm -f worker-configuration.d.ts && bun run typecheck` in a fresh checkout and assert it still succeeds, proving binding regeneration is part of the gate.

items.title: Typecheck scope may exclude test/ files that lint and format already cover
items.recommendation: Make test type coverage explicit: either include test/ in the tsconfig used by the typecheck script, or add a `tsconfig.test.json` plus a `typecheck:test` script and include both in the root `typecheck` command so the script's scope matches lint/format.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are linked to this feature, and the gap only manifests at the script/tsconfig level, outside the vitest suite.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: CI check that injects a deliberate type error into a test/ fixture, runs the typecheck command, and asserts it fails; remove the error afterwards.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/package.json scripts plus the package tsconfig include list

items.title: lint script only covers src/ and test/, excluding package config files (wrangler.toml, biome.json, vitest config, migrations)
items.recommendation: Run `biome check` without restricting to subdirectories (or explicitly include config files, e.g. `biome check src/ test/ wrangler.toml biome.json vitest.config.ts migrations/`), so config files that affect the deployed worker are linted too. Alternatively, if full-package linting is intended, use `biome check .` with appropriate `files.includes`/`files.ignore` rules in biome.json.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Package.json scripts are not executed by vitest tests; the test script (`vitest run`) never invokes the lint script, and there are no tests listed for this feature to assert script path coverage.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/package.json (extend the lint, lint:fix, and format scripts to cover config files or use a non-path-restricted biome invocation)

items.title: No automated verification that the typecheck script executes successfully
items.recommendation: Add a CI step or test that runs `bun run typecheck` on a clean tree and asserts exit code 0, so regressions in the script itself (not just in the code it checks) are caught automatically.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: feature.tests is empty and no CI configuration is included in the reviewed files; the script's own executability is currently unverified.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest test that spawns `bun run typecheck` (cwd = repo root) and asserts exit code 0 on a clean tree and non-zero when a temp file with a type error is added to the tsconfig include set.

items.title: Caret range on TypeScript 7 (native compiler) leaves typecheck behavior floating
items.recommendation: Pin the exact TypeScript version (or a tightly bounded range), verify the root tsconfig's compiler options are supported by TypeScript 7's native tsc, and lock the dependency via the lockfile so typecheck behavior is deterministic.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and nothing asserts the number or content of typecheck diagnostics, so compiler-version drift is undetectable.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step that installs with the locked typescript version, runs `bun run typecheck`, and asserts zero diagnostics.

items.title: typecheck script only typechecks the root project and may skip workspace packages
items.recommendation: Typecheck per workspace instead of (or in addition to) the root: add a `typecheck` script to each workspace package and change the root script to `bun run --filter '*' typecheck`, consistent with dev/build; alternatively use `tsc -b` with project references rooted in a tsconfig that includes every workspace. Wire the aggregate into CI as a required check.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no tests and no CI workflow is included in the reviewed file set, so nothing asserts that every workspace package is covered by the typecheck command.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest test (or CI step) that introduces a deliberate type error in a source file of a workspace package (e.g., packages/*) and asserts `bun run typecheck` exits non-zero; a companion check that the clean tree exits 0.

items.title: packageManager pinned to bun@canary undermines reproducibility of all scripts
items.recommendation: Pin packageManager to a stable bun release (e.g., `bun@1.x.y`) that satisfies the engines.bun `>=1.4.0` constraint, and reserve canary for CI jobs that explicitly test new features.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests or CI files in the reviewed set verify the resolved toolchain version or its stability.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI check that runs `bun --version` and asserts it matches the pinned packageManager version string.

items.title: typecheck script depends on tsc from an unsatisfiable peer dependency (typescript ^6)
items.recommendation: Declare typescript as a devDependency with a satisfiable, pinned range (e.g., `^5.9` or whatever stable line exists) and keep any peerDependency range only if the package genuinely exposes typescript types to consumers; then verify `bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run typecheck` succeeds in a clean checkout.
items.reproduction: Run `bun install` in infra/alchemy (or the workspace root) in an environment where no typescript@^6 version is published; install fails on peer resolution, after which `bun run typecheck` cannot resolve tsc.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This feature has no associated tests (tests: []), and the vitest suite does not exercise package.json script resolution or bun's peer-dependency auto-install, so the failure surfaces only during a real install.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step that runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` followed by `bun run typecheck` in infra/alchemy in a clean workspace, failing on any peer-resolution error or missing tsc binary.
items.minimumFixScope: infra/alchemy/package.json: move typescript into devDependencies with a satisfiable range (and correct the peer range if retained).

items.title: typecheck script does not pin a tsconfig, so tsc scope depends on ambient filesystem state
items.recommendation: Pin the project explicitly: `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json"` and ensure infra/alchemy/tsconfig.json is committed; optionally add a pre-script check that the file exists.
items.reproduction: From a checkout where infra/alchemy/tsconfig.json is absent but a root tsconfig.json exists, `bun run typecheck` compiles per the root config instead of failing or checking this package's intended settings.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are attached to this feature, and script behavior under missing/ambient tsconfig files is not exercised by the vitest suite.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI check that runs `bun run typecheck` in infra/alchemy and asserts tsc used the package-local tsconfig (e.g., by comparing `--showConfig` output against the committed tsconfig) or fails if tsconfig.json is missing.
items.minimumFixScope: infra/alchemy/package.json: add `-p tsconfig.json` to the typecheck script (and commit the tsconfig).

items.title: Typecheck types against @types/node 26 while engines allow Node 24, so the gate can pass code that crashes on the minimum supported runtime
items.recommendation: Align @types/node with the minimum declared engine (e.g. `@types/node: ^24` if Node 24 is the floor) or raise the engines minimum to Node 26; optionally add a CI job that runs typecheck on the lowest supported Node version.
items.reproduction: Add code calling a Node 26-only API (e.g. a recently added global) in apps/web source; `bun run typecheck` passes on a Node 24 environment despite engines claiming Node 24 support.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and unit tests run under the developer's local Node version, so the mismatch between the type-level Node version and the engines floor is never exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI job running `bun run typecheck` (and `bun run test`) on Node 24.x with the current @types/node 26 would not fail deterministically without a Node 26-only API usage; more directly, a script asserting `@types/node` major matches the engines minimum.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/package.json: change @types/node to the major of the engines minimum (^24) or update engines.

items.title: typecheck runs bare tsc without regenerating TanStack Router route files, so fresh-checkout CI can fail or check stale generated code
items.recommendation: Make typecheck generation-aware, e.g. `"typecheck": "tsr generate && tsc --noEmit"`, or commit generated route files and keep them in sync (for example via a pre-typecheck hook or CI step). At minimum, run the same generation step before typecheck as before build so both gates validate identical inputs.
items.reproduction: Fresh `bun install` + `bun run typecheck` in apps/web on a checkout where routeTree.gen.ts is not committed; tsc errors on missing generated module imports.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and the behavior is an artifact of script ordering plus repository generation state; vitest unit tests never execute the package scripts, so nothing exercises `tsc --noEmit` on a clean checkout.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI job (or a script-level test) that runs `bun run typecheck` on a pristine clone with generated route files removed and asserts it exits 0; this fails today and passes once `tsr generate` precedes `tsc`.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/package.json: update the typecheck script to run `tsr generate` before `tsc --noEmit`.

items.title: build emits to dist/ without cleaning the directory, risking stale bundles being treated as the artifact
items.recommendation: Remove the output directory before building (e.g., `rm -rf dist && wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir=dist`, or a `clean` script invoked before `build` in CI) so `dist/` always reflects the current source.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are linked to this feature; nothing asserts the contents or freshness of the `dist/` output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI check that runs `bun run build`, then asserts `dist/` contains exactly the expected bundle file(s) for the current entry point and no orphaned files from a previous build.

items.title: build dry-run validates only the default environment; staging/production config is never checked before release
items.recommendation: Add per-environment dry-run validation, e.g. `build:staging`/`build:production` scripts running `wrangler deploy --dry-run --env staging` and `--env production`, and have CI execute all three (default, staging, production) before tagging a release.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are linked to this feature, and vitest does not exercise package scripts or wrangler configuration validation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step that runs `bun run build` plus `wrangler deploy --dry-run --env staging` and `wrangler deploy --dry-run --env production` and asserts exit code 0 for each.

items.title: No automated coverage guards the build script's non-deploying dry-run behavior
items.recommendation: Add a CI step that runs `bun run build` and fails the pipeline if the output indicates a real deploy (e.g., assert the command exits 0 with dry-run output and that no `dist` upload/deploy step follows), or at minimum a lint-style check that the build script contains `--dry-run`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test suite is empty for this feature, and vitest only covers `src/` and `test/` per the `lint` script; package scripts are not exercised by any included test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI job that runs `bun run build` and asserts the command output contains dry-run markers and that no deploy is triggered (e.g., `wrangler deploy --dry-run` exits 0 without authentication).

items.title: packages/shared defines no test script even though it hosts the shared API contract
items.recommendation: Add a `test` script (e.g., `"test": "vitest run"`) with vitest in devDependencies, add at least smoke/round-trip tests for the exported RpcGroup and schemas, and confirm the root test command covers this workspace.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature's tests array is empty and the owned file contains no test script or test dependencies, so nothing currently exercises this package's behavior.

items.title: typecheck script depends on an implicit tsconfig.json that is not declared or visible in scope
items.recommendation: Make the config explicit and self-contained: change the script to `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and commit a packages/shared/tsconfig.json that includes src/**/*.ts with strict: true (ideally extending a shared base config). Consider `--pretty false` for CI log stability, and add a CI step that actually executes `bun run typecheck` inside packages/shared so the gate is proven to work end-to-end.

items.title: No automated verification that the build script produces a valid dist artifact
items.recommendation: Add a CI job (or a vitest test spawning the script) that runs `bun run build` and asserts the output artifact exists (`dist/index.html`, generated route tree file), so the release feature is exercised on every change.

items.title: Build script ships without type-checking (vite/esbuild transpiles without tsc)

items.title: deploy script can publish stale or missing build output (no predeploy build hook)

items.title: Version skew across @tanstack/router runtime, CLI, plugin, and devtools packages
items.recommendation: Align the four @tanstack/router packages on the same minor version (or a shared `@tanstack/router-core`-style exact version) and verify the generated route tree compiles with `tsc --noEmit` after `tsr generate`.

items.title: HTTP status mapping depends on a hardcoded literal reason string; every non-'no_pool' failure is reported as 503
items.recommendation: Carry structured error information from the service (e.g., a clientError/status field on V3QuoteError or a discriminated union) and map status from that field; treat only genuinely transient/server-side reasons as 503, and validate fee against the canonical V3 fee tiers (100/500/3000/10000) at the route boundary to reject unsupported tiers with a 400.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for the route, and the mapping behavior depends on the service's reason taxonomy which is not exercised anywhere in the included files.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that throws V3QuoteError with each known reason and asserts the expected status per reason, plus a test asserting fee values outside the canonical tier set return 400.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace the literal comparison with a structured status field on V3QuoteError and tighten the fee validation in the route.

items.title: Catch handler returns raw internal error strings to unauthenticated clients
items.recommendation: Return a fixed generic message (e.g., { error: "Quote failed", reason }) for non-V3QuoteError failures and log the detailed error server-side (console.error / observability), and ensure V3QuoteError messages are sanitized client-safe strings rather than wrapped underlying provider errors.

items.minimumFixScope: Replace String(error) in the catch handler with a constant generic message and log the original error.

items.title: Public quote endpoint fans out to an external RPC with no rate limiting or caching
items.recommendation: Add rate limiting (Cloudflare Rate Limiting binding or a Durable Object/KV-based limiter) on this route, and add a short-TTL cache keyed by (tokenIn, tokenOut, amountIn, fee, slippage) so repeated identical quotes are served without RPC fan-out; also consider a maximum URL/query length guard before BigInt parsing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for the route, and rate limiting is an operational property that the included test configuration does not exercise.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A test asserting that two consecutive identical requests only invoke the quote service once when a cache is present, and that requests beyond a configured per-IP budget receive 429.
items.minimumFixScope: Add a rate-limit binding/check at the top of the handler and a short-TTL cache layer around the service call.

items.title: No automated tests exist for GET /v3/quote despite the route being listed in the coverage config

items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that a forced service failure (mocked listPools rejection) returns a body that does not contain the underlying error message/stack.

items.title: GET /pools route has no test coverage while sibling routes are covered

Add src/routes/pools.ts to the coverage include list.
