items.recommendation: Add a route-level test suite using @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers (already configured in vitest.config.ts) exercising the /:address handler: valid checksummed address → 200, unknown address → 404, malformed address → 400, service failure → 500; also add "src/routes/tokens.ts" to the coverage include array.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this feature and the coverage configuration explicitly excludes the file from the include list.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Parametrized route test asserting status codes and body shape for: valid EIP-55 address of a listed token (200), unknown checksummed address (404), non-hex and wrong-length addresses (400), and a failing TokenListService (500).
items.minimumFixScope: Add apps/api/src/routes/tokens.test.ts and add "src/routes/tokens.ts" to the coverage include in vitest.config.ts.

items.title: 500 responses leak raw internal error text via String(err)
items.recommendation: Log the full error server-side (console.error or an Effect logger) and return a generic message such as { error: "Internal server error" } with 500; keep detailed diagnostics out of the response body.
items.reproduction: Cause TokenListService.getToken to fail (e.g., KV read error or invalid layer wiring) and observe the raw Effect error string, including internal identifiers, in the HTTP 500 body.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this route, so the error path (lines 93-95) is untested and the leak would not be caught.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Force getToken to throw and assert the 500 response body contains only a generic message and none of the internal error text.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/tokens.ts — replace String(err) with a logged, generic 500 response in both handlers.

items.title: GET /:address accepts non-EIP-55 addresses: false 404s for valid tokens (checksum not validated)
items.recommendation: Enforce EIP-55 in the :address handler: validate with viem's isAddress(address, { strict: true }) and reject non-checksummed input with 400, or normalize the input to checksum form (getAddress) before calling getToken so lowercase queries resolve to the canonical entry.
items.reproduction: GET /api/v1/tokens/<all-lowercase hex form of a token that exists in the checksummed list> → passes the shape regex at line 77, then returns 404 "Token not found" instead of 200 because the lookup key does not match the checksummed canonical entry (assuming getToken matches exactly, which is the documented storage form).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this route (feature tests list is empty), and the vitest coverage include in apps/api/vitest.config.ts (lines 67-83) omits src/routes/tokens.ts, so the address-validation path is completely unguarded.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Route test with a mocked/fake TokenListService asserting: (1) the lowercase form of a listed token returns 200 (via normalization) or 400 (if strict checksum is enforced), (2) a non-checksummed mixed-case address returns 400, (3) an unknown but checksum-valid address returns 404.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/tokens.ts — enforce EIP-55 in the :address handler or normalize input before getToken.

items.title: Catch-all 503 handler interpolates raw internal error text into the public response body and conflates data failures with outages
items.recommendation: Return a generic body (e.g., { error: 'price guard unavailable' }) for 503s, log the real error server-side (console.error), and classify data-level failures separately (e.g., 422 or 400 for tokens without a valid price) so clients can distinguish 'cannot verify' from 'service down'.
items.reproduction: GET /price-guard?token0=<valid address>&token1=<valid address>&price=1 where refreshPrice returns 0 or non-finite priceUsd for either token; observe the internal Error message echoed in the 503 body.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: apps/api/test/price-guard.test.ts imports only the pure evaluatePriceGuard function and never exercises the route handler or the catch path, so the error-interpolation and status-mapping behavior is entirely untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Route-level test that forces refreshPrice to fail (and to return a non-positive price) asserting the 503 body contains no internal error text and that the unpriced-token case maps to a distinct status (400/422) rather than 503.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/price-guard.ts lines 86-108 (error classification and sanitized response body).

items.title: GET /price-guard handler has no route-level tests; all validation and status-code branches are uncovered
items.recommendation: Add integration tests using @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers (already configured) that exercise the handler through Hono's app.request with mocked PriceService/runEffect, covering each 400 branch, the 200/422 split, the 503 path, and the maxDeviationBps default.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests only call the exported pure function directly and never construct the Hono app or issue requests, so none of the handler logic (validation, env handling, layer wiring, status mapping) executes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Parameterized route test: app.request('/price-guard?token0=...&token1=...&price=...&maxDeviationBps=...') asserting 400 for each invalid input, 200 for valid guard, 422 for deviation over threshold, and 503 when the service layer throws.

items.title: Unauthenticated endpoint accepts arbitrary token addresses and triggers two price refreshes per request with no rate limiting
items.recommendation: Add per-client rate limiting (e.g., token bucket backed by KV/Durable Object), validate tokens against a known token list before refreshing, and/or short-circuit with a cached guard result when available.
items.reproduction: Repeatedly call GET /price-guard with random valid-format token addresses; each request issues two refreshPrice calls for addresses absent from the cache.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No route-level tests exist, and the pure-function tests never touch the refresh path or the unauthenticated request surface.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Route test asserting that addresses not in the known token list return 400/404 without invoking refreshPrice (pre-refresh validation), plus a throttle test if rate limiting is added.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/price-guard.ts (token whitelist/rate-limit check before layer construction).

items.title: No tests cover the new POST /deposit-estimate route despite it being in the coverage include list
items.recommendation: Add a test file for this route (e.g. apps/api/test/routes/liquidity.test.ts) using the Cloudflare vitest pool: assert 200 responses with correct net-after-fee amounts for add_liquidity (multiple inputs) and add_liquidity_single_sided (exactly one input), and 400 responses for each rejection path, including grossAmount that overflows BigInt and token address format errors.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files exist for this route; the feature's tests list is empty and no test files were included in the review. The coverage config lists the file, but coverage configuration is not a test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: POST /deposit-estimate with { mode: 'add_liquidity', amounts: [{ grossAmount: '1000000' }] } asserting protocolFee.netAmount = 999000 (0.1% entry fee), plus 400 cases for { amounts: [] }, { amounts: 8+ entries }, single-sided with 2 entries, grossAmount 'abc', grossAmount exceeding uint256/BigInt range, and token '0x123'.
items.minimumFixScope: Add route-level tests under apps/api/test covering the handler's success and 400 paths.

items.title: Unbounded grossAmount digit strings allow CPU-exhaustion amplification and accept amounts outside the router's uint256 range
items.recommendation: Reject grossAmount strings longer than 78 digits (uint256 max) with a 400 before calling BigInt (e.g. extend the UINT_RE check with a length guard), which both bounds parse cost and enforces the on-chain amount range. Optionally add per-route rate limiting since the endpoint is unauthenticated.
items.reproduction: curl -X POST https://<worker>/api/v1/liquidity/deposit-estimate -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"amounts":[{"grossAmount":"'$(python3 -c 'print("9"*2000000)')'"}]}' — the BigInt parse of the 2M-digit string dominates request CPU time; 8 such entries amplify further.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this route, and even a naive test with a short overflow string (79+ digits) would not expose the CPU-cost dimension of unbounded lengths; the length cap would need an explicit boundary test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert 400 for grossAmount with 79 digits ('9'.repeat(79)) and confirm a 78-digit value is accepted, ensuring the digit-length cap matches uint256.
items.minimumFixScope: Add a digit-length cap (<= 78) in parseInputs before BigInt conversion.

items.title: insertTransaction writes the same (chain_id, tx_hash) key space as recordSwap but without conflict handling
items.recommendation: Add ON CONFLICT(chain_id, tx_hash) DO NOTHING (or DO UPDATE for status transitions) to insertTransaction, matching recordSwap's semantics, and document which writer owns which status.
items.reproduction: Call insertTransaction with a txHash already present in transactions (inserted via recordSwap or a prior insertTransaction call); the query throws a UNIQUE constraint error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for the module, and the collision only occurs across two different functions, which a single-function test would not exercise.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Insert the same (chain_id, tx_hash) twice via insertTransaction and assert the second call succeeds as a no-op rather than throwing.

items.title: upsertUser returns a nonce that is never persisted for existing users
items.recommendation: Persist the returned nonce on conflict, e.g. ON CONFLICT(address) DO UPDATE SET nonce = excluded.nonce, last_active_at = excluded.last_active_at, or read back the stored nonce after the upsert and return that instead of the pre-generated value.
items.reproduction: Call upsertUser('0x...') twice for the same address; the second call returns a nonce different from the value stored in the users row, and the returned value exists nowhere in the database.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature reports tests: [] and no test files are included for this module, so the insert-vs-return mismatch is never exercised; the upsert path looks correct at a glance.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test with a mocked/embedded SqlClient: call upsertUser twice for the same address and assert the nonce returned by the second call equals the nonce read back from the users table.

items.title: setIndexerCursor can regress next_block with concurrent or out-of-order indexer workers
items.recommendation: Make the update monotonic: ON CONFLICT(chain_id, indexer) DO UPDATE SET next_block = MAX(next_block, excluded.next_block), updated_at = excluded.updated_at (or add WHERE next_block < excluded.next_block to the DO UPDATE clause).
items.reproduction: setIndexerCursor(1, 'v3', 105n) followed by setIndexerCursor(1, 'v3', 103n) leaves next_block = 103.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this module (feature tests: []), and the bug only manifests with a second write after a first, which a naive single-call test would not catch.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that setIndexerCursor with a smaller nextBlock after a larger one leaves the larger value in place.

items.title: updateLiquidityPosition/updateV4LiquidityPosition silently drop updates when the position row does not exist
items.recommendation: Upsert instead of bare UPDATE (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE), or insert-on-miss when RETURNING yields no row, and return a signal that the row was created vs updated.
items.reproduction: Call updateLiquidityPosition with a tokenId that has no row in liquidity_positions; the function returns null with no error and no row created.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for the module, and the silent null return only shows up when the position row is absent, which requires a two-table setup to observe.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Call updateLiquidityPosition for a non-existent tokenId and assert either an insert happens or the function returns an explicit failure instead of a silent null.

items.title: No test coverage for the db query/schema module despite full vitest infrastructure
items.recommendation: Add unit tests using @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers with an in-memory D1 (or a mocked SqlClient) covering upsertUser, setIndexerCursor, insertTransaction vs recordSwap conflict behavior, the updateLiquidityPosition miss path, and the rowTo* converters' handling of null/0/1 values.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is the gap itself: no tests exist for this module, so every finding above is unguarded.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest suite that applies the D1 migration to an in-memory database and runs each exported query helper twice (second run exercising conflict/upsert paths) with assertions on returned and persisted state.
items.minimumFixScope: New test file under apps/api/test covering apps/api/src/db

items.title: test script hard-fails on an empty test suite (no --passWithNoTests)
items.recommendation: Add '--passWithNoTests' to the test script (or set passWithNoTests: true in the vitest config) so an empty suite is treated as a pass until tests exist. Once real tests are committed, the flag is harmless since it only affects the no-tests-found case.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no linked tests and this is a package-script behavior issue; test files, if any, would not exercise the script's exit-code behavior on an empty suite.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/api/package.json line 15: change "test": "vitest run" to "test": "vitest run --passWithNoTests"

items.title: Root `test` script silently omits the Solidity/forge contract test suite
items.recommendation: Chain both suites in the canonical script, e.g. `"test": "vitest run && bun run contracts:test"`, or if contract tests must stay separate, add a CI job that explicitly runs `contracts:test` and document the split so `test` is not treated as the complete repo-wide suite.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files are included in this feature, and the issue is in package.json script wiring, which test code cannot detect; the existence of the separate `contracts:test` script is itself evidence that the vitest `test` script does not cover the contracts package.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json scripts section (line 10, and optionally line 17)

items.title: `packageManager` pins mutable `bun@canary` tag, making installs non-reproducible
items.recommendation: Pin an exact stable version (e.g. `bun@1.4.x` satisfying `engines.bun`) or the exact version recorded in the lockfile, and install that pinned version in CI.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Toolchain version pinning is install-time metadata; no test executes against a pinned package manager, and no test files are included in this feature.

items.title: test:e2e assumes Playwright browsers are already installed with no install step in scripts
items.recommendation: Either add a `pretest:e2e`/`postinstall` step that runs `playwright install --with-deps` (or a dedicated `test:e2e:install` script wired into CI), or document the required bootstrap step.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Browser provisioning happens outside the test suite itself; unit tests cannot detect a missing browser install step.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/package.json scripts (add browser install step) or CI workflow documentation

items.title: Redundant coverage providers installed without an explicit provider in test:coverage
items.recommendation: Pick one coverage provider, remove the other from devDependencies, and pin it explicitly, e.g. `"test:coverage": "vitest run --coverage.provider=v8"` or declare `coverage.provider` in a vitest config.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is a package-script/dependency configuration concern; unit tests do not exercise script flags or devDependency resolution.

items.title: Stat component has no unit tests despite complete Vitest/Testing Library infrastructure
items.recommendation: Add apps/web/src/components/ui/Stat.test.tsx covering: label and value rendering, conditional desc rendering (absent vs present), trend class mapping for up/down/undefined, and default render without trend.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for Stat exists in the included files, and the feature metadata lists zero tests; the package.json test scripts only define how tests would run, not tests for this component.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: vitest + Testing Library test asserting container.className includes 'stat', value node class toggles between 'text-success' and 'text-error' for trend up/down and is absent otherwise, and desc is not rendered when the prop is omitted.

items.title: Stat renders label, value, and description as unlabeled sibling divs with no ARIA grouping or association
items.recommendation: Wrap the content in a container with role="group" and aria-label={label} (or use dl/dt/dd semantics), and add an aria-live region or visually-hidden trend text (e.g., aria-label including 'trending up/down') so the trend is not conveyed by color alone.
items.reproduction: Render <Stat label="TVL" value="$1.2M" trend="down" /> and inspect the accessibility tree: three bare divs with no grouping, no accessible name, and no announcement of the downward trend.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files exist for this component (feature tests list is empty), and the included code contains no accessibility assertions; only the rendering logic is exercised, if at all.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: A Testing Library test asserting the stat renders within a role="group" element with an accessible name equal to the label, and that a trend="down" stat includes a non-color-based announcement (aria-label or hidden text).

items.title: Short addresses render without mono font or full-address tooltip (inconsistent fallback branch)
items.recommendation: Use a single span that always applies `font-mono text-sm` and `title={address}`, and only vary the child text between the truncated and full value, e.g. compute `display = address.length < length * 2 + 3 ? address : `${address.slice(0, 2 + length)}…${address.slice(-length)}`` and render one span with both branches' attributes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this component (feature declares an empty tests array), so the attribute divergence between branches is unobserved.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render with a short address (e.g. "0x1234") and assert the span has classes `font-mono text-sm` and a `title` attribute equal to the full address; render with a 42-char address and assert the text equals the truncated form while `title` still holds the full value.

items.title: Unvalidated `length` prop: zero or negative values produce degenerate or expanding output
items.recommendation: Clamp or validate `length`, e.g. `const n = Math.max(1, Math.floor(length ?? 4))`, or fall back to rendering the full address when `length < 1`; add a dev-time guard if stricter behavior is desired.
items.reproduction: Render `<Address address="0xabcdef" length={-1} />` → "0…xabcdef" (longer than input); `<Address address="0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678" length={0} />` → "0x…".
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this component, and the default positive `length` path hides these edge cases from normal usage.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Parameterized test asserting that `length={0}`, `length={-1}`, and `length={2.5}` either render the full address or produce output no longer than the input and never shorter than the prefix+ellipsis+suffix structure.

items.title: Address component has no unit tests for its truncation logic
items.recommendation: Add a component test (e.g. apps/web/src/components/Address.test.tsx) covering: empty string, short string below threshold, 42-char address with default length producing "0x…5678" style output, custom `length`, and preservation of the full address in the `title` attribute.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no existing tests for this feature; this finding is precisely about that absence.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: `describe('Address')` block asserting exact rendered text for empty/short/42-char inputs, custom length, and `title` attribute presence on both branches.

items.title: Silent failure when reconnect attempts are exhausted without an error event
items.recommendation: Set an error in onclose when reconnectCountRef reaches reconnectAttempts (e.g., "connection lost, max reconnects reached"), and/or expose reconnectCount so consumers can render an exhausted-state message.
items.reproduction: Open the hook with an unreachable-but-cleanly-closing endpoint; after reconnectAttempts closes, state.error is undefined and the component shows a silent dash.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No hook or component tests exist; the exhausted-without-error path is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Hook test: with reconnectAttempts small and clean closes, assert state.error is set once attempts are exhausted; component test asserting the error UI renders.

items.title: formatPrice renders nonzero prices below 1e-8 as $0.00000000
items.recommendation: Use significant-digit formatting (e.g., toPrecision with a sensible digit count, or adaptive decimals) so small nonzero values never display as zero.
items.reproduction: formatPrice(1e-9) returns "$0.00000000".
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: formatPrice is module-private and untested (feature metadata tests: []).
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test: formatPrice(1e-9) must not return "$0.00000000" (assert it contains a nonzero digit).

items.title: Unvalidated envelope payload fields can throw: missing tokenAddress crashes the filter effect; null change24h/volume24h crash rendering
items.recommendation: Validate every field before use: `typeof payload.tokenAddress === "string"`, `typeof payload.change24h === "number"`, `typeof payload.volume24h === "number"`, treating null/undefined as absent; consider an error boundary as defense in depth.
items.reproduction: Server sends {"type":"price","data":{"tokenAddress":null,"price":1}} → TypeError in the filter effect; or sends change24h:null → render-time TypeError in formatPercent.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for the component (tests: []); malformed-frame paths are untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: RTL test feeding envelopes with missing tokenAddress and with null change24h/volume24h, asserting the component renders the fallback UI instead of throwing.

items.title: No tests for PriceTicker or its formatting helpers
items.recommendation: Add unit tests for formatPrice/formatPercent/formatVolume and RTL tests covering: envelope filtering by tokenAddress, error branch, volume toggle, placeholder rendering, and data reset on token change.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This finding is the gap itself: feature metadata lists tests: [] and no test file exists in the included files.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/src (new test file next to PriceTicker.tsx)

items.title: useWebSocket stale-reconnect race on url change: old socket's onclose schedules a reconnect to the previous URL and clobbers wsRef, leaking the live socket
items.recommendation: Prevent stale closures from reconnecting: capture a per-effect-run `active`/generation flag that cleanup flips, check it in onclose/connect, clear reconnectTimerRef at the start of each effect run, and only let onclose schedule a reconnect if the closing socket is still wsRef.current.
items.reproduction: Mount with url A and wait for open; change the URL to B; ~3-6s later the hook opens a second socket to url A while wsRef points at it; unmounting closes the A socket and leaves the B socket open until GC.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for the hook or component; this race requires a mocked WebSocket plus controlled close-event ordering and fake timers, which no included test covers.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Vitest with fake timers and a mocked WebSocket: mount the hook with url A, change url to B, then fire the old socket's close event and advance timers; assert no new WebSocket is constructed for url A and that wsRef/state reflect only url B's socket.

items.title: Stale price from the previous token remains displayed after tokenAddress/chainId change
items.recommendation: Reset the payload state whenever the subscription identity changes, e.g. add `useEffect(() => setData(null), [tokenAddress, chainId, wsUrl])` (or key the state to the token), so the ticker shows the placeholder while reconnecting and never labels an old token's price as the new one.
items.reproduction: Render PriceTicker with token A, deliver an envelope for A so a price shows, then re-render with token B without delivering any B envelope: the UI keeps showing A's price and change24h.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Feature metadata reports tests: [] and no test file was included; no component test exercises prop-change behavior.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: RTL test: render with token A, deliver A's envelope, assert price shown; rerender with token B without delivering B's envelope; assert the placeholder "—" (not A's price) is displayed.

items.title: tokenAddress and theme are interpolated into the iframe src without validation or URL encoding
items.recommendation: Validate tokenAddress as an EVM address (all mapped chains are EVM; e.g., /^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/) and encode interpolated values with encodeURIComponent, or reject invalid input by rendering an error state instead of an iframe.
items.reproduction: Render <DexScreenerChart tokenAddress="0xabc?embed=0&theme=light" /> and observe the generated src contains injected query parameters that override the component's own embed/theme params.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this component (tests array is empty), so URL construction with adversarial or malformed inputs is never exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render with tokenAddress containing '?', '#', '&', and '/' characters and assert the iframe src is either rejected (error state) or properly encoded so no parameter injection occurs.

items.title: DexScreenerChart has no unit tests despite testing-library and vitest being configured
items.recommendation: Add a unit test (e.g., apps/web/src/components/DexScreenerChart.test.tsx) covering default chainId/theme, each supported chain slug, className merging onto the wrapper, rest prop passthrough to the iframe, and the title attribute.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no tests and none are included in the review scope.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render the component and assert the iframe src equals the expected dexscreener.com URL for a known chainId/theme pair, and that the wrapper div receives the className while the iframe receives passthrough props.

items.title: Unknown chainId silently falls back to an Ethereum-scoped embed, showing potentially wrong chart data
items.recommendation: Do not silently coerce unknown chains to ethereum. Either render an explicit unsupported-chain fallback UI (e.g., a placeholder message), omit chain scoping and rely on DexScreener's own token resolution, or require the caller to only pass supported chain ids and surface a clear error/warning otherwise.
items.reproduction: Render <DexScreenerChart tokenAddress="0x..." chainId={137} /> and observe the iframe src becomes https://dexscreener.com/ethereum/0x... instead of rejecting or indicating the chain is unsupported.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no tests: the tests array is empty and no test file for this component exists, so the chainMap fallback behavior is unverified.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render the component with chainId={137} and assert the resulting iframe src does not contain "ethereum" (or that an unsupported-chain message is shown), plus a case asserting known chain ids map to the correct chain slugs.

items.title: Uncaught localStorage exceptions can crash the component and break theme toggle
items.recommendation: Wrap all localStorage access in a small safe helper (e.g., safeGetTheme()/safePersistTheme() with try/catch returning null/no-op on failure) so the UI degrades gracefully to the default theme and the toggle still updates data-theme even when persistence fails.
items.reproduction: In a sandboxed iframe or browser context where storage access throws, render the component and observe the mount effect throwing; alternatively call setItem with a throwing stub and click the button.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test harness (apps/web/test/components/ThemeToggle.test.tsx lines 8-23) replaces localStorage with a Map-backed stub that never throws, so no test exercises storage-failure behavior.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Stub localStorage.getItem to throw, render ThemeToggle, and assert rendering completes and data-theme defaults to 'aetherdex'; then stub setItem to throw and assert clicking still flips the data-theme attribute.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/web/src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx only: add try/catch around getItem/setItem (or a shared safe-storage helper).

items.title: No tests for invalid stored theme value or storage failure branches
items.recommendation: Add tests: (1) seed 'aetherdex-theme' with an invalid value like 'dark' and assert data-theme becomes 'aetherdex' without error; (2) seed with a JSON string or empty value and assert fallback; (3) a throwing-storage test as described in the storage-exception finding.
items.reproduction: None needed; this is a coverage observation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: All existing tests seed either no value or the valid 'light' value, so the else branch and the validation guard are unreached.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: mockStorage.setItem('aetherdex-theme', 'dark'); render(<ThemeToggle />); expect(document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme')).toBe('aetherdex').

items.title: Theme applied only after first paint, causing flash of default theme (FOUC) on reload
items.recommendation: Apply the stored theme before first paint: read localStorage in an inline module/script in the HTML entry (guarded by try/catch) that sets document.documentElement data-theme synchronously, and keep the component's effect as a fallback/initializer.
items.reproduction: Set 'aetherdex-theme' to 'light' in localStorage, reload the app, and observe the dark theme applied for the first frame before switching to light.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Testing-library render wraps effects in act() and flushes them synchronously, and tests assert the post-effect state (e.g., line 67), so the pre-paint gap is invisible to the current tests.
items.minimumFixScope: Add a small inline script in the app's HTML entry (or an imported module executed before React mounts) that sets data-theme from localStorage; component logic itself can stay unchanged.

items.title: Input generates a new random id via Math.random() on every render when no id prop is provided
items.recommendation: Use useId() from react (const generatedId = useId(); const inputId = id ?? generatedId) so ids are stable across renders and unique within the tree, and keep the explicit id prop override.
items.reproduction: Render <Input label="A" /> and <Input label="B" /> without ids, then re-render the parent (e.g., update controlled state); both inputs' id attributes change on each render.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares tests: [] and no test files were included; there is no coverage of id generation behavior.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render Input without an id, re-render via a state update, and assert the input's id attribute is unchanged; render two id-less Inputs and assert their ids differ.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace the Math.random() fallback in apps/web/src/components/ui/Input.tsx with useId().

items.title: Error state is not exposed to assistive technology (missing aria-invalid / aria-describedby)
items.recommendation: Set aria-invalid={error ? true : undefined} on the input and wire the error message with aria-describedby (give the error element an id derived from inputId, e.g. `${inputId}-error`). Keep the label association or drop it in favor of the describedby pattern.

items.title: No tests cover fetch failure paths (search errors, default-list errors, address 404)
items.recommendation: Add tests: fetch rejecting for /tokens; non-ok statuses; a 404 for a valid pasted address asserting 'No tokens found' and spinner cleared; and a default-list failure followed by reopen asserting the list is fetched again (retry) and eventually rendered.

items.title: Out-of-order search responses can overwrite newer results (no abort or stale-response guard)
items.recommendation: Create an AbortController per search and abort the previous request when the query changes or the component unmounts (pass signal into fetchTokens/fetchTokenByAddress), and/or track a monotonically increasing request id and ignore responses that are not from the latest query. Also clear results when the query is cleared.
items.reproduction: Type a slow query (e.g. 'W' against a throttled network), then quickly type a second query; if the first response resolves after the second, the list reverts to the first query's results. Equivalently: type 'WETH', and before the response arrives, clear the input — the stale WETH rows remain visible with an empty query.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test mock (lines 43-60) resolves fetch promises immediately and deterministically, so responses can never interleave; no test uses deferred promises or rejects a stale response.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock fetch with deferred promises per request URL; type query A, then query B; resolve B first, then A; assert results reflect B. Also: type a query, clear input before resolving, assert no rows are shown and no duplicate-key list entries appear.

items.title: liquidityDistribution heights are treated as raw percentages and silently clamped
items.recommendation: Either normalize inside the component (height = value / max * 100 with max>0 guard), or validate/throw on out-of-range values, and document the 0-100 contract on the prop (e.g., via JSDoc or a branded type).

items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render with a distribution containing values above 100 and assert bars are scaled relative to the maximum rather than all pinned at 100%.
items.minimumFixScope: Add normalization (divide by max) or a documented validation in RangeSelector.tsx.

items.recommendation: Compute the overlay geometry over the track width, e.g. left: calc(0.5rem + <pct> * (100% - 1rem)) and right: calc(0.5rem + (100 - <pct>) * (100% - 1rem)), or apply the same inset-x-2 to the overlay and keep percentages relative to the inset box.
items.reproduction: Set currentTick such that lowerTick snaps to minimum and upperTick to maximum; the highlight fills the container edge-to-edge while the thumbs stop ~8px inside each edge.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this component, and the geometry is only visible in rendered styles, which no included test asserts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render with known props and assert the overlay's style.left/right match the input's inset offset at the minimum/maximum handle positions (e.g., overlay left edge equals the input track's left edge when lower === minimum).

results.title: Bleeding-edge compiler options (es2025, stableTypeOrdering) can break typecheck on pinned TypeScript versions
results.recommendation: Verify the typescript version resolved by the lockfile supports all options used (>= the release introducing stableTypeOrdering, and es2025 target/lib); pin the dependency with a minimum version and add a CI step that runs `bun run typecheck` with the pinned version. If older TypeScript must be supported, drop stableTypeOrdering and downgrade target/lib.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature ships with no tests (tests: []), and the vitest suite does not exercise tsc option compatibility or compiler-version constraints; option-support failures surface only when typecheck runs.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step (or a small script/test) that runs `bun run typecheck` with the lockfile-pinned TypeScript and asserts exit code 0; alternatively a test that invokes the typescript API against this tsconfig and asserts no TS5023/unsupported-target diagnostics.
results.minimumFixScope: package.json (pin typescript >= required minimum) and/or tsconfig.json (remove or gate unsupported options).

results.title: No include field and broad excludes make root typecheck coverage implicit and silently partial
results.recommendation: Add an explicit include listing the source directories that must be typechecked, and either declare references to app tsconfigs or verify each app has its own typecheck script wired into the root `bun run typecheck` command so no tree is skipped silently.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this feature (tests: []), and vitest does not assert the file-list scope of the root typecheck program.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A script/test that builds the root program (e.g., via typescript API or `tsc --listFiles`) and asserts expected source dirs are covered and that each app in apps/ participates in the root typecheck (directly or via an invoked per-app config).
results.minimumFixScope: tsconfig.json: add include and references (or wire per-app typecheck into the root command).

results.title: VITE_WS_URL omitted from production secret validation loop
results.recommendation: Add VITE_WS_URL to the name list in the validation loop at line 111 so a missing/empty secret fails the deploy job before any infrastructure or Pages changes are made.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this workflow file; the inline validation loop is the only runtime guard, and it currently excludes the variable, so nothing detects the omission.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A shell test that extracts the deploy job's env block variable names (lines 70-88) and asserts every secret-sourced name appears in the validation loop's list (line 111).
results.minimumFixScope: Add `VITE_WS_URL` to the name list in .github/workflows/release.yml line 111.

results.title: Release version guard relies on a hardcoded package list that can silently drift
results.recommendation: Derive the package list from the workspace (e.g., enumerate package.json files under apps/ and packages/, or use `bun pm ls`/workspace metadata), or add a CI check that fails when a package.json exists that is not covered by the hardcoded list.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The check runs inline in the workflow and no tests are included for this feature; the drift only manifests at the moment a new package is added, with no test or automation forcing list updates.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that enumerates all package.json files under apps/ and packages/ and asserts each one appears in the version guard's file list.
results.minimumFixScope: Replace the hardcoded array in the inline Node script (lines 49-54) with a workspace-derived list, or add a drift-checking job/step.

results.title: Production web app (Pages) deployment is not smoke-tested
results.recommendation: After web:deploy:production, add a smoke check that curls the production web origin (e.g., the Pages URL or SIWE_URI) with --fail and asserts a 200 response with expected content, or verify the Pages deployment status via the Cloudflare API before the github-release job runs.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The workflow has a smoke-test step but it is limited to API endpoints; no test file is included for this feature.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A workflow step that runs `curl --fail --max-time 30 "$WEB_ORIGIN"` (with the origin derived from the deployed Pages URL or SIWE_URI) and asserts an expected HTTP status/marker after the web deploy step.
results.minimumFixScope: Extend the smoke-test step (lines 123-126) to include the web origin, or add a step between the web deploy and github-release jobs.

results.title: passWithNoTests: true can silently mask zero executed tests in CI
results.recommendation: Remove passWithNoTests from the shared config, or scope it to local development only (e.g., set it conditionally via an environment variable such as NODE_ENV !== 'production' or via a separate dev-only config override). Additionally, consider a CI assertion that the run executed at least one test (e.g., parse vitest's JSON reporter output and fail if numTotalTests === 0).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: vitest.config.ts is the test runner's own configuration; the repository has no test that executes the config and asserts how many tests the suite actually runs, so nothing guards against a silent zero-test pass.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A script or CI step that runs `vitest run --reporter=json` and fails if the reported total test count is 0, ensuring the projects entry always resolves to runnable tests.
results.minimumFixScope: Remove or conditionally disable the passWithNoTests option in vitest.config.ts.

results.title: Root dev/build scripts use --filter '*' and fail if any workspace lacks the script
results.recommendation: Ensure every workspace declares `dev` and `build` (even as no-ops), or drop the all-workspace filter and drive each app via the dedicated api:dev/web:dev scripts; add a CI check that lists workspaces and verifies script symmetry.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature; the failure happens when running the root scripts, before any vitest suite executes.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A config-validation test that enumerates workspaces and asserts each one declares the scripts referenced by root `--filter '*'` commands.
results.minimumFixScope: package.json scripts (lines 8-9) plus workspace package.json updates

results.title: packageManager pins floating bun@canary dist-tag, making installs non-reproducible
results.recommendation: Pin a concrete package manager version, e.g. `"packageManager": "bun@1.4.0"` (or a specific canary build hash if a pre-release is truly required), and enforce it in CI by verifying `bun --version` matches before `bun install`.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature; package.json toolchain pinning is not exercised by the vitest suite.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A config-validation test or CI step that reads package.json and asserts the packageManager value is an exact version (no 'canary', 'latest', or range tag).

results.title: typescript@^7.0.2 may not exist on npm or may change tsc CLI behavior
results.recommendation: Confirm `typescript@7.0.2` resolves on the registry and that `bun run typecheck` passes across all workspaces; otherwise pin a released major (e.g. 6.x/5.x) known to work with the workspace tsconfigs.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature; an install-time failure would prevent the test suite from running at all.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI smoke step running `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `bun run typecheck` to catch unresolvable or incompatible toolchain versions.

results.title: test:coverage script references a coverage provider not declared in devDependencies
results.recommendation: Add `@vitest/coverage-v8` (matching the vitest 4 major) to the root devDependencies.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and the failure occurs at script-invocation time, outside the coverage suite itself (the coverage run never starts).
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A config-validation test asserting that when a `test:coverage` script exists, a matching `@vitest/coverage-*` provider is present in devDependencies.

results.title: Hand-rolled forge coverage summary parser can silently mis-gate if the summary column layout changes
results.recommendation: Validate column semantics instead of position (e.g., match the header row '| File | % Lines | % Statements | % Branches | % Funcs |' before parsing and index by header), or compute the gate from the lcov.info report (already generated on line 204) rather than the human summary; add a unit test for the parser fed with captured forge output.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The parser is embedded in a YAML run block and is not covered by the repository's vitest/forge test suites; only real Foundry output would exercise it.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A small script/test that feeds a sample summary including the header row and a 'Total' row into the parsing logic and asserts the extracted lines/statements/functions values match expectations.
results.minimumFixScope: Harden the coverage step's parser (header validation or lcov-based computation) in .github/workflows/ci.yml.

results.title: Unpinned/never-verified third-party tooling installs (slither-analyzer, solc-select, echidna binary)
results.recommendation: Pin exact versions for pip installs (e.g., `pip3 install slither-analyzer==0.10.4 solc-select==1.0.4` or a requirements file with hashes) and pin/verify a SHA-256 digest of the echidna tarball before extraction (download, `sha256sum`, compare against a committed digest, then extract). Consider caching the installed tools so they are not re-downloaded every run.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Workflow install steps execute directly on runners; the repository's test suites (vitest/forge/playwright) do not exercise CI provisioning, so nothing validates version reproducibility or integrity.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A small smoke step or script that asserts the resolved tool versions match the pins (e.g., `slither --version`, `solc-select versions`) and that the echidna tarball digest matches a committed value.
results.minimumFixScope: Add version pins/hashes to the pip and curl install steps in .github/workflows/ci.yml.

results.title: No job-level timeouts: hung or unbounded steps can block the required ci-status gate for up to 6 hours
results.recommendation: Set timeout-minutes per job (e.g., 15-30 min for quality/backend/frontend, 45-60 min for contracts and e2e, 90-120 min for echidna) and enforce fuzzing limits via the echidna.yaml config (testLimit/timeout) as well.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Job timing is static workflow YAML and is not exercised by any test suite; there is no CI-level check that jobs declare timeouts.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A lint-style check (e.g., a small script) that parses the workflow and fails if any job lacks timeout-minutes.
results.minimumFixScope: Add timeout-minutes to each job in .github/workflows/ci.yml.

results.title: Workflow shell logic (secret validation, retry loop, smoke-test URL derivation) has no automated coverage and is not linted
results.recommendation: Add actionlint (or a YAML+shell lint step) to CI for `.github/workflows/*`, and add a unit test for the health-URL derivation covering: exact `/api/v1` suffix, trailing slash, and non-`/api/v1` base URLs. Prefer deriving the health URL from an explicit base secret or a dedicated `HEALTH_URL` rather than suffix manipulation.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The project's test command targets the TypeScript codebase; GitHub Actions YAML and inline shell blocks are outside its coverage, and no workflow-level test harness exists.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A shell test that runs the derivation expression against sample VITE_API_URL values (with and without trailing slash, with and without `/api/v1`) and asserts the expected health URL, plus an actionlint step in CI.
results.minimumFixScope: .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml — make the health URL derivation explicit/robust; optionally add actionlint to the repo's CI.

results.title: VITE_WS_URL is sourced from secrets but omitted from the Validate deployment inputs check, so a missing/empty websocket secret deploys a broken canary silently
results.recommendation: Add VITE_WS_URL to the name list in the Validate deployment inputs loop (line 61), or explicitly document it as optional and add a smoke-test assertion for it if the app can run without websockets.
results.reproduction: Delete or empty the VITE_WS_URL secret, push to main; the deploy job passes all validation and smoke tests while the deployed frontend receives an empty websocket URL.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this workflow (tests: []), and the omission is invisible to CI since the validation step only fails on variables that are listed.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A small script that parses the workflow YAML and asserts every env var whose value is `${{ secrets.* }}` appears in the Validate deployment inputs loop's name list; wire it into CI so future secret additions cannot be missed.
results.minimumFixScope: .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml — add `VITE_WS_URL` to the for-loop list at line 61.

results.title: Deploy checks out mutable `main` and verifies it against a CI-run SHA, creating a TOCTOU race that aborts deploys when main advances
results.recommendation: Check out the tested commit directly: set `ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}` on actions/checkout (keeping the Verify tested commit step as a guard, or replacing it since checkout is then exact). This removes the race window entirely while preserving the 'deploy exactly what CI tested' guarantee.
results.reproduction: Push commit A (CI completes, deploy job starts); push commit B before the deploy job's checkout step runs; `git rev-parse HEAD` returns B's SHA while TESTED_SHA is A's, so the Verify tested commit step exits non-zero and the deploy is skipped.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no tests (tests: []), and GitHub workflow_run timing races cannot be exercised by the repo's existing unit/integration suites; the behavior is only observable in production scheduling.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A workflow-level test (e.g., actionlint plus a small script) that parses the YAML and asserts the checkout `ref` is the pinned `head_sha` expression rather than a branch name, so a future change cannot silently reintroduce the moving-target checkout.
results.minimumFixScope: .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml — change the checkout step's `ref` to `${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}`.

results.title: Scheduled CodeQL runs share the concurrency group with push runs and can be cancelled mid-analysis
results.recommendation: Include the event type in the concurrency group key so schedule and push runs do not cancel each other, e.g. `group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}`, or set `cancel-in-progress: false` (or drop the concurrency block) for the schedule trigger.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no tests (tests: []), and GitHub Actions concurrency semantics cannot be exercised by the project's bun-based test/lint commands; this behavior is only observable in live workflow runs.

results.title: No CI validation covers the CodeQL workflow YAML or its referenced config file
results.recommendation: Add an actionlint (or at minimum a YAML syntax) check to the lint/test pipeline for .github/workflows and verify that the referenced ./.github/codeql-config.yml exists and is valid, so workflow breakage is caught in PR CI rather than only in live GitHub Actions runs.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are associated with this feature (tests: []), and none of the detected project commands target GitHub Actions workflow files.
results.minimumFixScope: Add a workflow-YAML lint step (e.g., actionlint) to CI and a check that ./.github/codeql-config.yml exists

results.title: No CI validation of workflow YAML/expressions; breakage surfaces only at the weekly scheduled run
results.recommendation: Add an actionlint check for .github/workflows/*.yml to CI (or extend the lint command), and configure a notification (status badge, scheduled-failure issue, or workflow dispatch fallback) so a missing weekly run is surfaced promptly.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing typecheck/lint/format/test commands are JavaScript-oriented and do not parse GitHub Actions YAML, and the workflow itself has no self-validation step.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: CI step running actionlint on .github/workflows/renovate.yml for PRs touching .github/

results.title: renovate-version container pin can silently drift from the action SHA pin
results.recommendation: Add a packageRule in renovate.json matching renovatebot/github-action with the renovateVersion option so renovate-version tracks the action version in lockstep (verify the rule exists before assuming drift is handled); otherwise document a manual bump procedure for both pins.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover synchronization between the action SHA and the renovate-version input; drift is only observable at the next scheduled run.
results.minimumFixScope: renovate.json (add renovateVersion packageRule) - outside included files, so verify current contents first

results.title: Long-lived write-scoped PAT available to scheduled job that rewrites workflow files
results.recommendation: Rotate RENOVATE_TOKEN regularly and scope it to the minimum (Contents and Pull requests write); consider dropping the Workflows write scope by disabling or narrowly constraining the github-actions manager, or use a GitHub App installation token with expiring, per-repo credentials; keep postUpgradeTasks disabled in renovate.json; treat any Renovate PR touching .github/ as high-risk and review diffs carefully.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this workflow's secret handling; this is a configuration-level security posture issue that CI tests cannot exercise without the real PAT.
results.minimumFixScope: .github/workflows/renovate.yml (and renovate.json if the github-actions manager scope is reduced)

results.title: V4 position reconcile maps ownership mismatch to 502 'Unable to read v4 position state'
results.recommendation: Use a dedicated error (or a tag on V4PositionReadError) for ownership mismatch and return 403 with the same message as the V3 path; reserve 502 for actual RPC/read failures.
results.reproduction: POST /api/v1/positions/v4/:tokenId/reconcile for a tokenId owned by another wallet returns 502 instead of 403.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No positions route tests exist in the included scope.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that reconciling a tokenId owned by a different wallet returns 403, while an RPC failure returns 502.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/positions.ts V4 reconcile handler and its error mapping.

results.title: POST /api/v1/positions records positions with no format validation (poolId, tokenId, ticks, liquidity, protocol)
results.recommendation: Add runtime validation matching sibling routes: poolId against the 64-hex poolKey pattern (or address pattern), integer ticks, liquidity as a non-negative integer string, tokenId as digits when provided, protocol within {v3,v4}; return 400 on failure.
results.reproduction: POST /api/v1/positions with body {poolId:'garbage', tickLower:1.5, tickUpper:2.5, liquidity:'abc', protocol:'v5'} returns 200 and persists the row.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No positions route tests exist in the included scope; the sole test covers only the price-guard helper.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Route test asserting malformed poolId/tick/liquidity/protocol bodies return 400 and are never passed to PositionService.

results.title: Route handlers have no test coverage — only the price-guard pure helper is tested
results.recommendation: Add route-level tests with mocked D1/RPC (the repo already depends on @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers and @effect/vitest) covering auth failures, TP/SL creation verification, reconcile ownership checks, and param validation for each route.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test deliberately targets only the exported pure function and cannot exercise handlers, middleware, or on-chain verification.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A route-level suite parameterizing each endpoint with valid/invalid inputs, asserting status codes and that services are never called on validation failures.

results.title: GET /api/v1/quote accepts unvalidated slippage (NaN/negative/unbounded) that can null out minAmountOut
results.recommendation: Validate slippage with Number.isFinite and a bounded range (e.g. 0 to 100 percent) before building the quote, returning 400 on invalid input, mirroring the v3-quote.ts validation.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only included test covers the price-guard helper; there are no swap route tests exercising query-parameter validation.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Route-level test asserting GET /quote with slippage=abc, slippage=-1, and slippage=999 each return 400 and never reach the quote service.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/swap.ts GET /quote handler — add slippage validation before getQuote.

results.title: Missing/invalid CHAIN_ID silently defaults to Sepolia in TP/SL routes and yields NaN chainId in POST /positions
results.recommendation: Use parseChainId in both files and return 500 'Invalid chain configuration' on null (or a non-safe-integer value), matching pools.ts/price-guard.ts; never fall back to a hardcoded chain.
results.reproduction: Deploy with CHAIN_ID unset: POST /api/v1/tp-sl/orders succeeds and persists the order with chainId 11155111.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No TP/SL or positions tests exist; the misconfiguration path is untested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that TP/SL and positions handlers return 500 when CHAIN_ID is missing or non-numeric, and never write a fallback chainId.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/tp-sl.ts chainIdFor and apps/api/src/routes/positions.ts POST /positions chainId computation.

results.title: POST /api/v1/swap/record accepts unverified tx hashes and amounts from any authenticated user
results.recommendation: Before inserting, fetch the transaction receipt on-chain and verify status success and that the sender matches session.userAddress (mirroring tp-sl.ts creation verification); at minimum validate txHash format and add a unique constraint on (chainId, txHash).
results.reproduction: Authenticated user POSTs /api/v1/swap/record with a random hex txHash, blockNumber 1, and amountUsd 1e9; the row is persisted without any on-chain check.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No swap route tests exist; the included test only exercises the price-guard helper.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Route test with mocked RPC: recording a txHash with no receipt (or a receipt whose sender is not the session user) must be rejected with 4xx and no row inserted.

results.title: TP/SL order id parsing via Number.parseInt accepts malformed ids and loses precision for large uint256 order ids
results.recommendation: Validate the param with /^[0-9]+$/ and keep the id as a decimal string (or BigInt) end-to-end instead of converting through Number.
results.reproduction: DELETE /api/v1/tp-sl/orders/12abc deletes order 12 instead of rejecting; an order with id 9007199254740993 resolves to 9007199254740992.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No TP/SL route tests exist; only the price-guard helper is tested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that /orders/12abc returns 400 and that an id > 2^53 round-trips through getOrder/cancelOrder without precision loss.

results.title: GET /api/v1/pools accepts unvalidated sortBy/sortDirection/filterToken query params
results.recommendation: Validate sortBy against ['tvl','volume','fees','created'], sortDirection against ['asc','desc'], and filterToken against /^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/ when provided; return 400 on violation.
results.reproduction: GET /api/v1/pools?sortBy=INJECTED returns 500 or unspecified ordering instead of 400.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No pools route tests exist in the included scope.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Route test asserting invalid sortBy/sortDirection/filterToken values return 400 and valid values pass through to the service.

results.title: No tests for the WorkerEnv tag and layer factory
results.recommendation: Add a small unit test (e.g., apps/api/src/layers/WorkerEnv.test.ts) using @effect/vitest that builds the layer and asserts the provided env is retrievable via Effect.service(WorkerEnv), and that the tag id is '@aetherdex/WorkerEnv'.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files are associated with this feature; the feature metadata lists an empty tests array and none of the included files reference a test.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: `const env = { DB: {} as D1Database, ... }; const result = await Effect.runPromise(Effect.provide(makeWorkerEnvLayer(env), Effect.service(WorkerEnv))); expect(result).toEqual(env)` plus an assertion on the tag's service id.

results.title: WorkerEnv tag uses Context.Service, an API removed in Effect 3/4; pinned effect 4.0.0-beta.100 expects Context.Tag
results.recommendation: Replace line 13 with `export const WorkerEnv = Context.Tag<WorkerEnv>("@aetherdex/WorkerEnv")` and keep the exported WorkerEnv interface; Layer.succeed on line 15 is then correct as-is.
results.reproduction: Run `bun run typecheck` in apps/api against the pinned effect version; expect TS2339 (Property 'Service' does not exist) on line 13, and a TypeError at import time under vitest or wrangler dev if the export is also missing at runtime.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this file (feature tests array is empty), and vitest's esbuild transform strips types without typechecking, so even a passing runtime test would not flag a missing/renamed Effect export; the typecheck script is the only gate and it is currently at risk.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest case that imports WorkerEnv.ts (import fails if Context.Service is undefined at runtime) and asserts WorkerEnv.serviceId (or the tag's id) equals '@aetherdex/WorkerEnv' and that Effect.provide(makeWorkerEnvLayer(env), Effect.service(WorkerEnv)) yields the same env instance.

results.title: Portfolio fetch race: aborted request's finally clears the pending state and stale cross-account positions remain visible
results.recommendation: Mirror positions.tsx: add an `active`/`cancelled` flag, guard setPositions/setIsPending in then/catch/finally with it, and clear positions when starting a new request.
results.reproduction: Start a slow /users/:address/positions request, switch wallet accounts before it resolves; the spinner disappears and the previous account's positions render until the second request completes.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The portfolio tests cover only pure helpers (getPortfolioStatus, formatPositionValue) and static render states; the fetch effect with abort semantics is untested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Component test that starts a fetch, unmounts/refetches with a pending promise, resolves the first request after abort, and asserts isPending stays true and positions are not clobbered.

results.title: Post-swap /record request is fire-and-forget: index sync failures are silent and the swap is reported as fully successful
results.recommendation: Surface record failures (retry with backoff, or show a non-blocking 'index sync pending' notice with a manual retry), and/or have the indexer reconcile from chain events as a backstop.
results.reproduction: Block the /record endpoint (or expire the auth token) and complete a swap; the page shows 'Swap Confirmed' and resets after 3 seconds, and the swap is absent from the index.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exercise the post-confirmation record flow; swap.spec.ts covers only initial page rendering.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test the confirmation effect: assert /record is called with the quote payload, and that a failed response triggers a visible retry path rather than silent swallow.

results.title: formatAmount decimal 'trim' is a no-op: slice never truncates and the 'at least 2 decimals' guarantee is not implemented
results.recommendation: Decide on the intended policy and implement it explicitly, e.g. cap fraction at 6 digits with trailing-zero trim: fracPart.replace(/0+$/, '').slice(0, 6) || '0', and pad to 2 when shorter if 'at least 2 decimals' is truly desired.
results.reproduction: Quote an amount whose formatted output has many fractional digits (e.g., 18-decimal token amounts) and observe the full un-capped fraction rendered in the 'You receive' area.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: formatAmount is module-private and the included tests never call it; swap coverage is limited to e2e rendering assertions.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test formatAmount for cases like '1500000000000000000'/18 (expect '1.5'), a tiny amount, and a zero-decimal token.

results.title: Pools filter input desynchronizes from the URL filterToken on navigation
results.recommendation: Derive the input value from Route.useSearch().filterToken (and update on navigation), or add an effect syncing search state when the URL value changes.
results.reproduction: Type a token into the filter, click the header 'Pools' link (resets filterToken to ''); the list is unfiltered but the input still shows the old token.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: pools.test.tsx tests only the PoolsResults presentational component with static props; no test mounts PoolsIndexPage with router search state.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Router-level test: navigate to /pools?filterToken=X, then to /pools, and assert the input clears to match the URL.

results.title: Stale swap quote expiry (expiresAt) is never enforced before building/signing the transaction
results.recommendation: Before calling /build (and ideally again before sendTransaction), verify quote.expiresAt * 1000 > Date.now() and abort with a 'Quote expired — refresh' error; alternatively re-fetch the quote when it is within a short window of expiry.
results.reproduction: Fetch a quote, wait longer than expiresAt, click Swap; the flow proceeds to wallet signing without any expiry warning or re-quote.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only swap tests are e2e rendering smoke tests (apps/web/test/e2e/swap.spec.ts lines 8-34) that never exercise the signing flow or quote lifecycle.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test handleSwap (or an extracted helper) with an expired quote and assert it rejects without calling /build or sendTransaction.

results.title: Pool detail page masks network/server failures as 'Pool not found' with no retry
results.recommendation: Check response.ok, distinguish HTTP/network errors from a 404 (missing pool), surface an error state with a retry button, and only render 'Pool not found.' for genuine 404s.
results.reproduction: Stop the API server and open /pools/<valid-pool-id>; the page shows 'Pool not found.' instead of an availability error.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for PoolDetailPage or its data fetching; pools.test.tsx only covers the PoolsResults list component.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render test that stubs a failed/500 fetch and asserts an error state with retry is shown rather than 'Pool not found.'

results.title: Exported money-moving validation logic (pool creation, rebalance position selection) has no unit tests
results.recommendation: Add unit tests for validatePoolCreationForm (distinct/ordered tokens, fee/tickSpacing caps, sqrtPriceX96 range, price too small to encode, past/equal deadline), buildPoolCreationTransactionIntent encoding, and selectIndexedPosition fallback semantics.
results.reproduction: Run bun --cwd apps/web run test; no test imports pools.new.tsx or positions.tsx helpers.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Coverage exists only for PoolsResults, PortfolioResults, playground lib/table, and swap rendering; the exported validators were evidently written for testability but never tested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Table-driven vitest suite over validatePoolCreationForm covering each error branch and a valid case producing a request.

results.title: listTokens accepts negative or NaN limits: unbounded result set or 500
results.recommendation: Clamp exactly like applyOptions in token-list.service.ts: const rawLimit = options?.limit; const limit = Math.min(rawLimit === undefined || !Number.isFinite(rawLimit) || rawLimit < 0 ? 100 : rawLimit, 500).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included in this feature, and observing the SQL LIMIT behavior requires a D1/SQLite-backed test that asserts row counts.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: listTokens({limit: -1}) and listTokens({limit: NaN}) must each return at most 500 rows (or the default limit), not the full table / an error.

results.title: No tests exist for either token service
results.recommendation: Add unit tests with injected SqlClient/fetcher mocks covering: limit edge cases (-1, NaN, 0, >500), upsert failure propagation, case-insensitive address lookup, chain scoping, and the full cache-fallback chain (KV hit, KV miss + fetch success, fetch failure + D1 fallback, all-miss).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist in this feature (tests: []), so there is nothing to contradict or cover the behaviors described.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest suite using @effect/vitest with mocked SqlClient and TokenListFetcher exercising each resolveTokens branch and the listTokens/getToken edge cases above.
results.minimumFixScope: New test files under apps/api/test/ for both services

results.title: D1 fallback serves arbitrary verified rows and truncates the canonical list at 500
results.recommendation: Add a source/canonical marker column (e.g., source = 'token-list') set by writeThroughD1 and filter on it in readD1Cache, and remove or raise the arbitrary 500 cap for getToken lookups (e.g., lookup by address directly from D1 instead of materializing a capped list).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included, and this path only activates when KV misses and the upstream fetch fails, so it is easy to miss in integration testing.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Seed D1 with 500+ verified rows (including a canonical row beyond the 500th by symbol order), simulate a fetch failure with empty KV, and assert getToken still finds the canonical token.

results.title: upsertToken silently swallows every write failure and reports success
results.recommendation: Do not swallow the error: expose an error channel (e.g., Effect<void, TokenWriteError>) or at minimum log the failure via Effect.logError and propagate, so HTTP callers can return 500/503. Also add is_native = excluded.is_native to the conflict update for consistency with the other columns.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no tests (tests: []), and the never error channel leaves tests nothing to assert on without injecting a failing SqlClient.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Inject a SqlClient stub whose query rejects and assert upsertToken fails (or logs) instead of resolving undefined.

results.title: getToken matches addresses case-sensitively; inconsistent with token-list service
results.recommendation: Normalize addresses on write (store lowercase) or compare case-insensitively: WHERE LOWER(address) = LOWER(${address}) AND chain_id = ${deps.chainId}; if normalizing, add a unique index on LOWER(address) to keep (chain_id, address) deduplication meaningful.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included; this requires a seeded row with checksummed casing plus a lowercase query to expose.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Insert a token with a checksummed address, call getToken with the lowercased address, and assert the token is returned.

results.title: Three of four Durable Objects (order book, websocket hub, volume alert hub) have zero test coverage; the only generic test is a placeholder
results.recommendation: Add vitest-pool-workers tests covering: WebSocket upgrade + receive of update frames, per-pool/per-token filtering, subscribe/unsubscribe persistence via attachments, and wake-after-hibernation broadcast for all three DOs (the harness already exists, per @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers in package.json and siwe-nonce-do.test.ts). Replace the placeholder index.test.ts with meaningful assertions or remove it.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is the finding itself: no such tests exist.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Per-DO test suites: connect N sockets with mixed filters, POST updates, assert only matching sockets receive frames; then simulate hibernation and repeat.

results.title: WebSocket error handlers send internal exception details to untrusted clients
results.recommendation: Send a fixed generic message (e.g. { type: 'error', message: 'Invalid message' }) to the client and console.error the full error server-side; narrow the catch to JSON.parse only.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exercise malformed-message handling on either DO.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Send a malformed frame (e.g. invalid JSON or a frame that throws in the handler) and assert the client receives a sanitized error without embedded exception text.

results.title: SiweNonceDO issue() is not atomic with consume(): a concurrent issue can have its fresh record deleted by an in-flight consume
results.recommendation: Wrap the issue() body (or at least the put/deleteAlarm/setAlarm sequence) in this.ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile so issue and consume serialize on the same lock, or run consume's block inside blockConcurrencyWhile that also covers setAlarm ordering.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: siwe-nonce-do.test.ts tests concurrent consume-only traffic (lines 5-23) and expiry paths, but no test interleaves issue() with consume().
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Fire issue() and consume() concurrently against the same named instance many times and assert every 201-issued nonce is consumable exactly once.

results.title: WebSocketHubDO knownTokens set does not survive hibernation, breaking list_pools and /stats after idle
results.recommendation: Persist knownTokens in ctx.storage (e.g. a storage set updated in the /price handler) and load it in hydrateSubscribers()/fetch, or reconstruct the token set by unioning watchedKeys from all socket attachments plus a persisted set for tokens without active subscribers.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for WebSocketHubDO; the included test files cover only nonce semantics (siwe-nonce-do.test.ts) and placeholder assertions (index.test.ts).
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that after issuing /price broadcasts, simulating instance eviction/wake, a list_pools request still returns the previously known token addresses.

results.title: OrderBookDO loses its subscriber map on hibernation; orderbook updates are silently dropped after wake
results.recommendation: Drop the in-memory map and enumerate ctx.getWebSockets() at broadcast time (as VolumeAlertHubDO does), carrying the pool filter in the socket attachment via serializeAttachment, and/or add a hydrateSubscribers() step (mirroring websocket-hub-do.ts lines 167-177) invoked at the start of fetch() and webSocketMessage(). Compute subscriber counts from getWebSockets().length for accurate stats.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test exists for OrderBookDO; the only DO tests (apps/api/test/siwe-nonce-do.test.ts) cover the nonce DO, and apps/api/test/index.test.ts is a placeholder asserting string concat and 2+2.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest-pool-workers test that accepts a WebSocket, hibernates/evicts the instance (or simulates wake on a fresh instance), POSTs /update, and asserts the still-connected socket receives the orderbook_update frame.

results.title: useWebSocket reconnect, message parsing, and url-change paths have no test coverage
results.recommendation: Add tests that fire onclose/onmessage/onerror events on MockWebSocket instances (e.g., a static helper to emit events), covering reconnect scheduling with fake timers, attempt cap, backoff values, JSON and non-JSON messages, and url-change remounts.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests assert only the happy-path open and cleanup behavior; the mock's close() never triggers onclose, so reconnect logic has zero coverage.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Emit onclose on the mock instance and assert a new WebSocket instance is created after reconnectInterval with reconnectCount incremented, and that after reconnectAttempts closes no further instances are created.

results.title: SIWE auth token persisted in localStorage, readable by any script and never expired client-side
results.recommendation: Prefer an httpOnly SameSite cookie set by the /auth/verify endpoint; otherwise store the token in sessionStorage with an expiry timestamp and validate it on read, and ensure the server enforces short-lived tokens with refresh/revocation.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file exists for useSiweAuth in the included set, and storage behavior is not asserted anywhere.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock localStorage and assert the token is not readable from localStorage when cookie mode is enabled (or that an expired stored token is treated as unauthenticated).

results.title: Stale WebSocket close event can trigger reconnect with the old URL and orphan the live socket after effect re-run
results.recommendation: Capture the socket instance in the onclose/onopen/onmessage handlers and bail out when wsRef.current !== ws; additionally use a monotonically increasing connection generation/epoch (or the effect run itself) to ignore events and reconnect timers from superseded connections, and clear reconnectTimerRef when the timer fires.
results.reproduction: Mount a component using useWebSocket with StrictMode (or change the url prop while connected); the first socket's close event fires after the remount, scheduling a reconnect to the old URL and creating a second connection that replaces wsRef.current, leaving the first new socket open and unreferenced.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: MockWebSocket.close is a vi.fn() that never dispatches an onclose event (test lines 12-19), and no test re-renders the hook with a different url while a socket is open, so the stale-close/reconnect path is never exercised; the unmount test only asserts close() was called.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render the hook, wait for open, re-render with a new url, then simulate the old instance's onclose firing afterwards; assert no additional WebSocket instance is created, wsRef still targets the new url socket, and reconnectCount is not incremented.

results.title: API_URL silently falls back to http://localhost:8080 and is baked into production builds
results.recommendation: Make the API base URL a required build-time variable (fail the build when missing in production mode) or default to a same-origin relative path, and add a CI check that the deployed bundle does not contain localhost.
