results.reproduction: Run `VITE_API_URL= bun run build` (or no env var) and deploy; the built JS contains http://localhost:8080 and all SIWE requests fail in production.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No build-time or e2e test asserts the API endpoint used in production bundles.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A build script test that runs `vite build` without VITE_API_URL and asserts the output contains no localhost URL.

results.title: Alert rules config has no tests validating threshold/severity/message invariants
results.recommendation: Add a small vitest unit test that iterates over ALERT_RULES and asserts: each rule has non-empty metric and message strings, threshold > 0, windowMinutes > 0, severity is one of "warn" | "critical", and optionally that message/percentage pairs are mutually consistent (0.01 ↔ "1%"). Also assert all rules share the same field set or that field differences (filter, ratio) are intentional.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files exist for this module; package.json's test setup (vitest run with @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers) has no test targeting monitoring config.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest test that imports ALERT_RULES and, for each rule key, asserts typeof rule.threshold === "number" && rule.threshold > 0, rule.windowMinutes > 0, rule.severity is "warn" | "critical", and rule.message.trim().length > 0.
results.minimumFixScope: Add apps/api/test/monitoring/alerts.test.ts (or equivalent) without changing alerts.ts.

results.title: AlertSeverity type is hand-maintained and can drift from severities actually used in ALERT_RULES
results.recommendation: Define a shared AlertRuleConfig interface (metric, threshold, windowMinutes, severity, message, plus optional filter/ratio) and annotate the map with it, e.g. `const ALERT_RULES = {...} satisfies Record<string, AlertRuleConfig>`. Derive the severity type from the config instead of hand-writing it, e.g. `type AlertSeverity = (typeof ALERT_RULES)[keyof typeof ALERT_RULES]["severity"]`, so any new severity value is either accepted everywhere or rejected at compile time.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no tests (tests: []), and this is a type-level contract issue that no runtime test currently exercises; the file is only covered by tsc --noEmit, which cannot detect drift between the hand-written AlertSeverity union and rule severities because both are inferred independently.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A type-level test asserting `type Severities = (typeof ALERT_RULES)[keyof typeof ALERT_RULES]["severity"]` is assignable to AlertSeverity and that every rule satisfies a common AlertRuleConfig shape (e.g., using a `satisfies` check or an expect-type assertion that each rule has metric, threshold, windowMinutes, severity, and message).

results.title: Type-unsafe casts mask a @wagmi/core v2/v3 adapter mismatch, defeating typecheck coverage
results.recommendation: Prefer depending on an @reown/appkit-adapter-wagmi version built against @wagmi/core v3 (or pin @wagmi/core to the adapter's expected major) so the casts can be removed; if the casts must stay, isolate them in one typed wrapper module with a comment and a smoke test that constructs the adapter and config.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this feature, and unit tests using happy-dom would not exercise the adapter's real runtime integration with wagmi v3; the mismatch is only detectable in a browser E2E test.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A Playwright smoke test that mounts AppKitProvider and asserts the WagmiProvider renders and `config` exposes the expected chain/account state, catching a v2/v3 runtime contract break.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/web/src/wagmi.tsx (align dependency majors or centralize the casts)

results.title: Missing VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID fails at runtime with a blank page instead of failing the build
results.recommendation: Validate the variable at build time (e.g., in vite.config.ts or a prebuild script that fails CI) and/or replace the module-scope throw with a rendered fallback screen (error boundary or a small component) so the failure is visible and diagnosable instead of a blank page.
results.reproduction: Run `vite build` without VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID set: the build succeeds. Serve the output: the page is blank and the console shows 'VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID is required...'.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature links no tests (tests: []), so the module-load throw path is never exercised; a unit test importing wagmi.tsx without the env var would crash the test runner, which is why the behavior has gone unnoticed.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that imports a non-throwing variant (or a build-time config check) asserting that a missing VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID produces a clear, controlled failure message rather than an uncaught module-scope exception.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/web/src/wagmi.tsx (move the guard into an initializer with a graceful failure path) plus optional build-time validation in the Vite config.

results.title: No tests cover app bootstrap, env validation, or wallet-provider wiring
results.recommendation: Add a render test asserting AppKitProvider/QueryClientProvider/RouterProvider mount without crashing (with VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID stubbed), and a config test asserting the queryClient defaults (staleTime 60000, refetchOnWindowFocus false) and the env-var guard behavior.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no tests, and the module-scope throw in wagmi.tsx actively discourages importing it in test setups without env setup, so the entry path is untested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest + testing-library test that stubs import.meta.env.VITE_REOWN_PROJECT_ID, renders <AppKitProvider>, and asserts the provider tree mounts and exposes a wagmi config.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/web/src (add test files; no production code change required)

results.title: Non-atomic KV read-modify-write on counters lets concurrent requests exceed the configured rate limit and delays circuit-breaker trips
results.recommendation: Serialize per-key counter updates, e.g., a Durable Object per caller/breaker used as an atomic counter, or a single DO sharded by key; alternatively detect and merge concurrent writes via the metadata timestamp. At minimum document that limits are approximate under concurrency.
results.reproduction: Set RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2 and fire 3 concurrent POSTs from the same caller bucket; observe 3x 200 (expected at most 2x 200).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: rate-limit.test.ts posts sequentially and awaits each response (lines 38-55, 58-66), so the get/put interleaving never occurs; the KV-error test (lines 113-122) covers fail-open on errors only, not the lost-update path.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: With RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2, Promise.all 3 posts against the same IP bucket and assert no more than 2 succeed.

results.title: MEV_PROTECTION_MODE=private with any non-empty PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL claims private routing that the middleware cannot provide
results.recommendation: Gate private mode on an actual relayer capability (e.g., a signing key binding or a health-checked relay client); degrade to client with a warning unless the relayer is confirmed available, and only emit the private/configured headers when submission through the relay is actually performed.
results.reproduction: Set MEV_PROTECTION_MODE=private and PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL to any non-empty string, issue a /build request, and observe X-MEV-Protection: private / X-MEV-Relay: configured with no relay submission code in the middleware.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: mev-protection.test.ts asserts the current intended behavior (headers claim private/configured when the URL is set, lines 82-92) and does not verify that any private submission occurs or that the URL is usable.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Configure MEV_PROTECTION_MODE=private with a placeholder/unreachable relay URL and assert the effective mode degrades to client (no X-MEV-Relay header) until relayer capability is confirmed.

results.title: Half-open trial admission is not exclusive: concurrent requests all pass as probes, and a failed trial can be masked by a concurrent successful trial
results.recommendation: Make trial admission single-flight and atomic: claim the probe with a short-TTL marker via a conditional/atomic KV write (or a Durable Object) and return 503 to any request observing an in-flight trial; serialize close/re-open decisions (e.g., re-read state before closeCircuit and only close if still half_open with the same openedAt) so a failed trial cannot be undone by a concurrent success.
results.reproduction: Open the circuit with 3 failing posts, sleep past cooldownSeconds, then fire N concurrent posts against a still-failing handler: all N reach the handler (expected exactly 1). Interleave one failing and one succeeding trial concurrently and observe the final state key absent (circuit closed) even though a trial failed.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: circuit-breaker.test.ts awaits each post sequentially (lines 55-97, 100-112, 149-157), so requests never interleave inside the middleware; the half-open tests exercise a single trial at a time and never a concurrent success+failure pair.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: After opening the circuit and sleeping past cooldown, Promise.all N posts against a failing handler and assert exactly 1 reaches the handler; plus a test running a failing trial and a succeeding trial concurrently and asserting the state key is still present (circuit open) afterward.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/middleware/circuit-breaker.ts — half-open admission path (lines 167-180) and close path (lines 211-213)

results.title: Swap quote expiry is never enforced: expiresAt/deadline are dead fields and the 'expired' error reason is unreachable
results.recommendation: Enforce expiry in getQuote/buildCalldata: reject quotes older than quote.expiresAt (or honor params.deadline when provided) with a SwapQuoteError('expired', ...) before building calldata, and stop minting a fresh deadline in buildCalldata — either pass the quote's expiresAt through or re-quote when the quote is stale.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests (quote-engine, chain-state-reader, position.service) never exercise swap.service; there is no test asserting that a stale quote is rejected or that buildCalldata respects expiresAt.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that buildCalldata on a quote whose expiresAt is in the past (or whose age exceeds the advertised window) fails with reason 'expired' and produces no calldata.

results.title: Phase-2 keeper/auto-recenter paths are stubs that emit plausible-but-wrong results: constant-zero counters, unreachable failure branches, and current-range values labeled as rebalance targets
results.recommendation: Either implement the stubbed paths (evaluate TP/SL with real price reads, compute and persist optimal target ranges before queueing) or explicitly mark the methods/metrics as not-implemented: return distinct 'stub' markers, throw a typed not-implemented error, or omit the counters from KeeperTickResult so consumers cannot mistake them for real zeros.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No keeper.service or auto-recenter.service tests are included, and the stub behavior is only visible by executing the full D1-backed tick path.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that tick() on a policy that passes the anti-whipsaw check reports rebalancesQueued/ordersTriggered consistent with what was actually queued (0 until implementation), or fails explicitly instead of returning zeros.

results.title: PriceService.readD1Price returns updatedAt double-converted to ms for millisecond-stored rows
results.recommendation: Return updatedAt: rowUpdatedAtMs (the same normalized value used for the freshness check) instead of row.updated_at * 1000.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No price.service tests are included, and the included tests never construct D1 rows with millisecond timestamps.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test readD1Price with a stub D1 returning updated_at = 1719715200000 (ms) and assert the returned PriceData.updatedAt equals 1719715200000; repeat with a seconds value.

results.title: KVCacheService reads parse JSON outside Effect.tryPromise: a single corrupt KV entry becomes an unhandled defect
results.recommendation: Wrap each JSON.parse in Effect.tryPromise (or Effect.try) alongside the kv.get and return Option.none on parse failure, matching the pattern in price.service.ts.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No kv.ts tests are included; the included tests never feed corrupt KV payloads to the service.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test getPrice/getSession with a KV mock returning 'not-json{' and assert the Effect succeeds with Option.none rather than dying.

results.title: SwapService.buildCalldata converts every typed failure into an Effect defect via Effect.die
results.recommendation: Remove the Effect.die catch and let buildCalldata's typed SwapQuoteError propagate (change the return type to Effect.Effect<{to,data,value}, SwapQuoteError>), or at minimum only die on unexpected (non-SwapQuoteError) errors.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No swap.service tests are included; the included tests only cover quote-engine, chain-state-reader, and position.service.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test buildCalldata with an unknown poolId resolves the failure as a typed SwapQuoteError with reason 'no_pool' (not a defect) when run via Effect.runPromise.

results.title: ChainStateReader tick scan issues up to 1025 parallel RPC readContract calls per getPoolState
results.recommendation: Lower the practical cap, make the scan size conservative by default, batch the probes (multicall3 or eth_call aggregation), or bound concurrency with a semaphore so a rate-limit failure is distinguishable and recoverable.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included chain-state-reader tests use tickScanEachSide: 1 with a mock client, so the live fan-out and rate-limit behavior are never exercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test makeStateViewReaderLayer with tickScanEachSide = 512 asserts the client receives no more than a configured concurrency bound (or fails with a typed error rather than an unhandled burst).

results.title: R2 appendToArchive is a read-modify-write with no locking: concurrent appends silently drop trade records
results.recommendation: Serialize appends per key (e.g., a per-period queue consumer with a single in-flight writer, or D1-backed append journaling), or use R2 conditional writes/ETag checks to detect concurrent modification and retry, so a lost update fails loudly instead of overwriting silently.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests for r2.ts are included, and the race only manifests with concurrent callers, which no single-threaded unit test exercises.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that two sequential appendToArchive calls on the same period preserve both batches; additionally, a test asserting the service rejects/retries when the object changed between get and put (stubbed conditional write).

results.title: simulatePriceScenarios reports feePercent validation errors under the currentPrice field key
results.recommendation: Add a dedicated error key for the fee input (e.g., extend PlaygroundField with a feePercent key, or define a separate fee error channel) so the message renders under the fee field; if the field-set limitation is intentional, document the currentPrice attachment and surface the message generically.
results.reproduction: simulatePriceScenarios({ currentPrice: 2000, lowerPrice: 1500, upperPrice: 2500, amount0: 1, amount1: 1, priceChangesPercent: [0], feePercent: -1 }) returns errors.currentPrice === 'Fee percent must be zero or positive.'.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: playground.test.ts covers invalid ranges and empty positions (lines 186-193) but never passes a negative/non-finite feePercent, so the misattributed error key is unexercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Call simulatePriceScenarios with feePercent: -1 and assert the returned errors are keyed by a feePercent-dedicated field (once added) rather than currentPrice.

results.title: Hand-written calldata ABIs are only regex-tested; ABI drift against deployed contracts would pass CI and revert on-chain
results.recommendation: Decode the produced calldata with viem decodeFunctionData against the same ABI and assert every argument value (ticks, amounts, fee, deadline, hookData/salt); add golden calldata fixtures generated from the deployed contracts' ABIs and selector-level assertions (like the existing 0xac9650d8 check) for zap and addLiquiditySingleSided.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests verify only that encodeFunctionData produced hex; they cannot detect any semantic mismatch between the locally hand-written ABI and the on-chain contract.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert decodeFunctionData(buildV4SingleSidedCall(...).calldata, AETHER_ROUTER_ABI) returns the exact args object (poolKey fields, liquidityDelta, minAmount0/minAmount1, deadline) for the fixture inputs.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/web/test/lib/v3-liquidity.test.ts and apps/web/test/lib/v4-liquidity.test.ts (plus golden fixtures from the contract ABIs).

results.title: V3 calldata builders accept non-positive deadlines while the V4 path rejects them
results.recommendation: Add a deadline > 0n validation in buildV3MintCall and buildV3SingleSidedZapCall (and, for symmetry, buildV3RebalancePlan), mirroring v4's validateInput check, or validate at the shared entry point before calldata construction.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: v3-liquidity.test.ts always passes future deadlines (2_000_000_000n and 123n); no test exercises a zero or past deadline for the v3 builders, so the divergence from the v4 path is untested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert buildV3MintCall and buildV3SingleSidedZapCall throw on deadline 0n (mirroring the existing v4 deadline rejection test coverage).

results.title: listPools and fetchTokens ignore HTTP error status (res.ok never checked)
results.recommendation: After fetch, check res.ok in listPools and fetchTokens and fail with an error that includes the HTTP status (mirroring fetchTokenByAddress), before calling res.json(). Optionally read the error body to surface the server message.
results.reproduction: Stub global fetch to resolve with new Response('<html>upstream error</html>', { status: 500 }) and run Effect.runPromise(listPools()): the rejection is a JSON parse error with no HTTP status anywhere in the message.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The suite contains no test/lib/api.test.ts at all; the only API-adjacent tests are protocol-fee tests for fetchDepositEstimate, which does check res.ok, so the inconsistent behavior in api.ts is never exercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock fetch to return a 500 with a non-JSON body; assert Effect.runPromise(listPools(...)) rejects with an error matching /HTTP 500/ (repeat for fetchTokens).

results.title: Protected RPC broadcast has no timeout or abort path; non-JSON 200 bodies throw a raw SyntaxError
results.recommendation: Wire an abort path (accept an AbortSignal and/or apply AbortSignal.timeout) and convert AbortError into a descriptive error; wrap response.json() so a malformed 200 body yields a clear 'invalid RPC response' error instead of a raw SyntaxError.
results.reproduction: Stub fetch to return a promise that never resolves; await submitProtectedRawTransaction(...) — the call hangs indefinitely with no way to abort.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: protected-submission.test.ts only covers the HTTPS rejection and a single happy-path broadcast returning a JSON result; no stalled-response, abort, or malformed-body cases are tested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Stub fetch with a never-resolving promise and assert the call rejects within a bounded timeout with a descriptive error; also stub a 200 non-JSON body and assert a descriptive parse error rather than SyntaxError.

results.title: Unauthenticated, unthrottled /api/v1/auth/nonce creates one persistent Durable Object instance per nonce — unbounded instance growth
results.recommendation: Rate-limit the nonce endpoint (mount rateLimit() or a dedicated nonce limiter) and/or replace per-nonce DO instances with a small fixed set of DOs storing records keyed by nonce, consumed under blockConcurrencyWhile — or accept the tradeoff explicitly with instance-growth monitoring.
results.reproduction: Repeatedly POST /api/v1/auth/nonce; observe a distinct DO instance created per request with no deletion mechanism (only the record expires via alarm).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests verify issue/consume semantics for a single nonce; instance-count growth over many issuances is not asserted and the resource cost is invisible in the test pool.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/auth/routes.ts (rate limit on /nonce) and/or apps/api/src/auth/siwe.ts + apps/api/src/durable-objects/siwe-nonce-do.ts (bounded nonce storage design).

results.title: Malformed or missing JSON body on POST /api/v1/auth/verify returns 500 instead of 400
results.recommendation: Wrap the body parse in try/catch (or use a Hono validation middleware) and return 400 for JSON parse failures; optionally use Hono's app.onError to distinguish HTTPException (client) from thrown errors.
results.reproduction: POST /api/v1/auth/verify with body '{invalid' (or no body); the response is 500 Internal server error rather than a 400 validation error.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: auth tests in the excerpted set exercise valid messages/signatures; the malformed-body path falls through to the global error handler and is not asserted as a 400.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: POST /api/v1/auth/verify with an invalid JSON body and assert status 400 (and no 5xx alert increment).
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/auth/routes.ts — catch the JSON parse error in the /verify handler and return 400.

results.title: Keeper advances the local nonce before receipt confirmation; a transient confirmation failure can double-execute or permanently stall an order on retry
results.recommendation: Persist submission state (nonce, txHash) before awaiting confirmation and make retries idempotent: on retry, first check on-chain order state / pending tx for the account before resubmitting; treat receipt-wait failures as 'submitted, unconfirmed' and reconcile rather than blindly retrying the submission.
results.reproduction: 1) Relay accepts eth_sendRawTransaction (tx N). 2) waitForTransactionReceipt throws (RPC timeout). 3) Queue retries sendTransaction. 4) Fresh signer: pendingNonce from public RPC = N → nonce N reused → relay rejects → order marked failed while tx N confirms. Same-instance retry: tx N+1 submitted while N pending → possible duplicate execution.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: keeper-signer.test.ts exercises single submissions and error mapping; the cross-retry interaction (private relay invisible to the public RPC's pending count, nonce advanced before confirmation) requires simulating a lost response between relay and receipt wait, which the existing test surface does not appear to cover.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test where the relay accepts a tx, waitForTransactionReceipt throws, and a subsequent sendTransaction with a fresh signer instance must not reuse the in-flight nonce (assert the second submission either skips to N+1 or is refused as duplicate before signing).
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/lib/keeper-signer.ts — move nextNonce advancement and confirmation handling behind a persisted in-flight marker, and add an on-chain/order-state idempotency check on the retry path.

results.title: Non-atomic KV read-modify-write in rate limiter and circuit breaker lets concurrent requests bypass limits and lose failure counts
results.recommendation: Move counters to a Durable Object (per-caller or per-breaker) with blockConcurrencyWhile for atomic increments, or accept and document the approximate enforcement; for the breaker, at minimum re-read the state/count immediately before opening and treat half-open admission under a single-flight guard.
results.reproduction: Fire N concurrent POSTs to a rate-limited route with max=1 and a fresh KV counter: all N pass because each reads count 0 and writes 1. Similarly, trigger 10 concurrent 5xx responses with failureThreshold=5: the stored count ends up well below 5 and the circuit does not open.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests (circuit-breaker.test.ts, mev-protection.test.ts, etc.) exercise sequential requests; reproducing the lost-update race requires concurrent interleaving, which the KV-backed design makes non-deterministic.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Promise.all of N concurrent consumeRateLimit(kv, key, {max:1}) calls asserting exactly one is allowed (currently fails); for the breaker, N concurrent recordFailure calls with threshold 5 asserting the circuit opens exactly once.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts and apps/api/src/middleware/circuit-breaker.ts — replace KV counter increments with an atomic primitive (DO) or document the race and cap burst exposure.

results.title: OrderBookDO broadcasts to an empty in-memory subscriber map after hibernation, silently dropping live order book updates
results.recommendation: Mirror the WebSocketHubDO pattern: enumerate ctx.getWebSockets() in broadcast() (and hydrate the subscribers map on wake), or drop the in-memory map entirely and serialize the subscription state in the socket attachment, filtering per-socket by the poolId tag/attachment.
results.reproduction: 1) Connect a WebSocket to /ws/orderbook/:poolId; receive the initial snapshot. 2) Let the DO idle long enough to be evicted (hibernation). 3) POST an /update to the DO (queue consumer path). 4) The client receives no orderbook_update even though the handler returns { ok: true, subscribers: 0 }.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included/excerpted tests were omitted from the review context, and unit tests in the vitest workers pool exercise fetch()/webSocketMessage() within a single instance lifetime; they cannot reproduce workerd's eviction-and-wake cycle that destroys the in-memory map.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A pool-workers test that (1) upgrades a socket on the DO, (2) simulates eviction by clearing instance memory (or asserts broadcast delivery derives from ctx.getWebSockets() rather than the in-memory Map), and (3) POSTs /update and asserts the socket receives orderbook_update with delivered == 1.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/durable-objects/order-book-do.ts only — make broadcast() enumerate ctx.getWebSockets() (and hydrate the map like WebSocketHubDO.hydrateSubscribers).

results.title: bun run typecheck excludes test/ and vitest.config.ts, so type errors in tests and the test harness go undetected
results.recommendation: Add "test/**/*" and "vitest.config.ts" to tsconfig include (with a separate tsconfig.test.json if DOM/worker types conflict), so `bun run typecheck` covers the whole package.
results.reproduction: Introduce a type error in any apps/api/test/*.ts file; `bun run typecheck` exits 0 and `bun run test` still runs (esbuild strips types).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is a gap in the verification tooling itself; no test can detect that tests are not type-checked.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/tsconfig.json — extend include to test/**/* and vitest.config.ts (and package.json typecheck script if a dedicated tsconfig is needed).

results.title: cancelOrder/executeOrder/expireOrder report OrderNotFoundError when the row exists but is not pending
results.recommendation: Distinguish the two cases: check existence first (or use RETURNING) and return a distinct state-conflict error when the order exists but is not pending; at minimum document that OrderNotFoundError covers non-pending states.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for tp-sl.service.ts is included in this feature, so the error semantics of the status transitions are unverified.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Seed an executed order, call executeOrder again, and assert a state-conflict error is returned rather than OrderNotFoundError.

results.title: Indexer fetches block timestamps with one sequential RPC call per unique block
results.recommendation: Fetch timestamps for all unique blocks concurrently (e.g., Promise.all over the unique block numbers) or batch the lookups, preserving a bounded concurrency limit.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover only log parsing and the reducer; the indexer's RPC fetching path is not under test.

results.title: V3QuoteService never verifies the RPC chain, unlike every other chain-bound reader in this feature
results.recommendation: Add chainId to V3QuoteServiceDeps and verify it (with caching) before quoting, mirroring the pattern in v4-position-reader.service.ts.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for v3-quote.service.ts is included in this feature, and the chain check is absent, so nothing asserts it.

results.title: Collect event ABI marks recipient as indexed, so real NonfungiblePositionManager Collect logs fail to decode and are silently dropped
results.recommendation: Change the Collect entry in POSITION_MANAGER_ABI so recipient is `indexed: false` (matching the deployed contract), and add a fixture decoding a real Collect log (topics = signature + tokenId, recipient/amount0/amount1 in data).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: v3-liquidity-events.test.ts only tests IncreaseLiquidity and pool Mint events; there is no Collect fixture, and any test built from this same (wrong) ABI would encode the bug into the fixture and pass.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Encode a Collect log with the canonical ABI (only tokenId indexed) and assert parseV3LiquidityLog returns eventType 'collect' with the correct recipient, amount0, and amount1.

results.title: executeOrder and recordKeeperExecution are separate non-transactional writes; keeper audit records can be lost or orphaned
results.recommendation: Wrap both writes in a single transaction (e.g., a CTE or transaction block that updates the order and inserts the keeper execution), and/or make executeOrder idempotent so a retry with the same txHash can backfill the record.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for tp-sl.service.ts, and the interplay between executeOrder and recordKeeperExecution is not exercised anywhere in the included tests.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: With a stubbed SqlClient that fails the second statement, assert the order status and keeper record stay consistent (both committed or both rolled back), and assert retry behavior with the same txHash.

results.title: verifyTrigger hardcodes TWAP to null and returns isTriggered as dualTriggerMet, so it always returns false
results.recommendation: Either implement the AetherHook TWAP read, or fail the effect with a VerificationError when TWAP is unavailable instead of returning a successful always-false verdict; surface errors[] to callers and stop computing an isTriggered result that is unconditionally overridden.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for verification.service.ts is included in this feature, and the placeholder is self-documented as a TODO, so no test asserts actual trigger behavior.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test verifyTrigger with a stubbed ChainStateReader asserting that when TWAP is unavailable the effect fails (or errors[] is non-empty) rather than returning isTriggered: false.

results.title: Volume-alert cooldown is a check-then-act race that can emit duplicate alerts
results.recommendation: Accept and document the duplicate risk, or make the guard atomic — e.g., use an insert with a unique constraint keyed on (chainId, poolId, window) in D1, or deduplicate by envelope identity in the hub.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for volume-alerts.service.ts is included in this feature, and the race only manifests with concurrent tick invocations, which the included tests never exercise.

results.title: TP/SL order lifecycle service has no tests covering status transitions and error semantics
results.recommendation: Add a vitest suite for tp-sl.service.ts using @effect/sql-d1 against an in-memory/seeded D1 covering create/get/list, every status transition including double-transition errors, and keeper execution recording.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for tp-sl.service.ts is included in the feature; existing tests cover only v3-liquidity-events and v3-position-reducer.

results.title: Integer-only fields typed as Schema.Number accept fractional values
results.recommendation: Use Schema.Int (or more specific refinements like Schema.NonNegativeInt / Schema.PositiveInt) for fee, tickSpacing, currentTick, chainId, decimals, and count fields.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no tests for the schemas, so the absence of integrality enforcement is unobserved.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest test asserting that decoding { fee: 3000.5, ... } with PoolSchema fails with a parse error while { fee: 3000 } succeeds.

results.title: No tests or test script for the shared API-contract package
results.recommendation: Add a `test` script (e.g. `vitest run`) plus a vitest devDependency, and add unit tests that encode/decode each schema against representative fixtures and assert decode failures for malformed payloads.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist anywhere in the package (no test script, no test files, no test devDependency), so there is nothing covering the schema contracts.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest test that decodes a full Pool fixture through PoolSchema and asserts the result matches the input, plus negative cases asserting failure for a missing field and a non-string sqrtPriceX96.
results.minimumFixScope: packages/shared/package.json (scripts + devDependencies) and a new test file under packages/shared/src/__tests__/

results.title: Shared contract built on exact-pinned beta and unstable API surface
results.recommendation: Track effect releases deliberately (upgrade in a dedicated commit, run full-workspace typecheck and decode smoke tests), and consider moving to stable Effect APIs once available; at minimum add a smoke test that constructs the RPC group and round-trips a payload to catch upstream churn.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist, so upstream beta API changes would only surface via typecheck of downstream packages at upgrade time.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A smoke test that builds PoolsRpcGroup and round-trips a ListPools payload through the RPC schema encoders/decoders.

results.title: Package exports raw TypeScript source with no build step
results.recommendation: Either keep private:true and document the workspace-only TS-source contract explicitly, or add a build step that emits dist/ with proper exports/types conditions (with a files allowlist) before any publication is considered.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is a packaging/tooling hazard not exercised by the current lint/typecheck scripts, and there are no tests or CI packaging steps in the package.

results.title: README/AGENTS.md toolchain claims contradict package.json (TypeScript, Biome, Vitest versions)
results.recommendation: Update README.md and AGENTS.md version inventories to match package.json (or pin the rc/native-preview toolchain if that is the intended state), and keep a single source of truth for toolchain versions.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Documentation drift is not exercised by tests.

results.title: Root typecheck excludes apps/** so the documented typecheck gate does not validate application code
results.recommendation: Compose per-workspace typecheck into the root script (e.g., `typecheck`: `bun run --filter '*' typecheck` with per-app typecheck scripts, or explicit `tsc -p apps/web` / `tsc -p apps/api` invocations), or wire tsconfig project references so the root gate covers all workspaces.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Typechecking is a build-time gate, not covered by unit tests; the gap only manifests as uncaught type errors in workspace code.

results.title: test:coverage depends on an undeclared @vitest/coverage-v8 provider
results.recommendation: Add @vitest/coverage-v8 (matching the vitest major version) to devDependencies and, when threshold enforcement is intended, configure coverage.thresholds per project in vitest.config.ts.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test exercises the npm scripts; the failure manifests only when a developer or CI runs `bun run test:coverage`.

results.title: packageManager pinned to floating bun@canary tag — non-reproducible toolchain
results.recommendation: Pin an exact build (e.g., bun@1.4.x-canary.<build> or a released version) in packageManager, and record the resolved `bun --version` output in tooling/scripts/VERSIONS.md as AGENTS.md already intends, ideally with a CI check that the installed Bun matches the recorded version.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Toolchain reproducibility is not exercised by unit tests; nothing in the test suite verifies the resolved Bun version.

results.title: Root vitest config only runs apps/web tests; documented 'all workspaces' test command silently skips the backend
results.recommendation: List every test-bearing workspace in vitest.config.ts projects (e.g., projects: ["./apps/web", "./apps/api"] or a glob), and drop passWithNoTests (or set it per-project) so empty/missing suites fail loudly. Add a root project or CI step that asserts the expected projects are configured.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The misconfiguration causes the test command to skip suites while still succeeding, so no failing test can surface it — the gap is in the runner configuration itself, not in any test body.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A small root vitest project that imports the vitest config and asserts every workspace directory containing a vitest config (or test files) — at minimum apps/api — appears in the projects list.

results.title: MEV private relay accepts cleartext http URLs in safety-config, contradicting the https-only policy enforced in keeper-signer
results.recommendation: Reuse the same https-only parsing as keeper-signer (new URL + protocol === "https:" check) in readMevProtectionConfig, requiring a valid host, and add unit tests for safety-config.ts covering http, ws, bare 'http://', and malformed values.
results.reproduction: readMevProtectionConfig({ PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL: "http://relay.example" }) returns privateRelayUrl = "http://relay.example", whereas readKeeperSignerConfig with the same env value yields privateRelayUrl = null.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: keeper-signer.test.ts (lines 82-89) tests parseRelayUrl's https enforcement, but there is no test file for safety-config.ts at all, so the lenient http-accepting regex in readMevProtectionConfig is untested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: expect(readMevProtectionConfig({ PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL: "http://relay.example" }).privateRelayUrl).toBeNull(); expect(readMevProtectionConfig({ PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL: "http://" }).privateRelayUrl).toBeNull(); expect(readMevProtectionConfig({ PRIVATE_TX_RELAY_URL: "https://relay.example" }).privateRelayUrl).toBe("https://relay.example")

results.title: Keeper nonce tracking is per-signer-instance: a transient failure after private-relay acceptance can reuse a nonce and permanently fail the order
results.recommendation: Make nonce state durable (persist nextNonce in KV/D1 keyed by keeper address, or have the relay/submission path acknowledge the accepted nonce) and treat post-acceptance failures as ambiguous: before retrying with a fresh signer, query the relay/RPC for the transaction by hash or advance the nonce from durable state instead of re-deriving it from the public pending count.
results.reproduction: 1) Signer A submits via private relay; relay accepts and returns a valid hash. 2) waitForTransactionReceipt throws (RPC timeout) → KeeperRpcError. 3) Queue retries with a freshly constructed signer B. 4) preflight reads pending nonce from the public RPC (does not include the private tx) → same nonce N. 5) Relay rejects with nonce-too-low (non-retryable) → submission fails permanently.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: keeper-signer.test.ts line 422-443 ('serializes concurrent submissions and allocates distinct pending nonces') exercises only concurrent calls on one signer instance where nextNonce is shared; no test simulates a retry with a new signer instance after a transient failure post-acceptance.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Create signer A, submit with mocked waitForTransactionReceipt rejecting; then create signer B with the same config and a chain stub whose getTransactionCount still returns 7; assert the second submission does not reuse nonce 7 (either via a nonce store or an explicit duplicate-nonce guard).
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/lib/keeper-signer.ts (durable nonce state or ambiguity-aware retry) + regression test

results.title: Public submission signs transactions without an explicit chainId (chain: null), losing EIP-155 replay protection
results.recommendation: Create the wallet client with the configured chain (e.g. define a viem chain with the keeper's chainId) or pass chainId explicitly in the sendTransaction call so the signature includes EIP-155 chainId, mirroring the private-relay path (line 456).
results.reproduction: With KEEPER_ALLOW_PUBLIC_SUBMISSION=true on an EIP-155 chain, walletClient.sendTransaction is called with chain: null and no chainId; the resulting legacy signature omits the EIP-155 chainId.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The public-submission tests (keeper-signer.test.ts lines 384-443) use a stubbed walletClient that returns a hash without performing real signing, and assert only that chain: null is passed; no test verifies the chainId embedded in the signed transaction.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Use a real local account with the public path against a stubbed transport capturing the serialized transaction and assert the raw tx contains the EIP-155 chainId (e.g. re-derive the v value / inspect the serialized fields for the configured chain).
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/lib/keeper-signer.ts (supply chainId in public submission) + signing-level regression test

results.title: Unauthenticated /nonce endpoint creates one Durable Object per request with no rate limiting
results.recommendation: Add per-client/IP rate limiting (e.g., a KV- or DO-based token bucket) on POST /nonce and /verify, and/or cap outstanding nonces per client; alternatively use a single DO that stores nonces keyed by name instead of one DO per nonce.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this source group, and rate-limit behavior would require the DO implementation, which is not included in this feature's files.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that issues N nonce requests from the same client and asserts the client is throttled after a configured limit (or that a bounded number of DO instances are created).
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/auth/routes.ts and/or the siwe-nonce Durable Object

results.title: No tests exist for the authentication flow (session validation, SIWE verify, nonce consumption)
results.recommendation: Add vitest/cloudflare-pool-workers tests covering: happy-path verify → session readable via /me; reusing the same nonce twice fails; expired session JSON is rejected and deleted from KV; wrong chainId/domain/uri in message fails; malformed session JSON falls through to 401 on requireAuth; logout deletes the session so /me then returns 401.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files exist for this source group (tests: [] in feature metadata); the vitest infrastructure is configured in apps/api/package.json but nothing covers apps/api/src/auth.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: verifyAndCreateSession: issue nonce, verify with valid signature, assert second verify with the same (message, signature) fails with invalid/expired nonce; authMiddleware: write a session with expiresAt in the past into KV and assert requireAuth returns 401 and the KV key is removed.

results.title: /verify collapses all failures, including server-side errors, into a 401 Authentication failed response
results.recommendation: Distinguish failure classes: map Effect.fail from verification logic to 401, but map thrown/unexpected errors (KV, DO, JSON parsing) to 500 with a generic server-error message and log the underlying error; do not expose String(err) internals to clients.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this source group; the error-classification behavior is untested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock KVCacheService.putSession to throw and assert POST /verify returns 500 (not 401); assert an invalid signature returns 401.

results.title: Inconsistent handling of invalid sessions in authMiddleware: malformed JSON is never deleted and kv.delete is unguarded
results.recommendation: Delete the session key in the catch block as well (best-effort, wrapped in try/catch), and wrap the validation-failure kv.delete in try/catch so middleware failures never 500 the request.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this source group, and malformed-session cleanup is an edge path unlikely to be exercised manually.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Insert a session key with invalid JSON into KV, make a request with that Bearer token, and assert the middleware passes through and the key is deleted.

results.title: fetchTokenPrice ignores the chain id and hardcodes the Ethereum CoinGecko endpoint; price KV keys are chain-agnostic
results.recommendation: Map CHAIN_ID to the CoinGecko platform (e.g., 'ethereum', 'base', 'arbitrum-one') and namespace KV keys by chain, or restrict price refresh to the configured chain explicitly.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover fetchTokenPrice or KV key scoping.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test fetchTokenPrice with a non-Ethereum chain id asserting the correct platform in the request URL, and that price keys include the chain.

results.title: No test coverage for cron and queue handlers; index.test.ts is a placeholder
results.recommendation: Add unit tests for the trigger-condition matrix (take_profit/stop_loss × zeroForOne × spot/TWAP), toScaledBigInt, keeper tick enqueue/expire behavior, and handler skip paths; replace the placeholder index.test.ts.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The listed tests only cover v3-indexer-cursor helpers; no test imports cron-handler or queue-handler.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Parameterized tests over the four trigger branches asserting isTriggered, plus a keeper-tick test with mocked D1 asserting enqueue and expiry side effects.

results.title: Price-refresh consumer performs unbounded sequential HTTP fetches with no timeout
results.recommendation: Add an AbortSignal timeout to fetchTokenPrice, cap per-message token count, and/or process tokens with bounded concurrency (e.g., batches of 5-10).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover handlePriceRefresh or fetchTokenPrice.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock a hanging fetch and assert fetchTokenPrice aborts within a bounded time and handlePriceRefresh continues to the next token.

results.title: Unguarded JSON.parse of KV payload aborts the entire pool refresh
results.recommendation: Wrap the JSON.parse per address (or per batch) so a corrupt entry degrades to null for that token only, matching the per-pool try/catch already used in the write loop.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover refreshTopPools behavior with malformed cache entries.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Seed one corrupt `price:` KV value among valid ones and assert the remaining pools still receive poolSpot writes.

results.title: TP/SL and auto-recenter evaluation depends on `poolSpot` cache entries that are only written for the top 50 pools by TVL
results.recommendation: Compute/store pool spot prices for all pools referenced by active orders/policies (e.g., backfill poolSpot for pools with pending tp_sl_orders or active position_policies), or fall back to an on-chain spot read in the evaluation handlers.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exercise the poolSpot lifecycle or the skip paths in handleTpSlEvaluate.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Seed a pending order for a pool ranked outside the top 50 by TVL, run the refresh + evaluate flow, and assert the order is evaluated rather than skipped.

results.title: Inconsistent silent chain-id fallbacks: keeper tick defaults to 11155111 and price enqueue to 1 when CHAIN_ID is invalid
results.recommendation: Use `parseChainId` consistently in all ticks and skip (log) on invalid CHAIN_ID instead of falling back to a hardcoded chain.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover cron-handler tick behavior with invalid CHAIN_ID.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Call runKeeperTick and enqueuePriceRefresh with CHAIN_ID='not-a-chain' and assert no queries/enqueues occur.

results.title: Auto-recenter never triggers: poolSpot cache payload never contains the `tick` field the handler requires, and the handler queues no rebalance action
results.recommendation: Either write `tick` into the poolSpot payload in `refreshTopPools` (or a dedicated pool-state writer), or derive the tick from the stored 1e18 price in `handleAutoRecenterCheck` as its own comment suggests; and actually dispatch the rebalance work (queue message or direct call) instead of only logging/updating counters.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for `refreshTopPools` or `handleAutoRecenterCheck`; the only worker test (v3-indexer-cursor.test.ts) covers cursor helpers, and index.test.ts is a placeholder.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Integration test: run `handleAutoRecenterCheck` against a poolSpot KV entry produced by `refreshTopPools` with an out-of-range tick and assert a rebalance is enqueued; also assert the poolSpot payload contains the tick field.

results.title: Input generates non-deterministic DOM ids with Math.random() instead of useId()
results.recommendation: Replace Math.random() with React's useId() (const inputId = id ?? useId()), which is stable across hydration and collision-free.
results.reproduction: Render <Input label="X" /> twice without an id; the id attributes differ between renders, and a hydrated/prerendered page would mismatch the client-generated id.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included test imports or renders Input, so id generation behavior is entirely untested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render <Input label="x" />, re-render, and assert the id attribute is stable across renders; also assert the label's htmlFor matches the input's id.

results.title: Card accepts variant="bordered" but never implements it
results.recommendation: Either remove "bordered" from the variant union, or implement it (e.g., treat it as forcing the border regardless of the `bordered` prop). Also consider whether `bordered` defaulting to true while "default" is the default variant is intentional.
results.reproduction: Render <Card variant="bordered" bordered={false}> — no border class is emitted despite the variant name; render <Card variant="bordered"> — identical markup to <Card variant="default">.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only test file for this feature (apps/web/test/index.test.ts) never imports or renders any component from this source group, so the dead variant is never exercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A component test asserting that <Card variant="bordered" bordered={false}> still renders the border classes (if the variant is kept), or a type-level test asserting the variant union no longer contains "bordered" (if removed).

results.title: Feature's only test never imports or exercises any owned component
results.recommendation: Add component tests under apps/web/test that import from the ui barrel and render Button, Card, Input, and Stat (e.g., with @testing-library/react, which is already in devDependencies), covering loading disables the button, variant/className composition, and label/input id association. Ensure a vitest environment (happy-dom) is configured for DOM assertions.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test deliberately avoids the components — it is a smoke test of the test harness itself, not of the feature.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test file that renders each component via @testing-library/react and asserts: Button with loading disables the button and shows the spinner; Card variant="compact" emits card-compact; Input without id matches label htmlFor to input id; Stat trend="down" emits text-error.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/web/test (new test file) plus confirming vitest environment config

results.title: Button applies daisyUI loading state twice (btn loading class plus a second spinner span)
results.recommendation: Pick one mechanism: either keep the `loading` class on the button (and drop the inner span, letting the `btn loading` modifier render the spinner) or drop the class and keep the span. Also consider aria-busy for accessibility.
results.reproduction: Render <Button loading> with daisyUI styles applied; two spinner indicators appear inside the button.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test imports or renders Button, and the smoke test asserts only vitest globals and window/document existence.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render <Button loading> and assert exactly one element with the daisyUI loading spinner classes is present.

results.title: Button propagates className via rest spread after attribute composition, allowing callers to silently clobber styling
results.recommendation: No change required; pattern is idiomatic.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: N/A

results.title: Selected-token logo renders without the image-host allowlist used in the results list
results.recommendation: Render the selected-token logo only when isSafeImageUrl(token.logoURI) is true, mirroring TokenListItem, and apply the same guard in TokenChip.tsx. Consider centralizing logo rendering in a single shared component.
results.reproduction: Mock /tokens to return a token with logoURI 'https://evil.example/pixel.png'; open the picker (placeholder shows, no img), select the token, and observe an in the button.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: TokenSearch.test.tsx fixtures all use logoUrl: null, so no test exercises a logoURI value, let alone one from a disallowed host.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Select a token whose logoURI is 'https://untrusted.example/x.png' and assert the button contains no img element (and that a disallowed-host token still renders the symbol text).

results.title: PriceTicker crashes on WebSocket frames without tokenAddress
results.recommendation: Add a typeof payload.tokenAddress === 'string' condition to the existing guard (or use optional chaining: payload.tokenAddress?.toLowerCase() === tokenAddress.toLowerCase()) before setData.
results.reproduction: Feed the useWebSocket hook an envelope of the form { type: 'price', data: { price: 1.23 } } (no tokenAddress) and observe an uncaught TypeError in the effect.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no PriceTicker tests in the included test files, and the useWebSocket hook is not stubbed anywhere, so the frame-filtering path is entirely untested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render PriceTicker with a mocked useWebSocket that first emits { type:'price', data:{ price: 1 } } (no tokenAddress) and assert the component does not throw and keeps showing the placeholder price.

results.title: ThemeToggle reads/writes localStorage unguarded and applies stored theme only after first paint
results.recommendation: Read the stored theme synchronously in the useState initializer (with try/catch around getItem) and apply the data-theme attribute in the same render, or use useLayoutEffect; wrap both getItem and setItem in try/catch with a sensible fallback so storage failures degrade gracefully instead of crashing.
results.reproduction: Set localStorage['aetherdex-theme']='light', reload the page: first paint is 'aetherdex' before flipping to 'light'. Alternatively, make localStorage.getItem throw and observe the effect error propagate.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: ThemeToggle.test.tsx stubs localStorage with a permissive Map-based mock (lines 8-23) and asserts post-mount behavior only; it never simulates storage throwing and cannot observe pre-effect paint.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test where the localStorage mock's getItem throws, asserting the component still renders with data-theme='aetherdex'; plus a test asserting data-theme equals the stored value on the very first render (initializer-based, no effect).

results.title: Stale in-flight search responses can overwrite newer TokenSearch results
results.recommendation: Guard searchTokens with a request sequence number or AbortController: capture a monotonically increasing request id (or abort the previous fetch) before each call, and ignore setResults/setIsSearching from any response whose id is not the latest. The cleanup in the debounce effect should also invalidate the in-flight request.
results.reproduction: Mock fetch with manually resolved deferred promises: type 'US' (slow request), then type 'USD' (fast request), then resolve the 'US' promise after the 'USD' promise; the list shows tokens matching 'US' while the input says 'USD'.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: TokenSearch.test.tsx mocks fetch as an instant resolver and types queries sequentially; no test simulates overlapping in-flight requests with out-of-order resolution, so the race is never exercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that returns manually-controlled deferred promises from the fetch mock, types 'US' then 'USD', resolves the 'US' request after 'USD', and asserts the rendered list matches 'USD' and the spinner state reflects the newest request.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/web/src/components/TokenSearch.tsx (searchTokens and the debounce effect only)

results.title: Address truncation is wrong when length is 0
results.recommendation: Guard the truncation branch: only truncate when length > 0 (or when the computed result is shorter than the original), e.g., if (length <= 0 || address.length < length * 2 + 3) return the full address.
results.reproduction: Render <Address address={'0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678'} length={0} /> and observe output longer than the input with a spurious ellipsis.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for Address.tsx, and the default (length=4) path is the only one that would be exercised incidentally.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A parameterized test rendering Address with lengths 0, 1, 4 and asserting the rendered text length is strictly less than the input length whenever the input is long enough to truncate.

results.title: Most owned components have no tests; formatting and range-clamping edge cases are uncovered
results.recommendation: Add unit tests for the pure formatting helpers (formatPrice, formatUsd, formatChange, formatVolume), Address truncation boundaries, and RangeSelector snap/clamp invariants (lower < upper, step alignment, NaN inputs); add a PoolStats test with a mocked fetch covering empty/malformed pairs responses and the chainId filter.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test files only import ThemeToggle and TokenSearch; the other components are not referenced by any included test.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A new test file (e.g., apps/web/test/components/format.test.tsx) covering formatPrice(0), formatPrice(0.001), formatPrice(-5), formatUsd(2_000_000), and a RangeSelector render asserting the two range inputs never cross (lower <= upper).
results.minimumFixScope: Add tests only; no production code changes required.

results.title: Hand-rolled SIWE message omits EIP-4361 Issued At and leaves nonce replay window unbounded
results.recommendation: Build the message with the `siwe` package (or at minimum append an Issued At line) and keep the nonce server-issued, single-use, and expiry-bound.
results.reproduction: Attempt verification of the generated message with a siwe-compliant parser: parsing/verification fails on missing issuedAt.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No useSiweAuth test is among the included files; the handshake is only exercised against the live backend, so message-format conformance is never asserted.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test that the constructed message round-trips through siwe.Message parsing and includes issuedAt.

results.title: listPools/fetchTokens parse error responses as JSON and hide the HTTP status
results.recommendation: Mirror fetchTokenByAddress: check res.ok and Effect.fail with the HTTP status before parsing.
results.reproduction: Point the app at a backend returning 500 with a non-JSON body and call listPools; the error message says "Pools parse failed" rather than reporting HTTP 500.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests among the included files are not visible (test/lib/* omitted); unit tests typically mock 2xx JSON responses only.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock a 500 response with an HTML body; assert the resulting error mentions the HTTP status.

results.title: PoolStats assumes pairs is always an array; DexScreener returns pairs:null for unknown tokens
results.recommendation: Normalize with `const pairs = json.pairs ?? []` before filtering/sorting, and consider retry:false for this third-party, rate-limited query.
results.reproduction: Open PoolStats with any address that has no pairs on DexScreener; the queryFn throws and the query enters error state with retries.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No PoolStats test is among the included files; typical mocks return a pairs array, and the null-pairs shape of the real API is easy to miss.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock fetch returning {pairs:null}; assert the query resolves to null without error state and without retries.

results.title: useWebSocket URL-change race defeats the unmount guard: stale onclose reconnects to the old URL and leaks the active socket
results.recommendation: Guard every handler by socket identity (e.g. `if (wsRef.current !== ws) return` inside onopen/onmessage/onclose/onerror) and clear any pending reconnect timer when a new connection is opened, or track a per-connection generation counter captured in connect().
results.reproduction: Mount useWebSocket with url A, wait for onopen, then re-render with url B. Observe isConnected flicker, a reconnect timer to A, and two live sockets (A's reconnect socket plus B's orphaned one).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The useWebSocket test file (test/hooks/useWebSocket.test.ts) was omitted from the included excerpts, so there is no evidence it exercises URL changes while connected; typical tests cover open/close/reconnect on a fixed URL only.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test: connect with url A, change url to B while connected, assert exactly one live socket (track close() calls), no reconnect timer scheduled for A, and isConnected stays true for B.

results.title: TokenSearch debounced search applies stale responses over newer queries (no abort/sequencing)
results.recommendation: Create an AbortController per debounce run and abort it in the effect cleanup, or track a request sequence number and discard resolutions from stale runs (the cancelled-flag pattern already used for defaultTokens load).
results.reproduction: Type "uni" and let the 300ms debounce fire, then type "usdc" before the first response arrives; if the first request resolves last, the dropdown shows "uni" results for the "usdc" query.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: test/components/TokenSearch.test.tsx was omitted from the included excerpts; happy-path tests with instantly-resolving mocks cannot expose interleaved slow responses.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock fetch with manually-resolved promises: trigger query A, change to query B before A resolves, resolve A after B; assert displayed results and isSearching reflect B.

results.title: PriceTicker crashes when a WebSocket frame carries a numeric price without tokenAddress
results.recommendation: Guard with `typeof payload.tokenAddress === "string"` before toLowerCase() (or validate envelopes with a runtime schema such as Effect Schema, consistent with api.ts), and require Number.isFinite(payload.price).
results.reproduction: Point PriceTicker at a hub that emits {type:"ping", data:{price:0}} or any envelope whose data has price but no tokenAddress; the component throws.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No PriceTicker test is among the included files, and the omitted useWebSocket test cannot cover PriceTicker's payload-shape assumptions; tests likely only feed well-formed PricePayload frames.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render PriceTicker with a mocked WebSocket that delivers {data:{price:1}} without tokenAddress; assert no throw and the placeholder dash is shown.

results.title: Input generates a new Math.random-based id on every render
results.recommendation: Use React's useId() for a stable id.
results.reproduction: Render Input, force a parent re-render, and observe the input's id attribute change.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests (ui.test.tsx omitted from included files) typically query by label/role text, which does not assert id stability across re-renders.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render Input inside a stateful parent, re-render the parent, and assert the input id is unchanged.

results.title: README documents outdated Vite version and wrong typecheck tool
results.recommendation: Update README to Vite 8 and correct the typecheck annotation to tsc.
results.reproduction: Read README.md, then compare with package.json scripts/dependencies.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Not applicable; documentation accuracy is not covered by tests.

results.title: Beta dependency and unstable API surface (effect/unstable/rpc) with no upgrade guard
results.recommendation: Keep the exact beta pin deliberately (document why in the manifest), and add a contract test that constructs the RpcGroup and decodes a sample payload so an upgrade that changes the unstable API fails CI instead of production.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist in this feature, so the RPC definitions' validity against the unstable API is never exercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that calls RpcGroup.make(ListPools) and decodes an example payload through the RPC's payload schema, run after any dependency bump.
results.minimumFixScope: Add RPC-definition smoke test in packages/shared; no production change required beyond the existing pin.

results.title: Shared contract package has no tests and no test script
results.recommendation: Add a test script (e.g. bun test) and schema round-trip tests using Schema.encodeSync/decodeUnknownSync for PoolSchema, TokenSchema, ListPoolsPayloadSchema, and the response schemas, plus a smoke test that Rpc.make/RpcGroup.make construct successfully.

results.title: List-pools response has two competing shapes: bare array in RPC vs unused PoolListResponseSchema wrapper
results.recommendation: Pick one contract: either set the RPC success schema to PoolListResponseSchema or delete the unused wrapper schemas (and align TokenListResponseSchema/TokenResponseSchema usage) so the shared package exposes a single shape per operation.
