results.title: Health endpoint body always reports status "ok" even when dependency probes fail (503)
results.recommendation: Derive the body status from the probe results, e.g. `status: allHealthy ? "ok" : "degraded"` (compute allHealthy before building the payload, or set the field after), so the payload and the HTTP status code can never disagree.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only linked test file (apps/api/test/index.test.ts) contains placeholder assertions for string concatenation and arithmetic; no test exercises the /health handler or its degraded path.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: With stubbed bindings where checkD1/checkKV/checkR2 fail, call app.request('/health') and assert the HTTP status is 503 and the body's status field is not "ok".

results.title: Structured request log is skipped for requests whose handler throws (500s logged without request context)
results.recommendation: Wrap the post-next logging in try/finally (or catch, log the 500 entry, and rethrow) so a structured log line with method, path, status 500, and duration is emitted for every request, including failures.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests do not exercise middleware behavior or logging at all.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Register a stub route that throws, spy on console.log/console.error, and assert a JSON log line containing method, path, and status 500 is emitted in addition to the onError output.

results.title: CORS default allowlist includes http://localhost:3000 and is inherited by any environment that omits CORS_ORIGINS
results.recommendation: Remove localhost from the fallback default (use only the production origin) and require CORS_ORIGINS to be set explicitly per environment, or gate the localhost entry on c.env.ENVIRONMENT being a dev value.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No CORS tests exist in the linked suite; the placeholder tests never construct requests with an Origin header.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Call the origin callback (or app.request with an Origin header) with ENVIRONMENT=production and no CORS_ORIGINS set, asserting that http://localhost:3000 is not allowed.

results.title: Feature test suite is placeholder-only; the API entry point has no test coverage
results.recommendation: Replace the placeholder tests with real coverage using the already-declared @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers devDependency: test /health (healthy and degraded), CORS allow/deny for configured origins, invalid poolId → 400, canonicalized poolId forwarding (uppercase hex input maps to lower-case idFromName), 404 JSON shape, and onError returning a generic 500.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests assert unrelated trivial behavior and were evidently written as scaffolding; they cannot catch regressions in any code path of apps/api/src/index.ts.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Describe suite: (1) `app.request('/health')` with healthy bindings → 200 + status "ok"; (2) with a failing D1 stub → 503 + degraded status; (3) `app.request('/ws/orderbook/0xABC...')` with 64-hex uppercase poolId → request forwarded with lower-cased poolId; (4) invalid poolId → 400.

results.title: Dev-stage name derivation diverges between the alchemy scripts and the Pages upload script
results.recommendation: Derive the dev stage name once (e.g., a shared helper script or a single environment variable set before all commands) using the same sanitization, and use that value in `plan:dev`, `deploy:dev`, `destroy:dev`, and `web:deploy:dev`; add `test -n "$USER"` guards to the alchemy dev scripts as well.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The package has no test script and no test files, so the shell pipelines in package.json scripts are never exercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A shell test that runs the STAGE_SUFFIX derivation against representative usernames (all-lowercase, mixed case, longer than 44 chars, characters outside [a-z0-9-]) and asserts the resulting Pages project name matches the stage name used by `deploy:dev`.
results.minimumFixScope: infra/alchemy/package.json (scripts: stage derivation and USER guard)

results.title: No test coverage for the deploy script pipelines
results.recommendation: Add a `test` script (e.g., a small Bun/shell test that executes the script pipelines with sample environment values and asserts expected stage/project names and failure modes).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test script or test files exist in the package.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that runs `web:deploy:dev`'s STAGE_SUFFIX derivation with representative usernames and asserts the output equals the stage name used by `deploy:dev` (same as the regression test for the stage-derivation finding).

results.title: Floating dependency specs ("latest" and ">=" ranges) make installs non-reproducible
results.recommendation: Pin exact versions or narrow ranges, commit the lockfile, and add a CI step that verifies `bun install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No CI or install-verification logic exists in the reviewed files.

results.title: Package entrypoint is a Hello World stub and package metadata lacks main/exports
results.recommendation: Point `module`/`exports` at the real stack entrypoint, or drop the entrypoint fields entirely if this is purely a scripts package, and remove the scaffold `console.log` side effect.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist in the package, and nothing imports the package to trigger the side effect.

results.title: loadTimestamps issues one sequential getBlock RPC call per unique block, making batch latency scale with block count
results.recommendation: Fetch timestamps in parallel or batched (viem batchRequests / multicall, or parallel Promise.all over getBlock calls with bounded concurrency), and/or persist block timestamps in a small cache table so repeated windows and backfills reuse previously fetched values instead of re-querying the RPC.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No service tests exist, and the decoder tests do not exercise RPC call patterns.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Service test with a counting fake client asserting the number of getBlock calls for a batch of N unique blocks is N (or fewer after a timestamp cache is added).

results.title: Swaps for pools initialized before the initial index window are persisted without pool linkage and the pool row is never created
results.recommendation: Ensure the pool exists before recording a swap: either upsert a minimal pool row from the Swap event (using the poolId with null/placeholder token fields) or require/validate that genesisBlock covers contract deployment and fail loudly when swaps reference unknown pools. Additionally, add a repair/backfill query that re-associates orphaned swap rows once the pool row exists.
results.reproduction: Configure a chain with no genesisBlock and no cursor, deploy the indexer more than 10,000 blocks after the v4 PoolManager contract, and run indexBatch for v4_pool_manager: the Initialize event is outside the first window, the pool is never upserted, and every swap on it is persisted with poolId=null and null token linkage.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test file only exercises the pure decoders (parseV4PoolManagerLog, toRawLog); there are no tests for persistV4, resolveStartBlock, or the pool-missing swap path, so the orphaned-swap behavior is unverified.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Service-level test with a fake PublicClient returning a Swap log for a pool whose Initialize is outside the indexed range: assert recordSwap receives poolId and token linkage once the pool later becomes known, and that a backfill over the same range repairs previously orphaned rows.

results.title: Core indexer service logic (cursor advancement, batch windowing, swapSides, orphan-pool path) has no tests
results.recommendation: Add a service-level test suite using the documented clientFactory injection point (line 38) with a deterministic fake PublicClient and an in-memory/seed D1 binding, covering: cursor resolution from DB vs genesisBlock vs head-10k fallback, cursor advancement order relative to persist failures, swapSides mapping for both signs and the zero case, and the pool-missing swap path.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing suite deliberately targets only pure side-effect-free decoders (see file header doc), so none of the service behaviors are exercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Effect/vitest test driving indexBatch with a fake client: assert that a persist failure leaves the cursor unchanged, that a successful batch advances it to toBlock + 1n, and that swapSides maps (amount0>0, amount1<0) and (amount0<0, amount1>0) to the correct tokenIn/tokenOut/amountIn/amountOut.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/services/indexer.service.ts plus a new test file

results.title: Non-reproducible bun canary dist-tag in packageManager
results.recommendation: Pin the package manager to a stable exact version, e.g. "packageManager": "bun@1.4.0" (matching engines.bun), or if canary is genuinely required, pin a specific canary version/commit so resolution is deterministic. Optionally add a CI check that verifies the packageManager field matches /^bun@\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no tests for this feature (the owned file is a placeholder), and unit tests would not exercise package manager version resolution; only a CI/version-manager step would.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step asserting the packageManager field in package.json matches an exact semver (e.g. bun@<version>) rather than a dist-tag, failing on mutable tags like canary.

results.title: lint script coverage misses e2e test files and root configs
results.recommendation: Either expand the paths in scripts.lint (and lint:fix/format) to cover all project source, e.g. 'biome check src/ test/ e2e/' plus explicit root config files, or run 'biome check .' (with ignores for dist/ and node_modules) so e2e tests and configs are included. Verify the e2e test directory name in the repo before choosing paths.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and package.json script scope is not exercised by the vitest test suite; lint coverage is only observable when running the lint script against the full repo.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/web/package.json scripts.lint (and lint:fix, format) path arguments

results.title: lint script only checks src/, leaving package-level files outside verification
results.recommendation: Either widen the script to cover the whole package (e.g. 'biome check .') or list the extra files explicitly (e.g. 'biome check src/ package.json tsconfig.json'), and ensure the monorepo-root lint/CI job covers whatever this per-package script does not.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This feature ships no tests and script scope is a configuration property; no included test exercises which files the lint command inspects.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI check that places a file with a deliberate formatting/lint violation outside src/ (e.g. at the package root), runs 'bun run lint', and asserts a non-zero exit — proving out-of-scope files are covered.

results.title: Caret range on @biomejs/biome allows non-reproducible lint results
results.recommendation: Pin the exact Biome version (e.g. '2.5.5' without the caret) or rely strictly on a committed lockfile with 'bun install --frozen-lockfile' in CI so lint results are deterministic.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and dependency-version drift is not exercised by unit tests; it is a release-process concern.

results.title: packageManager pinned to floating 'bun@canary' tag makes builds non-reproducible and may violate the declared engines range
results.recommendation: Pin a concrete stable version, e.g. `"packageManager": "bun@1.4.x"` (or the current stable release), and keep `engines.bun` consistent with the pinned version; a floating `@canary` tag is not acceptable for a release pipeline.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no tests, and a version-pinning/reproducibility problem would not be observable from functional tests of the lint command itself; it only manifests across installs and CI runs.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI check that runs the pinned package manager (e.g., `bun --version` after install) and asserts the resolved version is an exact, stable version matching the packageManager field rather than a canary build.
results.minimumFixScope: Single-line change to package.json line 40 pinning a stable bun version (and aligning line 37 if needed).

results.title: lint script does not fail on Biome warnings, so the CI lint gate can pass with outstanding diagnostics
results.recommendation: Change the script to `biome check --error-on-warnings .` (or use `biome ci .` for CI semantics) so warning-level diagnostics fail the lint gate, or explicitly configure warning severities in biome.json.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no tests; Biome's exit-code semantics are only exercised when CI runs the script, and a pass-with-warnings state produces no failure that a test would observe.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step that seeds a warning-level diagnostic in a fixture file and asserts `bun run lint` exits non-zero, or an assertion that the exact command executed contains `--error-on-warnings`/`ci`.

results.title: Aggregate `build` script fails (or silently skips) any workspace lacking a `build` script
results.recommendation: Verify every workspace package defines a `build` script (or use `--if-present` where the installed bun supports it), scope the filter to packages that actually produce artifacts, and document how `contracts:build`/`web:build` relate to the aggregate `build`. Add a CI check that runs `bun run build` and asserts all expected artifacts exist afterward.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature and script presence across workspace packages is not exercised by the vitest suite declared in package.json.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step (or a small script invoked from `test`) that asserts every workspace package under apps/*, packages/*, infra/* either defines a `build` script or is explicitly excluded, and that `bun run build` exits 0 and produces expected artifacts.
results.minimumFixScope: package.json scripts plus `build` script definitions in workspace packages.

results.title: Build toolchain pinned to `bun@canary`, making `build` non-reproducible
results.recommendation: Pin a stable, released bun version (e.g., `bun@1.2.x`) in `packageManager` and align `engines` with it; if canary is truly required, pin a specific canary build identifier.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and toolchain version pinning is an environment concern outside the vitest suite.

results.title: `format` script rewrites files in place, so any CI/release gate invoking it never fails on unformatted code and mutates the tree
results.recommendation: Split into `format` = `biome format .` (check-only, exits non-zero on diffs) and `format:fix` = `biome format --write .` (mutating), mirroring the existing `lint`/`lint:fix` pair; or keep `format` mutating but add a separate `format:check` script and use it (or `biome ci`) in CI/release gates.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and package scripts are not exercised by the vitest suite; the mutating-vs-checking behavior is only observable when the script is invoked by CI/release tooling, which is not part of the included files.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A workflow-level check that runs `biome format .` (no `--write`) against a fixture containing an unformatted file and asserts a non-zero exit code and no file modifications.
results.minimumFixScope: package.json (scripts `format`/`format:fix`) plus whatever CI config consumes the script.

results.title: `format` (and `lint`) bypass the workspace delegation used by sibling scripts, leaving non-Biome sources unformatted and generated files exposed to rewriting
results.recommendation: Decide on a single convention: either keep root-level `biome format --write .` and add explicit coverage for Solidity (e.g., a `format` script that also runs `forge fmt` in packages/contracts), or delegate via `bun run --filter '*' format` with per-workspace scripts; ensure biome.json ignores generated/artifact directories before running `--write .` repo-wide.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests or CI definitions are included, so the workspace-delegation inconsistency and the Solidity/artifact coverage gaps are not exercised anywhere.
results.minimumFixScope: package.json scripts (and per-workspace format scripts and/or biome.json ignores, depending on the chosen convention).

results.title: format and lint scripts only cover src/ and test/, omitting package-root config files
results.recommendation: Scope the format/lint scripts to the package root (e.g. `biome check --write .` with a biome.json `files.ignore` for dist/generated output) or explicitly list root-level config files so format and lint cover the whole package consistently.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover the script scope; the feature metadata lists no tests and package.json has no test entries for the format script.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step that runs biome in check mode across the package root (including config files) and fails on any unformatted file, proving the format script's scope is complete.
results.minimumFixScope: Update the path arguments of the format (and lint) scripts in apps/web/package.json to include package-root config files or the package root with proper ignores.

results.title: format script uses deprecated `biome format` command, inconsistent with `biome check`-based lint
results.recommendation: Align format with lint by using `biome check --write src/ test/` (or add a `format:check` script such as `biome check src/ test/` for CI), so formatting and linting share one command family and survive a Biome major upgrade.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no tests, and package.json contains no test entries that exercise script definitions; script behavior is only verified manually or in CI pipelines not included in this review.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A repo-level test (or CI step) that parses apps/web/package.json and asserts the format and lint scripts use the same biome subcommand family, plus a smoke check that a formatted tree passes `biome check` in dry-run mode.
results.minimumFixScope: Edit the format script in apps/web/package.json to use `biome check --write` and add a format:check script for CI.

results.title: Typecheck gate relies on tsconfig discovery and stale wrangler-generated bindings
results.recommendation: Pin the config with `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and either commit the generated bindings file and add a `pretypecheck` hook running `wrangler types`, or chain the scripts as `"typecheck": "wrangler types && tsc --noEmit"` so the gate always validates current bindings.

results.suggestedRegressionTest: CI smoke check: run `rm -f worker-configuration.d.ts && bun run typecheck` in a fresh checkout and assert it still succeeds, proving binding regeneration is part of the gate.

results.title: Typecheck scope may exclude test/ files that lint and format already cover
results.recommendation: Make test type coverage explicit: either include test/ in the tsconfig used by the typecheck script, or add a `tsconfig.test.json` plus a `typecheck:test` script and include both in the root `typecheck` command so the script's scope matches lint/format.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are linked to this feature, and the gap only manifests at the script/tsconfig level, outside the vitest suite.

results.title: lint script only covers src/ and test/, excluding package config files (wrangler.toml, biome.json, vitest config, migrations)

Alternatively, if full-package linting is intended, use `biome check .` with appropriate `files.includes`/`files.ignore` rules in biome.json.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Package.json scripts are not executed by vitest tests; the test script (`vitest run`) never invokes the lint script, and there are no tests listed for this feature to assert script path coverage.

results.title: No automated verification that the typecheck script executes successfully

results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest test that spawns `bun run typecheck` (cwd = repo root) and asserts exit code 0 on a clean tree and non-zero when a temp file with a type error is added to the tsconfig include set.

results.title: Caret range on TypeScript 7 (native compiler) leaves typecheck behavior floating
results.recommendation: Pin the exact TypeScript version (or a tightly bounded range), verify the root tsconfig's compiler options are supported by TypeScript 7's native tsc, and lock the dependency via the lockfile so typecheck behavior is deterministic.

results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step that installs with the locked typescript version, runs `bun run typecheck`, and asserts zero diagnostics.

results.title: typecheck script only typechecks the root project and may skip workspace packages
results.recommendation: Typecheck per workspace instead of (or in addition to) the root: add a `typecheck` script to each workspace package and change the root script to `bun run --filter '*' typecheck`, consistent with dev/build; alternatively use `tsc -b` with project references rooted in a tsconfig that includes every workspace. Wire the aggregate into CI as a required check.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no tests and no CI workflow is included in the reviewed file set, so nothing asserts that every workspace package is covered by the typecheck command.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest test (or CI step) that introduces a deliberate type error in a source file of a workspace package (e.g., packages/*) and asserts `bun run typecheck` exits non-zero; a companion check that the clean tree exits 0.

results.title: packageManager pinned to bun@canary undermines reproducibility of all scripts
results.recommendation: Pin packageManager to a stable bun release (e.g., `bun@1.x.y`) that satisfies the engines.bun `>=1.4.0` constraint, and reserve canary for CI jobs that explicitly test new features.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests or CI files in the reviewed set verify the resolved toolchain version or its stability.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI check that runs `bun --version` and asserts it matches the pinned packageManager version string.

results.title: typecheck script depends on tsc from an unsatisfiable peer dependency (typescript ^6)
results.recommendation: Declare typescript as a devDependency with a satisfiable, pinned range (e.g., `^5.9` or whatever stable line exists) and keep any peerDependency range only if the package genuinely exposes typescript types to consumers; then verify `bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run typecheck` succeeds in a clean checkout.

results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step that runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` followed by `bun run typecheck` in infra/alchemy in a clean workspace, failing on any peer-resolution error or missing tsc binary.
results.minimumFixScope: infra/alchemy/package.json: move typescript into devDependencies with a satisfiable range (and correct the peer range if retained).

results.title: typecheck script does not pin a tsconfig, so tsc scope depends on ambient filesystem state
results.recommendation: Pin the project explicitly: `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json"` and ensure infra/alchemy/tsconfig.json is committed; optionally add a pre-script check that the file exists.

results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are attached to this feature, and script behavior under missing/ambient tsconfig files is not exercised by the vitest suite.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI check that runs `bun run typecheck` in infra/alchemy and asserts tsc used the package-local tsconfig (e.g., by comparing `--showConfig` output against the committed tsconfig) or fails if tsconfig.json is missing.

results.title: Typecheck types against @types/node 26 while engines allow Node 24, so the gate can pass code that crashes on the minimum supported runtime
results.recommendation: Align @types/node with the minimum declared engine (e.g. `@types/node: ^24` if Node 24 is the floor) or raise the engines minimum to Node 26; optionally add a CI job that runs typecheck on the lowest supported Node version.

results.title: typecheck runs bare tsc without regenerating TanStack Router route files, so fresh-checkout CI can fail or check stale generated code
results.recommendation: Make typecheck generation-aware, e.g. `"typecheck": "tsr generate && tsc --noEmit"`, or commit generated route files and keep them in sync (for example via a pre-typecheck hook or CI step). At minimum, run the same generation step before typecheck as before build so both gates validate identical inputs.
results.reproduction: Fresh `bun install` + `bun run typecheck` in apps/web on a checkout where routeTree.gen.ts is not committed; tsc errors on missing generated module imports.

results.title: build emits to dist/ without cleaning the directory, risking stale bundles being treated as the artifact
results.recommendation: Remove the output directory before building (e.g., `rm -rf dist && wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir=dist`, or a `clean` script invoked before `build` in CI) so `dist/` always reflects the current source.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are linked to this feature; nothing asserts the contents or freshness of the `dist/` output.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI check that runs `bun run build`, then asserts `dist/` contains exactly the expected bundle file(s) for the current entry point and no orphaned files from a previous build.

results.title: build dry-run validates only the default environment; staging/production config is never checked before release
results.recommendation: Add per-environment dry-run validation, e.g. `build:staging`/`build:production` scripts running `wrangler deploy --dry-run --env staging` and `--env production`, and have CI execute all three (default, staging, production) before tagging a release.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are linked to this feature, and vitest does not exercise package scripts or wrangler configuration validation.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step that runs `bun run build` plus `wrangler deploy --dry-run --env staging` and `wrangler deploy --dry-run --env production` and asserts exit code 0 for each.

results.title: No automated coverage guards the build script's non-deploying dry-run behavior
results.recommendation: Add a CI step that runs `bun run build` and fails the pipeline if the output indicates a real deploy (e.g., assert the command exits 0 with dry-run output and that no `dist` upload/deploy step follows), or at minimum a lint-style check that the build script contains `--dry-run`.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test suite is empty for this feature, and vitest only covers `src/` and `test/` per the `lint` script; package scripts are not exercised by any included test.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI job that runs `bun run build` and asserts the command output contains dry-run markers and that no deploy is triggered (e.g., `wrangler deploy --dry-run` exits 0 without authentication).

results.title: packages/shared defines no test script even though it hosts the shared API contract
results.recommendation: Add a `test` script (e.g., `"test": "vitest run"`) with vitest in devDependencies, add at least smoke/round-trip tests for the exported RpcGroup and schemas, and confirm the root test command covers this workspace.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature's tests array is empty and the owned file contains no test script or test dependencies, so nothing currently exercises this package's behavior.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest smoke test that imports the package entrypoint (src/index.ts) and asserts the exported RpcGroup/schemas are constructible and serializable per their declared contracts.
results.minimumFixScope: packages/shared/package.json (add test script and vitest devDependency)

results.title: typecheck script depends on an implicit tsconfig.json that is not declared or visible in scope
results.recommendation: Make the config explicit and self-contained: change the script to `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and commit a packages/shared/tsconfig.json that includes src/**/*.ts with strict: true (ideally extending a shared base config). Consider `--pretty false` for CI log stability, and add a CI step that actually executes `bun run typecheck` inside packages/shared so the gate is proven to work end-to-end.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no tests, and a missing/broken compiler config only surfaces when the command is executed by a developer or CI; there is no automated check exercising the script itself.
results.minimumFixScope: packages/shared/package.json plus a committed packages/shared/tsconfig.json (if one is not already present)

results.title: No automated verification that the build script produces a valid dist artifact
results.recommendation: Add a CI job (or a vitest test spawning the script) that runs `bun run build` and asserts the output artifact exists (`dist/index.html`, generated route tree file), so the release feature is exercised on every change.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test scripts (lines 11-15) run vitest/playwright unit and e2e suites, which do not execute the build script or check its output artifact.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test/CI step that runs `bun run build` and asserts `dist/index.html` exists and the generated route tree file is present after `tsr generate`.
results.minimumFixScope: CI configuration or a new test file invoking the build script

results.title: Build script ships without type-checking (vite/esbuild transpiles without tsc)
results.recommendation: Compose the check into the build path, e.g. `"build": "tsr generate && tsc --noEmit && vite build"`, or add an explicit CI step that runs `bun run typecheck` before `bun run build` and gate releases on it.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no tests (`tests: []`), and no CI workflow file is included in the review scope; the typecheck script (line 16) is separate from the build script and nothing in the owned file enforces its execution during builds.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI job that runs `bun run typecheck` followed by `bun run build` and fails the pipeline if either step fails; optionally a vitest test spawning the build and asserting `dist/` contains index.html.

results.title: deploy script can publish stale or missing build output (no predeploy build hook)
results.recommendation: Rename the current script to `deploy:only` and add `"deploy": "bun run build && bun run deploy:only"` (or use a `predeploy` hook) so deploys always build from the current source.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover the deploy script, and deploy is a manual/CI command with no automated invocation in the included files.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI deploy job that verifies `dist/` is regenerated (e.g., by running build inside the deploy job) rather than reusing a cached artifact.

results.title: Version skew across @tanstack/router runtime, CLI, plugin, and devtools packages
results.recommendation: Align the four @tanstack/router packages on the same minor version (or a shared `@tanstack/router-core`-style exact version) and verify the generated route tree compiles with `tsc --noEmit` after `tsr generate`.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Unit/e2e tests exercise app behavior, not the compatibility of generated route-tree code with the router runtime; a version-skew failure would surface only at codegen/build time.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A CI step that runs `tsr generate && tsc --noEmit` and fails on any diff or type error, pinning the toolchain to a known-good combination.

results.title: HTTP status mapping depends on a hardcoded literal reason string; every non-'no_pool' failure is reported as 503
results.recommendation: Carry structured error information from the service (e.g., a clientError/status field on V3QuoteError or a discriminated union) and map status from that field; treat only genuinely transient/server-side reasons as 503, and validate fee against the canonical V3 fee tiers (100/500/3000/10000) at the route boundary to reject unsupported tiers with a 400.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for the route, and the mapping behavior depends on the service's reason taxonomy which is not exercised anywhere in the included files.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test that throws V3QuoteError with each known reason and asserts the expected status per reason, plus a test asserting fee values outside the canonical tier set return 400.
results.minimumFixScope: Replace the literal comparison with a structured status field on V3QuoteError and tighten the fee validation in the route.

results.title: Catch handler returns raw internal error strings to unauthenticated clients
results.recommendation: Return a fixed generic message (e.g., { error: "Quote failed", reason }) for non-V3QuoteError failures and log the detailed error server-side (console.error / observability), and ensure V3QuoteError messages are sanitized client-safe strings rather than wrapped underlying provider errors.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this route, so the error-serialization behavior is unexercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Stub the quote service to throw a non-V3QuoteError Error with a message containing an RPC URL, assert the response body's error field does not contain that string while the status is 503.
results.minimumFixScope: Replace String(error) in the catch handler with a constant generic message and log the original error.

results.title: Public quote endpoint fans out to an external RPC with no rate limiting or caching
results.recommendation: Add rate limiting (Cloudflare Rate Limiting binding or a Durable Object/KV-based limiter) on this route, and add a short-TTL cache keyed by (tokenIn, tokenOut, amountIn, fee, slippage) so repeated identical quotes are served without RPC fan-out; also consider a maximum URL/query length guard before BigInt parsing.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for the route, and rate limiting is an operational property that the included test configuration does not exercise.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A test asserting that two consecutive identical requests only invoke the quote service once when a cache is present, and that requests beyond a configured per-IP budget receive 429.
results.minimumFixScope: Add a rate-limit binding/check at the top of the handler and a short-TTL cache layer around the service call.

results.title: No automated tests exist for GET /v3/quote despite the route being listed in the coverage config
results.recommendation: Add a vitest test suite for this route covering: each 400 path, the 503 env-misconfiguration path, a mocked quote success asserting amountOut/minAmountOut/gasEstimate/protocolFee shape and exact minAmountOut arithmetic (e.g., amountOut=1_000_000n with slippage=0.5 gives 995_000n), the no_pool→404 mapping, and the rpc_error→503 mapping.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files are included in the feature (tests: []), so there is nothing covering the route's validation, error mapping, or minAmountOut arithmetic despite the coverage include.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: apps/api/test/v3-quote.test.ts using the Cloudflare test pool: mount v3Quote with stubbed env (RPC_URL, V3_FACTORY_ADDRESS, V3_QUOTER_ADDRESS), assert 400 for missing/format-invalid params and out-of-range fee/slippage, assert 503 when env unset, inject a V3QuoteService returning a fixed amountOut and assert minAmountOut = (amountOut * (10_000 - round(slippage*100))) / 10_000, and assert 404 for no_pool reason vs 503 otherwise.
results.minimumFixScope: Add a test file under apps/api/test covering the route with the Cloudflare vitest pool; no production code change required.

results.title: Internal error details exposed to clients via String(err) in 500 responses
results.recommendation: Log the full error server-side (e.g., c.env.ENVIRONMENT-gated console/logger) and return a generic message such as { error: "Internal server error" } with 500; keep structured error codes for expected failures.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this route, and the coverage configuration does not include src/routes/pools.ts, so the error-response shape is unverified.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that a forced service failure (mocked listPools rejection) returns a body that does not contain the underlying error message/stack.

results.title: sortBy/sortDirection/filterToken are forwarded to PoolService without enum/format validation
results.recommendation: Validate sortBy against the allowed set (tvl|volume|fees|created) and sortDirection against (asc|desc) before building options, returning 400 with a descriptive message on mismatch; validate filterToken against the 0x + 64-hex pattern (consistent with the poolId check at line 65) or reject/ignore it. Never rely on the type cast as validation.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature (tests: []), and the coverage configuration omits src/routes/pools.ts entirely, so no test exercises the validation boundary of these params.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Route-level test asserting that GET / with sortBy=name, sortDirection=sideways, and filterToken=not-an-address each return 400, and that valid enum values reach the service with the parsed options intact.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/pools.ts (validate params at lines 42-44 and return 400 on invalid values).

results.title: GET /pools route has no test coverage while sibling routes are covered
results.recommendation: Add route tests under apps/api/test/ covering: default and boundary limit (1, 200, 0, 201, non-numeric), offset (0, negative, non-numeric), invalid sortBy/sortDirection, valid request shape { pools, count }, and the 404 poolId path (bad hex, missing pool). Add src/routes/pools.ts to the coverage include list.

results.suggestedRegressionTest: Vitest route test (cloudflareTest pool) exercising GET /api/v1/pools with query matrices for limit/offset/sortBy/sortDirection and asserting 200/400 status codes and response shape.

results.title: sortBy/sortDirection query params cast to enums without runtime validation
results.recommendation: Validate sortBy against {tvl, volume, fees, created} and sortDirection against {asc, desc} at the handler boundary, returning 400 for anything else, and ensure the service builds ORDER BY only from a parameterized whitelist.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for the pools routes and the validation is absent from the handler, so the invalid-input path is entirely unexercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Request GET /api/v1/pools?sortBy=invalid and GET /api/v1/pools?sortDirection=up; assert 400 responses rather than 500 or injected queries.
results.minimumFixScope: Add an explicit whitelist check for both params in the GET / handler before constructing PoolQueryOptions.

results.title: GET /:poolId has no tests and pools.ts is missing from vitest coverage include
results.recommendation: Add a vitest-pool-workers integration test hitting GET /api/v1/pools/:poolId covering malformed id (400), unknown id (404), known id (200), and add src/routes/pools.ts to the coverage include array.

results.title: poolId accepts mixed-case hex but is not normalized before lookup

results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this route, so the mixed-case acceptance path is untested.

results.minimumFixScope: Add toLowerCase() normalization after validation in the GET /:poolId handler.

results.title: 500 responses disclose internal error details via String(err)
results.recommendation: Log the full error server-side (console.error / Worker logging) and return a generic body such as { error: "Internal error" } with status 500; only expose sanitized messages for known, client-relevant failure types.

results.suggestedRegressionTest: Integration test via @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers SELF.fetch that forces the pool service to fail (e.g., by injecting a failing DB layer) and asserts the 500 body does not contain the thrown message, SQL text, or stack trace.
results.minimumFixScope: Replace String(err) with a generic error body plus server-side logging in both catch blocks in pools.ts.

results.title: Internal error details leaked to clients via String(err) in 500 responses
results.recommendation: Return a stable generic body such as `{ "error": "Internal server error" }` with 500, and log the real error server-side (e.g., `console.error`/Observability) where it cannot reach clients.

results.title: No tests cover the tokens route (GET / and GET /:address)

results.suggestedRegressionTest: Parameterized Vitest request tests hitting GET /api/v1/tokens (mounted route) with `limit=abc`, `limit=-5`, `limit=100000`, `limit=0`, `?search=...`, and GET /api/v1/tokens/:address with bad/unknown/valid addresses.

results.title: Documented `verified` query parameter is silently ignored by GET / handler
results.recommendation: Either implement the `verified` filter (parse `c.req.query("verified")` and pass it through to `listTokens`/the token-list service, or filter the returned list), or remove it from the JSDoc contract so the documented API matches behavior. If filtering is deferred, reject the parameter with 400 when it is present and unsupported, so callers cannot silently receive unfiltered data.

results.title: GET /:address has no tests and src/routes/tokens.ts is omitted from vitest coverage include
results.recommendation: Add a route-level test suite using @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers (already configured in vitest.config.ts) exercising the /:address handler: valid checksummed address → 200, unknown address → 404, malformed address → 400, service failure → 500; also add "src/routes/tokens.ts" to the coverage include array.

results.title: 500 responses leak raw internal error text via String(err)
results.recommendation: Log the full error server-side (console.error or an Effect logger) and return a generic message such as { error: "Internal server error" } with 500; keep detailed diagnostics out of the response body.

results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this route, so the error path (lines 93-95) is untested and the leak would not be caught.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Force getToken to throw and assert the 500 response body contains only a generic message and none of the internal error text.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/tokens.ts — replace String(err) with a logged, generic 500 response in both handlers.

results.title: GET /:address accepts non-EIP-55 addresses: false 404s for valid tokens (checksum not validated)
results.recommendation: Enforce EIP-55 in the :address handler: validate with viem's isAddress(address, { strict: true }) and reject non-checksummed input with 400, or normalize the input to checksum form (getAddress) before calling getToken so lowercase queries resolve to the canonical entry.
results.reproduction: GET /api/v1/tokens/<all-lowercase hex form of a token that exists in the checksummed list> → passes the shape regex at line 77, then returns 404 "Token not found" instead of 200 because the lookup key does not match the checksummed canonical entry (assuming getToken matches exactly, which is the documented storage form).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this route (feature tests list is empty), and the vitest coverage include in apps/api/vitest.config.ts (lines 67-83) omits src/routes/tokens.ts, so the address-validation path is completely unguarded.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Route test with a mocked/fake TokenListService asserting: (1) the lowercase form of a listed token returns 200 (via normalization) or 400 (if strict checksum is enforced), (2) a non-checksummed mixed-case address returns 400, (3) an unknown but checksum-valid address returns 404.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/tokens.ts — enforce EIP-55 in the :address handler or normalize input before getToken.

results.title: Catch-all 503 handler interpolates raw internal error text into the public response body and conflates data failures with outages
results.recommendation: Return a generic body (e.g., { error: 'price guard unavailable' }) for 503s, log the real error server-side (console.error), and classify data-level failures separately (e.g., 422 or 400 for tokens without a valid price) so clients can distinguish 'cannot verify' from 'service down'.
results.reproduction: GET /price-guard?token0=<valid address>&token1=<valid address>&price=1 where refreshPrice returns 0 or non-finite priceUsd for either token; observe the internal Error message echoed in the 503 body.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: apps/api/test/price-guard.test.ts imports only the pure evaluatePriceGuard function and never exercises the route handler or the catch path, so the error-interpolation and status-mapping behavior is entirely untested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Route-level test that forces refreshPrice to fail (and to return a non-positive price) asserting the 503 body contains no internal error text and that the unpriced-token case maps to a distinct status (400/422) rather than 503.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/price-guard.ts lines 86-108 (error classification and sanitized response body).

results.title: GET /price-guard handler has no route-level tests; all validation and status-code branches are uncovered
results.recommendation: Add integration tests using @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers (already configured) that exercise the handler through Hono's app.request with mocked PriceService/runEffect, covering each 400 branch, the 200/422 split, the 503 path, and the maxDeviationBps default.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests only call the exported pure function directly and never construct the Hono app or issue requests, so none of the handler logic (validation, env handling, layer wiring, status mapping) executes.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Parameterized route test: app.request('/price-guard?token0=...&token1=...&price=...&maxDeviationBps=...') asserting 400 for each invalid input, 200 for valid guard, 422 for deviation over threshold, and 503 when the service layer throws.

results.title: Unauthenticated endpoint accepts arbitrary token addresses and triggers two price refreshes per request with no rate limiting
results.recommendation: Add per-client rate limiting (e.g., token bucket backed by KV/Durable Object), validate tokens against a known token list before refreshing, and/or short-circuit with a cached guard result when available.
results.reproduction: Repeatedly call GET /price-guard with random valid-format token addresses; each request issues two refreshPrice calls for addresses absent from the cache.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No route-level tests exist, and the pure-function tests never touch the refresh path or the unauthenticated request surface.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Route test asserting that addresses not in the known token list return 400/404 without invoking refreshPrice (pre-refresh validation), plus a throttle test if rate limiting is added.
results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/price-guard.ts (token whitelist/rate-limit check before layer construction).

results.title: No tests cover the new POST /deposit-estimate route despite it being in the coverage include list
results.recommendation: Add a test file for this route (e.g. apps/api/test/routes/liquidity.test.ts) using the Cloudflare vitest pool: assert 200 responses with correct net-after-fee amounts for add_liquidity (multiple inputs) and add_liquidity_single_sided (exactly one input), and 400 responses for each rejection path, including grossAmount that overflows BigInt and token address format errors.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files exist for this route; the feature's tests list is empty and no test files were included in the review. The coverage config lists the file, but coverage configuration is not a test.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: POST /deposit-estimate with { mode: 'add_liquidity', amounts: [{ grossAmount: '1000000' }] } asserting protocolFee.netAmount = 999000 (0.1% entry fee), plus 400 cases for { amounts: [] }, { amounts: 8+ entries }, single-sided with 2 entries, grossAmount 'abc', grossAmount exceeding uint256/BigInt range, and token '0x123'.
results.minimumFixScope: Add route-level tests under apps/api/test covering the handler's success and 400 paths.

results.title: Unbounded grossAmount digit strings allow CPU-exhaustion amplification and accept amounts outside the router's uint256 range
results.recommendation: Reject grossAmount strings longer than 78 digits (uint256 max) with a 400 before calling BigInt (e.g. extend the UINT_RE check with a length guard), which both bounds parse cost and enforces the on-chain amount range. Optionally add per-route rate limiting since the endpoint is unauthenticated.
results.reproduction: curl -X POST https://<worker>/api/v1/liquidity/deposit-estimate -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"amounts":[{"grossAmount":"'$(python3 -c 'print("9"*2000000)')'"}]}' — the BigInt parse of the 2M-digit string dominates request CPU time; 8 such entries amplify further.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this route, and even a naive test with a short overflow string (79+ digits) would not expose the CPU-cost dimension of unbounded lengths; the length cap would need an explicit boundary test.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert 400 for grossAmount with 79 digits ('9'.repeat(79)) and confirm a 78-digit value is accepted, ensuring the digit-length cap matches uint256.
results.minimumFixScope: Add a digit-length cap (<= 78) in parseInputs before BigInt conversion.

results.title: insertTransaction writes the same (chain_id, tx_hash) key space as recordSwap but without conflict handling
results.recommendation: Add ON CONFLICT(chain_id, tx_hash) DO NOTHING (or DO UPDATE for status transitions) to insertTransaction, matching recordSwap's semantics, and document which writer owns which status.
results.reproduction: Call insertTransaction with a txHash already present in transactions (inserted via recordSwap or a prior insertTransaction call); the query throws a UNIQUE constraint error.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for the module, and the collision only occurs across two different functions, which a single-function test would not exercise.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Insert the same (chain_id, tx_hash) twice via insertTransaction and assert the second call succeeds as a no-op rather than throwing.

results.title: upsertUser returns a nonce that is never persisted for existing users
results.recommendation: Persist the returned nonce on conflict, e.g. ON CONFLICT(address) DO UPDATE SET nonce = excluded.nonce, last_active_at = excluded.last_active_at, or read back the stored nonce after the upsert and return that instead of the pre-generated value.
results.reproduction: Call upsertUser('0x...') twice for the same address; the second call returns a nonce different from the value stored in the users row, and the returned value exists nowhere in the database.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature reports tests: [] and no test files are included for this module, so the insert-vs-return mismatch is never exercised; the upsert path looks correct at a glance.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test with a mocked/embedded SqlClient: call upsertUser twice for the same address and assert the nonce returned by the second call equals the nonce read back from the users table.

results.title: setIndexerCursor can regress next_block with concurrent or out-of-order indexer workers
results.recommendation: Make the update monotonic: ON CONFLICT(chain_id, indexer) DO UPDATE SET next_block = MAX(next_block, excluded.next_block), updated_at = excluded.updated_at (or add WHERE next_block < excluded.next_block to the DO UPDATE clause).
results.reproduction: setIndexerCursor(1, 'v3', 105n) followed by setIndexerCursor(1, 'v3', 103n) leaves next_block = 103.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this module (feature tests: []), and the bug only manifests with a second write after a first, which a naive single-call test would not catch.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that setIndexerCursor with a smaller nextBlock after a larger one leaves the larger value in place.

results.title: updateLiquidityPosition/updateV4LiquidityPosition silently drop updates when the position row does not exist
results.recommendation: Upsert instead of bare UPDATE (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE), or insert-on-miss when RETURNING yields no row, and return a signal that the row was created vs updated.
results.reproduction: Call updateLiquidityPosition with a tokenId that has no row in liquidity_positions; the function returns null with no error and no row created.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for the module, and the silent null return only shows up when the position row is absent, which requires a two-table setup to observe.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Call updateLiquidityPosition for a non-existent tokenId and assert either an insert happens or the function returns an explicit failure instead of a silent null.

results.title: No test coverage for the db query/schema module despite full vitest infrastructure
results.recommendation: Add unit tests using @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers with an in-memory D1 (or a mocked SqlClient) covering upsertUser, setIndexerCursor, insertTransaction vs recordSwap conflict behavior, the updateLiquidityPosition miss path, and the rowTo* converters' handling of null/0/1 values.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is the gap itself: no tests exist for this module, so every finding above is unguarded.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest suite that applies the D1 migration to an in-memory database and runs each exported query helper twice (second run exercising conflict/upsert paths) with assertions on returned and persisted state.
results.minimumFixScope: New test file under apps/api/test covering apps/api/src/db

results.title: test script hard-fails on an empty test suite (no --passWithNoTests)
results.recommendation: Add '--passWithNoTests' to the test script (or set passWithNoTests: true in the vitest config) so an empty suite is treated as a pass until tests exist. Once real tests are committed, the flag is harmless since it only affects the no-tests-found case.

results.minimumFixScope: apps/api/package.json line 15: change "test": "vitest run" to "test": "vitest run --passWithNoTests"

results.title: Root `test` script silently omits the Solidity/forge contract test suite

results.title: Stat renders label, value, and description as unlabeled sibling divs with no ARIA grouping or association
results.recommendation: Wrap the content in a container with role="group" and aria-label={label} (or use dl/dt/dd semantics), and add an aria-live region or visually-hidden trend text (e.g., aria-label including 'trending up/down') so the trend is not conveyed by color alone.

results.title: Short addresses render without mono font or full-address tooltip (inconsistent fallback branch)
results.recommendation: Use a single span that always applies `font-mono text-sm` and `title={address}`, and only vary the child text between the truncated and full value, e.g. compute `display = address.length < length * 2 + 3 ? address : `${address.slice(0, 2 + length)}…${address.slice(-length)}`` and render one span with both branches' attributes.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this component (feature declares an empty tests array), so the attribute divergence between branches is unobserved.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render with a short address (e.g. "0x1234") and assert the span has classes `font-mono text-sm` and a `title` attribute equal to the full address; render with a 42-char address and assert the text equals the truncated form while `title` still holds the full value.

results.title: Unvalidated `length` prop: zero or negative values produce degenerate or expanding output
results.recommendation: Clamp or validate `length`, e.g. `const n = Math.max(1, Math.floor(length ?? 4))`, or fall back to rendering the full address when `length < 1`; add a dev-time guard if stricter behavior is desired.
results.reproduction: Render `<Address address="0xabcdef" length={-1} />` → "0…xabcdef" (longer than input); `<Address address="0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678" length={0} />` → "0x…".
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this component, and the default positive `length` path hides these edge cases from normal usage.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Parameterized test asserting that `length={0}`, `length={-1}`, and `length={2.5}` either render the full address or produce output no longer than the input and never shorter than the prefix+ellipsis+suffix structure.

results.title: Address component has no unit tests for its truncation logic
results.recommendation: Add a component test (e.g. apps/web/src/components/Address.test.tsx) covering: empty string, short string below threshold, 42-char address with default length producing "0x…5678" style output, custom `length`, and preservation of the full address in the `title` attribute.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no existing tests for this feature; this finding is precisely about that absence.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: `describe('Address')` block asserting exact rendered text for empty/short/42-char inputs, custom length, and `title` attribute presence on both branches.

results.title: Silent failure when reconnect attempts are exhausted without an error event
results.recommendation: Set an error in onclose when reconnectCountRef reaches reconnectAttempts (e.g., "connection lost, max reconnects reached"), and/or expose reconnectCount so consumers can render an exhausted-state message.
results.reproduction: Open the hook with an unreachable-but-cleanly-closing endpoint; after reconnectAttempts closes, state.error is undefined and the component shows a silent dash.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No hook or component tests exist; the exhausted-without-error path is untested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Hook test: with reconnectAttempts small and clean closes, assert state.error is set once attempts are exhausted; component test asserting the error UI renders.

results.title: formatPrice renders nonzero prices below 1e-8 as $0.00000000
results.recommendation: Use significant-digit formatting (e.g., toPrecision with a sensible digit count, or adaptive decimals) so small nonzero values never display as zero.
results.reproduction: formatPrice(1e-9) returns "$0.00000000".
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: formatPrice is module-private and untested (feature metadata tests: []).
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test: formatPrice(1e-9) must not return "$0.00000000" (assert it contains a nonzero digit).

results.title: Unvalidated envelope payload fields can throw: missing tokenAddress crashes the filter effect; null change24h/volume24h crash rendering
results.recommendation: Validate every field before use: `typeof payload.tokenAddress === "string"`, `typeof payload.change24h === "number"`, `typeof payload.volume24h === "number"`, treating null/undefined as absent; consider an error boundary as defense in depth.
results.reproduction: Server sends {"type":"price","data":{"tokenAddress":null,"price":1}} → TypeError in the filter effect; or sends change24h:null → render-time TypeError in formatPercent.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for the component (tests: []); malformed-frame paths are untested.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: RTL test feeding envelopes with missing tokenAddress and with null change24h/volume24h, asserting the component renders the fallback UI instead of throwing.

results.title: No tests for PriceTicker or its formatting helpers

results.title: useWebSocket stale-reconnect race on url change: old socket's onclose schedules a reconnect to the previous URL and clobbers wsRef, leaking the live socket
results.recommendation: Prevent stale closures from reconnecting: capture a per-effect-run `active`/generation flag that cleanup flips, check it in onclose/connect, clear reconnectTimerRef at the start of each effect run, and only let onclose schedule a reconnect if the closing socket is still wsRef.current.
results.reproduction: Mount with url A and wait for open; change the URL to B; ~3-6s later the hook opens a second socket to url A while wsRef points at it; unmounting closes the A socket and leaves the B socket open until GC.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for the hook or component; this race requires a mocked WebSocket plus controlled close-event ordering and fake timers, which no included test covers.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Vitest with fake timers and a mocked WebSocket: mount the hook with url A, change url to B, then fire the old socket's close event and advance timers; assert no new WebSocket is constructed for url A and that wsRef/state reflect only url B's socket.

results.title: Stale price from the previous token remains displayed after tokenAddress/chainId change
results.recommendation: Reset the payload state whenever the subscription identity changes, e.g. add `useEffect(() => setData(null), [tokenAddress, chainId, wsUrl])` (or key the state to the token), so the ticker shows the placeholder while reconnecting and never labels an old token's price as the new one.
results.reproduction: Render PriceTicker with token A, deliver an envelope for A so a price shows, then re-render with token B without delivering any B envelope: the UI keeps showing A's price and change24h.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Feature metadata reports tests: [] and no test file was included; no component test exercises prop-change behavior.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: RTL test: render with token A, deliver A's envelope, assert price shown; rerender with token B without delivering B's envelope; assert the placeholder "—" (not A's price) is displayed.

results.title: tokenAddress and theme are interpolated into the iframe src without validation or URL encoding
results.recommendation: Validate tokenAddress as an EVM address (all mapped chains are EVM; e.g., /^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/) and encode interpolated values with encodeURIComponent, or reject invalid input by rendering an error state instead of an iframe.

results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this component (tests array is empty), so URL construction with adversarial or malformed inputs is never exercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render with tokenAddress containing '?', '#', '&', and '/' characters and assert the iframe src is either rejected (error state) or properly encoded so no parameter injection occurs.

results.title: DexScreenerChart has no unit tests despite testing-library and vitest being configured

results.title: Unknown chainId silently falls back to an Ethereum-scoped embed, showing potentially wrong chart data

results.title: Uncaught localStorage exceptions can crash the component and break theme toggle

results.title: Search query sent to the API untrimmed while the emptiness guard uses trim()

results.title: Selected-token logo rendered without the host allowlist check applied to list items
results.recommendation: Apply isSafeImageUrl to selectedToken.logoURI before rendering (fall back to the placeholder/avatar or omit the img), matching the list-item behavior.

results.title: No tests cover fetch failure paths (search errors, default-list errors, address 404)
results.recommendation: Add tests: fetch rejecting for /tokens; non-ok statuses; a 404 for a valid pasted address asserting 'No tokens found' and spinner cleared; and a default-list failure followed by reopen asserting the list is fetched again (retry) and eventually rendered.

results.title: Out-of-order search responses can overwrite newer results (no abort or stale-response guard)
results.recommendation: Create an AbortController per search and abort the previous request when the query changes or the component unmounts (pass signal into fetchTokens/fetchTokenByAddress), and/or track a monotonically increasing request id and ignore responses that are not from the latest query. Also clear results when the query is cleared.

Equivalently: type 'WETH', and before the response arrives, clear the input — the stale WETH rows remain visible with an empty query.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test mock (lines 43-60) resolves fetch promises immediately and deterministically, so responses can never interleave; no test uses deferred promises or rejects a stale response.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock fetch with deferred promises per request URL; type query A, then query B; resolve B first, then A; assert results reflect B. Also: type a query, clear input before resolving, assert no rows are shown and no duplicate-key list entries appear.

results.title: liquidityDistribution heights are treated as raw percentages and silently clamped
results.recommendation: Either normalize inside the component (height = value / max * 100 with max>0 guard), or validate/throw on out-of-range values, and document the 0-100 contract on the prop (e.g., via JSDoc or a branded type).
results.reproduction: Pass liquidityDistribution={[1e18, 2e18, 1e18]}; all bars render at 100% height.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this component; the normalization contract is undocumented and unasserted.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render with a distribution containing values above 100 and assert bars are scaled relative to the maximum rather than all pinned at 100%.
results.minimumFixScope: Add normalization (divide by max) or a documented validation in RangeSelector.tsx.

results.title: Selection highlight overlay is misaligned with the actual slider track
results.recommendation: Compute the overlay geometry over the track width, e.g. left: calc(0.5rem + <pct> * (100% - 1rem)) and right: calc(0.5rem + (100 - <pct>) * (100% - 1rem)), or apply the same inset-x-2 to the overlay and keep percentages relative to the inset box.
results.reproduction: Set currentTick such that lowerTick snaps to minimum and upperTick to maximum; the highlight fills the container edge-to-edge while the thumbs stop ~8px inside each edge.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this component, and the geometry is only visible in rendered styles, which no included test asserts.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render with known props and assert the overlay's style.left/right match the input's inset offset at the minimum/maximum handle positions (e.g., overlay left edge equals the input track's left edge when lower === minimum).
results.minimumFixScope: Adjust the overlay's left/right style computation in RangeSelector.tsx to account for the input inset.

results.title: RangeSelector has no automated tests despite non-trivial tick clamping/snapping invariants
results.recommendation: Add apps/web/src/components/RangeSelector.test.tsx covering: window centering for negative currentTick, snapping of off-grid props, inverted props (lowerTick > upperTick) being re-ordered via clamps, lower handle capped at upper - spacing, upper handle floored at lower + spacing, and onChange payloads always on the tick grid with lower < upper.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files exist for this component or its helpers; the feature's tests list is empty.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render with currentTick=0, tickSpacing=60, lowerTick=upperTick=0; assert both handles render and onChange never produces lowerTick >= upperTick; repeat with lowerTick=100000, upperTick=-100000 and assert the emitted range is ordered and inside [minimum, maximum].
results.minimumFixScope: Add a component test file exercising the derivation and onChange invariants.

results.title: Declared variant "bordered" has no effect — misleading API contract
results.recommendation: Remove "bordered" from the variant union and keep only the `bordered` boolean (or, if distinct variants are intended, wire "bordered" into the border class computation and drop the redundant boolean). At minimum, document that variant only controls compact vs. default so consumers don't rely on a non-existent behavior.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Feature metadata lists tests: [] and no test files were included; nothing exercises the variant prop, so the dead variant value is not detected.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest + @testing-library/react test rendering <Card variant="bordered" /> and <Card variant="default" /> and asserting their rendered className strings are identical, plus a test asserting each declared variant maps to the intended classes — this forces the variant union and implementation to stay in sync.

results.title: No unit tests for the Card component family
results.recommendation: Add a vitest + @testing-library/react test file (e.g., apps/web/src/components/ui/Card.test.tsx) covering: base class emission ("card bg-base-200"), border class toggling via the `bordered` prop, variant class emission, custom className merging/appending, and HTML attribute passthrough via ...rest for Card, CardBody, CardTitle, and CardActions.
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this feature — the feature metadata lists tests: [] and none of the included files reference a Card test.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render <Card bordered={false} variant="compact" className="custom" data-testid="card" /> and assert the rendered div has class "card bg-base-200 card-compact custom" and the data-testid attribute is passed through.
results.minimumFixScope: New test file only; no production code changes required.

results.title: Active network button remains clickable and issues a redundant switchChain call
results.recommendation: Skip the switchChain call when chainId === chain.id, or render the active chain's entry as a disabled/non-interactive item (aria-current, disabled attribute).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this component, so the always-clickable active chain entry has not been asserted.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Test that clicking the chain whose id equals the current chainId does not invoke switchChain, or that the button is disabled.

results.title: No tests cover the WalletConnect component (wallet auth and network switching flow)
results.recommendation: Add a vitest + @testing-library/react test file for WalletConnect that mocks @reown/appkit and wagmi hooks and covers: disconnected state renders Connect Wallet and calls open(), connected state renders address/ENS and the network list, switch buttons call switchChain with the right chainId, and Disconnect calls disconnect().
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test file for this component was included and the feature metadata lists no tests; the component has no test coverage to build on.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: A vitest test mocking useAppKit/useAccount/useChains/useSwitchChain/useDisconnect that asserts the Connect Wallet button appears when isConnected is false and that clicking a network item invokes switchChain({ chainId }) when connected.

results.title: switchChain/disconnect failures are silently swallowed with no user feedback
results.recommendation: Consume the error/status returned by useSwitchChain and useDisconnect (e.g., via onError callbacks or the error state) and render an inline error message in the dropdown; also close the dropdown or show a pending state while switching. Disable or no-op the button for the currently active chain (chainId === chain.id).
results.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this component (feature metadata lists tests: [] and no test file was included), so the absence of error handling has never been exercised.
results.suggestedRegressionTest: Render WalletConnect with mocked wagmi hooks where switchChain rejects; assert an error message appears in the dropdown and that the active chain's button does not invoke switchChain.
